title: P0: web signup sets a password but web login has no email/password form; email registrants can never sign in
description: sign-up-form.tsx:70-72 calls supabase.auth.signUp({email,password}), so web users DO set a password. login-form.tsx renders only Google/Apple SSO, a Register with Email link and a Forgot password link. There is no signInWithPassword anywhere on web, so anyone who registers by email can never log back in. /forgot-password and /update-password routes exist and are meaningless without it. auth/password-input.tsx (86 lines) and auth/email-input.tsx exist with ZERO consumers, i.e. they were built for this and left unwired. This is also the sole cause of the red Playwright suite (8/10 failing since ~2026-05-15). Supersedes/duplicates jits-rvy, raised from P2 to P0. IN PROGRESS this session.
close_reason: Fixed in 46fb344. login-form.tsx now calls supabase.auth.signInWithPassword, wiring up auth/password-input.tsx which had existed with zero consumers. Sign In is the single Signal Red CTA, which demoted Register with Email to secondary chrome. Errors map so an unknown address and a wrong password read identically (no account enumeration). 8 unit tests. This also turned the Playwright suite green: 8 failed/2 passed to 12 passed/0 failed.

title: P1: no web caller adopted the Result query variants; a transient read redirects a real gym manager
description: manage-content.tsx:29 still uses lenient getGymDetail, so a transient gym_managers failure makes isGymManager false and redirects a real manager off their own page. Same class: gym-header-manage-link.tsx:21, gym-detail-content.tsx:24, gyms-content.tsx:9. The new contract is consumed only by two mobile files. IN PROGRESS this session.
close_reason: Fixed in 46fb344. All four web callers moved to the Result variants. manage-content.tsx no longer redirects on an unknown: the redirect runs only on ok && !isGymManager, so a transient gym_managers failure shows an error plate instead of throwing a real manager off their own page. gym-detail-content.tsx renders from partial when the session list is trustworthy so a live session is never hidden behind a capability failure. Web tokens.css still resolves --text-tertiary #6B7280 (3.49:1) and --text-on-accent #E8EDF2 on #E63946 (3.54:1, and 2.87:1 on hover, below the 3:1 non-text floor). description: Both platforms: the only writer of 'incoming' is the realtime INSERT handler, so a challenge arriving while the user is not on the Arena is permanently invisible. title: Accessibility token repair: fix the 6 failing contrast pairs and the invisible card edge (ships first, token-only)
description: The mobile app's most common text style fails WCAG AA in both themes, and cards are effectively invisible against the page. Verified by independent computation against the real token values in apps/mobile/lib/tokens.ts. Dark theme (plate #1A1D24 on page #0D0F14): ink-3 #6B7280 on plate is 3.49:1, ink-on-cta #E8EDF2 on CTA #E63946 is 3.54:1, cta as text on plate is 4.05:1, plate vs page separation is 1.14:1. Light theme (plate #DEE2E9 on page #F2F4F7): ink-3 on plate is 3.72:1, cta as text on plate is 3.21:1, plate vs page is 1.18:1. ink-3 is the color of the single most common text style in the app, used at 10px in 163 places, so this is the highest-leverage defect in the codebase. The light hairline is also specified weaker (alpha 0.14) than the dark one (0.25), so the theme that needs the stronger edge has the weaker one. The user approved shipping this FIRST, ahead of the nav and Arena work, precisely because it is a token-only change with zero call sites: every screen built afterwards then inherits correct colors instead of needing a re-sweep. CRITICAL: do NOT change the brand red. The design proposal's remedy of deepening the CTA to #D22736 measures 4.37:1 and still fails AA (the proposal's claim of 5.14:1 is wrong). Keep accentCta #E63946 and darken the button LABEL to the existing Void token #0D0F14, which measures 4.60:1 and passes. That keeps app.json's push accent untouched and therefore needs no native rebuild. Token edits must land in all three hand-mirrored files or they will drift: apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js, apps/mobile/lib/tokens.ts, and apps/web/app/design-system/tokens.css. OTA: yes, fully OTA shippable, no native rebuild.
design: Direction A (Instrument) as approved by the user. Fix execution, not identity. Label-darkening is preferred over brand-red deepening specifically because it keeps the change OTA-only.
acceptance_criteria: Every text-on-surface pair in both themes measures at least 4.5:1 for normal text, verified by a computed contrast check and not by eye. ink-on-cta passes AA with the brand red #E63946 unchanged. Plate vs page separation is visually distinguishable and the light hairline is at least as strong as the dark one. All three token files carry identical values. Typecheck and the full mobile and shared test suites stay green. No change to app.json and no native rebuild required.
notes:
SCOPE CORRECTION (recorded after the independent review of this diff).

The acceptance criterion "All three token files carry identical values" is NOT met by this issue and will not be, deliberately.

1. This issue was implemented MOBILE ONLY, two files: apps/mobile/lib/tokens.ts and apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js. That was an intentional scope cut, not an omission. A different Claude session owns apps/web and was actively working in that tree, so editing the web tokens here would have collided with concurrent work.

2. The web half is tracked separately as jits-ozvd (P1, bug), which carries the exact per-token deltas to apply, the text/fill call-site split, and the coordination warning about the other session.

3. The mirror count is FOUR files, not three. The third mirror named in the description above (apps/web/app/design-system/tokens.css) has a previously unknown twin: apps/web/public/design/tokens.css, a near-identical copy whose dark block is `:root` only (no `[data-theme="dark"]` selector) and which carries a trailing utility-resets section the other file does not have. Any future token change must land in all four, or read the count off jits-ozvd rather than off this issue.

Until jits-ozvd lands, mobile and web are knowingly diverged on 9 or more variables per theme.

title: P0: recording maxDuration 600s races the match clock, truncating the clip and uploading mid-match
description:
GAP 2. WHY THIS IS P0: it silently loses the end of every full-length match, which is the part people most want to watch.

THE DEFECT: `maxDuration` is 600s (`lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:277`), EXACTLY equal to the default `matches.duration_seconds` of 600. But recording starts AFTER the match starts: there is up to a 3s camera-ready backstop plus up to 8s of not-ready retries, and pauses extend wall-clock time further. So on any full-length match the OS cap fires BEFORE the match ends. That hits the "settled without an explicit stop" branch, which UPLOADS the truncated clip mid-match, and the later real stop() then no-ops. The final minutes are never captured and nothing tells the user.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- The recording cap can no longer expire before a match of the configured duration ends. Give the cap real headroom over `matches.duration_seconds` rather than matching it, and account for the start delay and for pause time.
- If the OS cap DOES fire (it is a backstop, it must still be handled), it must not be treated as a normal completion: the user is told the recording hit its limit, and the later real stop must not silently no-op into nothing.
- Derive the cap from the match's duration where that is knowable rather than hardcoding a second magic number that will drift from the backend default the same way this one did.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: A 10-minute match on device produces a single clip covering the whole match including the final minute, uploaded once, after the match ends. Forcing the OS cap produces a clear user-facing message and no silent truncation. A regression test asserts the cap is strictly greater than the match duration plus the worst-case start delay. Verified on physical hardware, not just in the simulator.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-18 on branch impl-video-p0, commit 37e52ec. Cap derived in apps/mobile/lib/video/recording-limits.ts from matches.duration_seconds plus a 600s pause allowance plus a start/stop budget computed from the recorder's own retry constants (14s), clamped to [900, 7200]. A 600s match now caps at 1214s instead of 600s. The backstop firing is classified (limit vs interrupted, from the elapsed recording wall-clock) and surfaced through UploadProgressBanner instead of passing as a plain success; a stop arriving after it logs instead of no-opping silently. The viewfinder also mounts from the READY step so the capture session is warm before start_match. STILL NEEDS PHYSICAL HARDWARE: the simulator has no camera, so the 10-minute end-to-end recording in the AC is unverified. Awaiting independent review; not closed.
REVIEW ROUND 2, commit 3b8e97f. Two lifecycle defects the hoist introduced or exposed, both fixed: (F2) the recorder now outlives the viewfinder, so the 3s camera-ready backstop fired against a null cameraRef when a match ended inside it, hitting 'Camera not ready' and, because the status chip is persistent, accusing the user of a camera failure through result, confirm and summary. The backstop now checks the ref and MatchRecorderCamera calls a new releaseCamera() on unmount. (F3) 'stopping' had NO exit: issuePendingStop gives up after 2s and the machine sat in stopping forever, which since the hoist also pinned a live viewfinder and a lit iOS mic indicator over the result and summary steps. Added STOP_WATCHDOG_MS (10s, derived from the re-issue budget plus 8s of finalize slack) that releases the camera and reports that the recording did not finish. Also closed the PRE-EXISTING dead end where recordAsync settling with no URI while not stopping returned with no transition at all, leaving the machine stranded in 'recording': the one path where the cap could fire and the user was told nothing.
N5 from the b5b7d8c review, no action needed, recorded so it is not re-reported as a defect. On a near-2 GiB clip whose native finalize takes longer than the 8s of slack in STOP_WATCHDOG_MS (10s total = the 2s stop re-issue budget + 8s), the watchdog can fire and flash 'The recording did not finish' before recordAsync settles and the chip self-corrects to 'Uploading...'. It self-heals, the clip is still uploaded (stoppingRef is deliberately left true so a late settle takes the normal stopped path), and it is vastly better than the infinite spinner with a pinned camera and lit mic indicator that it replaced. If it ever proves annoying on real hardware, scale the slack with the recorded duration rather than raising the flat 8s.
close_reason: Merged to development as b5b7d8c. Review rejected the first attempt: it routed the fix through component state, and refresh() at confirm-to-summary unmounted the recorder on EVERY match, so videoId, the chip and any failure were destroyed regardless of upload timing. The shipped fix keys the upload outcome on matchId in a module-scope store written with no mounted guard, so it survives a provider remount, a step transition, and an upload completing after the recorder is gone. Verified robust rather than layered: deleting the accompanying revalidating predicate leaves all five regression tests green, and all five are proven red against the pre-fix commit. maxDuration is now derived from the retry constants (1214s for a 600s match) with those constants moved beside it. NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE: the simulator has no camera.

title: Decouple MatchFlowWizard from the required sessionId (exitHref / exitLabel / allowTimekeeper)
description:
WAVE 1a. THIS SHIPS FIRST AND ALONE. Both Arena and the video hardening build on it.

WHY: `apps/mobile/components/match-flow/match-flow-wizard.tsx:17` takes `sessionId` as a REQUIRED prop, and the only thing it is used for is exit navigation. Four hardcoded redirects assume a session lobby:
- `steps/ready-step.tsx:62` and `:117`
- `steps/summary-step.tsx:168`
- `components/match-flow/wizard-status.tsx:48`
all of them `router.replace('/(app)/session/${sessionId}/lobby')`. The prop is threaded through `match-flow-wizard.tsx:17,59,111` and `match-step-renderer.tsx:28,50,87,163`.

An Arena match has no session, so as long as this prop is required there is no way to run one. The backend already permits a sessionless match: `chk_match_origin` is `CHECK (challenge_id IS NOT NULL OR session_id IS NOT NULL)` (jr_be migration 20260405000600_matches_session_support.sql:54-56) and `matches.session_id` is nullable. The blocker is purely the mobile client's prop contract.

This is EXACTLY the coupling web had before 5b90ff1, and web already solved it: it replaced `sessionId` with an `exitHref` / `exitLabel` pair plus an `allowTimekeeper` flag. Mobile does the same refactor. Read the web change first and mirror its shape so the two platforms do not diverge.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- `sessionId` is no longer a required prop of MatchFlowWizard. Callers pass `exitHref` (where Done / Back goes) and `exitLabel` (the button copy), plus `allowTimekeeper`.
- All four hardcoded `router.replace` sites use `exitHref`.
- `sessionId` is removed from the threading in match-step-renderer where it was only carrying exit intent. If a step genuinely needs the session id for data (not navigation), keep it, but as an optional prop, and say so in the PR.
- The existing session entry point (`/(app)/session/[id]/lobby`) passes `exitHref` for the session lobby and `exitLabel` "Back to Lobby", so session matches behave exactly as they do today.
- While in here: `wait` in `lib/match-flow/step-router.ts:20-39` is unreachable dead code. Note it, do not necessarily delete it in this change, file a follow-up if removal is not trivially safe.

DO NOT in this issue: add the Arena route, add video changes, or change any step's behavior. This is a navigation-contract refactor only, and it is deliberately small so it can land fast and unblock two parallel workstreams.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). JS only.
design:
Mirror web's 5b90ff1 prop shape exactly rather than inventing a mobile-specific one: `exitHref`, `exitLabel`, `allowTimekeeper`. Divergent prop names across platforms is how the two match flows drift apart, and the match flow is the single most correctness-sensitive screen in the product.

`allowTimekeeper` exists because a session match has a third party (the gym running the session) who can operate the clock, while a peer-to-peer Arena match does not. Carry the flag even if mobile does not branch on it yet, so the contract is stable when it does.
acceptance_criteria: MatchFlowWizard compiles and runs with no `sessionId` prop. A session match started from the session lobby completes end to end and Done returns to the session lobby with the label "Back to Lobby", identical to today. A wizard mounted with an arbitrary `exitHref` returns there instead. No `router.replace('/(app)/session/...')` string literal remains in the match-flow tree. Unit tests cover exit routing for both a session exit and a non-session exit. Mobile typecheck and test suite are green.
notes: TRAP FOR WHOEVER DOES ARENA (jits-54km): allowTimekeeper was deliberately NOT added to mobile in this change, because mobile has zero timekeeper branches (all nine 'timekeeper' hits in apps/mobile are comments; step-router collapses the variants, the step renderer has no branch, and the session lobby creates matches with no timekeeper_id). If it is ever added, it MUST default to TRUE, matching web's default at apps/web/app/(app)/session/[id]/match/[matchId]/match-flow-content.tsx:39. A false default would silently change session match semantics, since web uses allowTimekeeper to gate isTimekeeper, hasTimekeeper and timekeeperEnabled all at once.
close_reason: Merged to development as fd2ae38. Independently reviewed, two defects found and fixed (exit-guard bypass on the group-less route spelling, blank exitLabel rendering an unlabeled CTA), both proven closed by mutation. Session path verified byte-identical. Gate green on the merged result.

title: [epic] Match with video on prod: record, upload, watch (no analysis)
description:
WAVE 2b. Depends on the wizard decoupling (1a). Runs in parallel with Arena.

SCOPE, AND THE BOUNDARY MATTERS: this targets PROD and is record, upload, watch ONLY. NO AI analysis, no slicing, no Cloud Run, no edge functions, no analysis UI. The jits-kaf tree owns the analysis pipeline and is NOT in scope here. Where the two touch the same file, this epic is a prerequisite: analysis of a clip that was never captured or never uploaded is meaningless.

WHAT ALREADY WORKS: the happy path exists and has been verified on hardware once. expo-camera CameraView mounted on the live step (`steps/live-step.tsx:67`, `:135`), recording 720p MP4 H.264/AAC via `lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:125`. Upload is a single-shot `FileSystem.uploadAsync` BINARY_CONTENT POST straight to `storage/v1/object/match-videos/<match_id>/<uploader_athlete_id>/<ts>.mp4` (`lib/video/upload-recording.ts`), a path convention that matches the prod storage RLS exactly, followed by `upsertMatchVideo` writing the row with status 'ready'. Playback is `apps/mobile/app/(app)/video/[id].tsx` on expo-av, resolving via `getMatchVideoSignedUrl` (queries.ts:1829) which prefers `normalized_path` then `storage_path`. Mobile records MP4 so normalized_path is null and storage_path is signed, which is correct on prod.

WHAT IS BROKEN: eleven verified gaps, filed as children. Two are P0 because they lose footage or lose all user feedback: the upload UI unmounts the instant the upload starts, and the OS recording cap fires BEFORE a full-length match ends and uploads a truncated clip mid-match.

NOT A RISK, do not treat it as one: oversize. The 2 GiB client cap matches the prod bucket limit and is unreachable at 720p for 600s. It is filed as a correct-error-message issue, not a P0.

TEST BASELINE: existing coverage is `apps/mobile/__tests__/lib/video/upload-recording.test.ts` (9 cases), `use-video-recorder.test.ts` (13 cases), `step-router.test.ts`, `ready-step.test.tsx`, plus packages/shared `match-video.test.ts` and `athlete-videos.test.ts`. NOT covered: LiveStep, CameraOverlay, UploadProgressBanner, video/[id].tsx, PastMatchVideos, the normalized_path preference, and the whole record-upload-watch sequence. There is no mobile e2e harness at all.

DELIVERY: every child is OTA-safe (EAS Update). expo-camera, expo-av, expo-file-system and expo-video-thumbnails are all already installed. If a fix needs a package that is not, it becomes a native rebuild and comes back to the user first.
acceptance_criteria: On prod, on physical hardware: a full-length (10 minute) match records end to end without truncation, the user sees upload state from the moment the match ends through to success or failure on every subsequent wizard step, a failed upload can be retried manually and survives an app restart, backgrounding mid-record or mid-upload does not lose the clip, and the finished video is watchable directly from the match summary. Playback failures state their actual reason. Test coverage exists for the full sequence.

title: [epic] Mobile native build: nav surgery, Arena, video hardening, style refresh
description:
PROGRAM EPIC. Four mobile-only workstreams, sequenced. The web half of this work already shipped on `development` at 5b90ff1 (Gyms out of web primary nav, /arena and /arena/swipe un-hidden, /arena/match/[matchId] added, instant challenge handshake hook, Arena on brand tokens). MOBILE WAS NOT TOUCHED. Nothing in this epic re-specs web.

WHY: mobile is the priority surface (see the `native-first-then-web-rollout` memory) and it is currently missing the product's headline social loop. There is no Arena on mobile at all: no route, no lobby presence, no way to issue a challenge, just a disabled button on the athlete profile. At the same time the tab bar carries two gym tabs (one of them manager-gated) that crowd out Arena, and the match video path has eleven verified defects including two that lose footage outright.

BUILD ORDER (encoded as real dependency edges, not prose):
- WAVE 1a, ALONE AND FIRST: decouple MatchFlowWizard from its required `sessionId` prop. Everything else builds on it.
- WAVE 1b, parallel with 1a: navigation surgery (4-up tab bar, gym and session discovery onto Home, manager entry relocated onto /gyms/[id], manager ROUTES kept alive).
- WAVE 2a: Arena (depends on 1a and 1b).
- WAVE 2b: match-with-video hardening (depends on 1a).
- WAVE 3: style refresh, gated on the user approving a design direction first.

SETTLED DECISIONS, DO NOT REOPEN:
- Both mobile gym tabs come out. The bar becomes Home, Arena, Rankings, Profile.
- Gym and session entry moves to the Home dashboard.
- Arena on mobile gets full parity with web PLUS a swipe surface.
- Match-with-video targets PROD and is record, upload, watch ONLY. No AI analysis, no slicing, no Cloud Run, no edge functions. The jits-kaf tree covers analysis and is explicitly NOT in scope here.
- Delivery is local `expo run:ios --device` builds plus EAS Update OTA. No EAS cloud builds and no TestFlight release without the user's explicit go. See the delivery gate child issue.
- Style work needs an approved design direction before any style code is written.

SCOPE BOUNDARY vs jits-kaf: jits-kaf is the full video integration epic including the chunked AI analysis pipeline. This program owns only the client-side record/upload/watch reliability on mobile. Where the two touch the same file, this program's issues win on sequencing because they are prerequisites for anything analysis-related working at all.
design:
OTA vs NATIVE REBUILD LEDGER for this program. Every child issue carries its own one-line classification; this is the summary.

OTA-SAFE (the overwhelming majority): all navigation work (the tab bar and every app header are custom JS), the whole Arena feature, every video-path fix listed here, font swaps (fonts load at runtime via @expo-google-fonts with NO expo-font config plugin), icon swaps (lucide-react-native over already-linked react-native-svg), and every token or className change.

NEEDS A NATIVE REBUILD: the native splash (app.json:96-102), the app icon (app.json:7) and Android adaptive icon (app.json:44-47), the push accent color (app.json:120-124), `userInterfaceStyle`, `edgeToEdgeEnabled`, and any new native dependency at all.

RUNTIME VERSION TRAP: `runtimeVersion.policy` is "appVersion" (app.json:10), so an OTA update only reaches binaries at the same version, currently 0.2.0. Bumping `expo.version` as part of a JS-only release would ORPHAN the update: it would never reach the installed builds. Do not bump the version for an OTA release.
acceptance_criteria: All four workstream epics are closed, the mobile quality gate (typecheck plus the test suite plus expo export) is green, and the app has been exercised on physical hardware through: Home to gym to session, Arena to challenge to match to video, and back. No EAS cloud build or TestFlight submission has happened without an explicit user go.

- WAVE 3: style refresh, gated on the user approving a design direction first.

SETTLED DECISIONS, DO NOT REOPEN:
- Both mobile gym tabs come out. The bar becomes Home, Arena, Rankings, Profile.
- Gym and session entry moves to the Home dashboard.
- Arena on mobile gets full parity with web PLUS a swipe surface.
- Match-with-video targets PROD and is record, upload, watch ONLY. No AI analysis, no slicing, no Cloud Run, no edge functions. The jits-kaf tree covers analysis and is explicitly NOT in scope here.
- Delivery is local `expo run:ios --device` builds plus EAS Update OTA. No EAS cloud builds and no TestFlight release without the user's explicit go. See the delivery gate child issue.
- Style work needs an approved design direction before any style code is written.

SCOPE BOUNDARY vs jits-kaf: jits-kaf is the full video integration epic including the chunked AI analysis pipeline. This program owns only the client-side record/upload/watch reliability on mobile. Where the two touch the same file, this program's issues win on sequencing because they are prerequisites for anything analysis-related working at all.

title: Decouple MatchFlowWizard from the required sessionId (exitHref / exitLabel / allowTimekeeper)
description:
WAVE 1a. THIS SHIPS FIRST AND ALONE. Both Arena and the video hardening build on it.

WHY: `apps/mobile/components/match-flow/match-flow-wizard.tsx:17` takes `sessionId` as a REQUIRED prop, and the only thing it is used for is exit navigation. Four hardcoded redirects assume a session lobby:
- `steps/ready-step.tsx:62` and `:117`
- `steps/summary-step.tsx:168`
- `components/match-flow/wizard-status.tsx:48`
all of them `router.replace('/(app)/session/${sessionId}/lobby')`. The prop is threaded through `match-flow-wizard.tsx:17,59,111` and `match-step-renderer.tsx:28,50,87,163`.

An Arena match has no session, so as long as this prop is required there is no way to run one. The backend already permits a sessionless match: `chk_match_origin` is `CHECK (challenge_id IS NOT NULL OR session_id IS NOT NULL)` (jr_be migration 20260405000600_matches_session_support.sql:54-56) and `matches.session_id` is nullable. The blocker is purely the mobile client's prop contract.

This is EXACTLY the coupling web had before 5b90ff1, and web already solved it: it replaced `sessionId` with an `exitHref` / `exitLabel` pair plus an `allowTimekeeper` flag. Mobile does the same refactor. Read the web change first and mirror its shape so the two platforms do not diverge.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- `sessionId` is no longer a required prop of MatchFlowWizard. Callers pass `exitHref` (where Done / Back goes) and `exitLabel` (the button copy), plus `allowTimekeeper`.
- All four hardcoded `router.replace` sites use `exitHref`.
- `sessionId` is removed from the threading in match-step-renderer where it was only carrying exit intent. If a step genuinely needs the session id for data (not navigation), keep it, but as an optional prop, and say so in the PR.
- The existing session entry point (`/(app)/session/[id]/lobby`) passes `exitHref` for the session lobby and `exitLabel` "Back to Lobby", so session matches behave exactly as they do today.
- While in here: `wait` in `lib/match-flow/step-router.ts:20-39` is unreachable dead code. Note it, do not necessarily delete it in this change, file a follow-up if removal is not trivially safe.

DO NOT in this issue: add the Arena route, add video changes, or change any step's behavior. This is a navigation-contract refactor only, and it is deliberately small so it can land fast and unblock two parallel workstreams.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). JS only.

title: [epic] Match with video on prod: record, upload, watch (no analysis)
description:
WAVE 2b. Depends on the wizard decoupling (1a). Runs in parallel with Arena.

SCOPE, AND THE BOUNDARY MATTERS: this targets PROD and is record, upload, watch ONLY. NO AI analysis, no slicing, no Cloud Run, no edge functions, no analysis UI. The jits-kaf tree owns the analysis pipeline and is NOT in scope here. Where the two touch the same file, this epic is a prerequisite: analysis of a clip that was never captured or never uploaded is meaningless.

WHAT ALREADY WORKS: the happy path exists and has been verified on hardware once. expo-camera CameraView mounted on the live step (`steps/live-step.tsx:67`, `:135`), recording 720p MP4 H.264/AAC via `lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:125`. Upload is a single-shot `FileSystem.uploadAsync` BINARY_CONTENT POST straight to `storage/v1/object/match-videos/<match_id>/<uploader_athlete_id>/<ts>.mp4` (`lib/video/upload-recording.ts`), a path convention that matches the prod storage RLS exactly, followed by `upsertMatchVideo` writing the row with status 'ready'. Playback is `apps/mobile/app/(app)/video/[id].tsx` on expo-av, resolving via `getMatchVideoSignedUrl` (queries.ts:1829) which prefers `normalized_path` then `storage_path`. Mobile records MP4 so normalized_path is null and storage_path is signed, which is correct on prod.

WHAT IS BROKEN: eleven verified gaps, filed as children. Two are P0 because they lose footage or lose all user feedback: the upload UI unmounts the instant the upload starts, and the OS recording cap fires BEFORE a full-length match ends and uploads a truncated clip mid-match.

NOT A RISK, do not treat it as one: oversize. The 2 GiB client cap matches the prod bucket limit and is unreachable at 720p for 600s. It is filed as a correct-error-message issue, not a P0.

TEST BASELINE: existing coverage is `apps/mobile/__tests__/lib/video/upload-recording.test.ts` (9 cases), `use-video-recorder.test.ts` (13 cases), `step-router.test.ts`, `ready-step.test.tsx`, plus packages/shared `match-video.test.ts` and `athlete-videos.test.ts`. NOT covered: LiveStep, CameraOverlay, UploadProgressBanner, video/[id].tsx, PastMatchVideos, the normalized_path preference, and the whole record-upload-watch sequence. There is no mobile e2e harness at all.

DELIVERY: every child is OTA-safe (EAS Update). expo-camera, expo-av, expo-file-system and expo-video-thumbnails are all already installed. If a fix needs a package that is not, it becomes a native rebuild and comes back to the user first.

title: [bug] Web recording is dead on Safari/iOS and reports 'Camera access denied'
description:
PROBLEM: apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts picks a mimeType from a WebM-only preference list (:171-172: vp9 -> vp8 -> video/webm) with a '?? "video/webm"' fallback. Safari's MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported returns false for EVERY WebM type, so .find() returns undefined and the unsupported fallback string is handed to 'new MediaRecorder(stream, { mimeType })' at :173, which throws NotSupportedError.

That constructor sits INSIDE the same try whose catch at :195-196 sets 'Camera access denied. You can still manage the match without video.' So on Safari/iOS the recorder never starts AND the user is told it is a camera-permission problem. Anyone debugging this will chase permissions indefinitely.

Impact: no web user on Safari (all iOS browsers, plus macOS Safari) can record a match at all. Silent for us, misleading for them.

FIX:
1. Probe 'video/mp4' FIRST (Safari supports MediaRecorder video/mp4; modern Chromium does too), then fall back to the WebM list.
2. Never construct MediaRecorder with a type that isTypeSupported rejected - if nothing is supported, fail with an explicit 'This browser cannot record video' message.
3. Split the try/catch: getUserMedia failure => permission/device message; MediaRecorder construction failure => codec message. They are different faults and must not share copy.
4. Derive the stored file extension and blob type from the ACTUAL recorder.mimeType rather than the hardcoded 'webm' at :84 and :151.

Item 4 overlaps jits-kaf.1.2 (the WebM-vs-MP4 container decision); items 1-3 are worth shipping regardless of which container option is chosen.

DISCOVERED BY: adversarial audit of the video upload path, 2026-09-10. Verified by code reading (Safari not directly tested from this machine).

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-11 (jits_web, uncommitted; pending independent review).

apps/web/lib/video/recorder-codec.ts (NEW, pure + unit-tested):
- MIME_PREFERENCE now leads with MP4/H.264 ('video/mp4;codecs="avc1.42E01E"' -> avc1 -> video/mp4) before the WebM list. Fixes Safari, and per jits-kaf.1.2 option A an H.264 source is also the only container that survives the slicer's '-c copy' fast path untouched.
- pickMimeType() returns string|null and NEVER returns a type isTypeSupported rejected; also returns null when MediaRecorder is undefined (SSR/old browser).
- extensionFor(mimeType) derives the storage extension from the recorder's ACTUAL mimeType rather than the hardcoded 'webm'.

apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts:
- startRecording() split into two try blocks: a getUserMedia failure keeps the 'Camera access denied' copy; a codec failure now says "This browser can't record video" / "Couldn't start the recorder on this browser" and logs the real error. The two faults no longer share copy.
- When pickMimeType() returns null the stream is released and we bail with an honest message instead of constructing MediaRecorder with an unsupported type.
- Upload path uses recorder.mimeType (authoritative; the browser may hand back a different type than requested) for BOTH the storage contentType and the extension.
- Added upsert:true so a retry against the same path replaces rather than 409s (partial jits-od3).
- stopRecording() now stops the camera tracks inside onstop, AFTER the final dataavailable has flushed. Previously they were stopped synchronously alongside recorder.stop(), which can truncate the last chunk.
- 'catch { fail("Upload failed") }' now preserves and logs the underlying error; we were blind in the field.

apps/web/lib/video/recorder-codec.test.ts: 11 tests covering the Safari-only-MP4 case, Chromium preference order, WebM fallback, the null cases, and extension mapping.

Gate: typecheck clean all 3 workspaces; 257 tests pass (web 45->56); eslint clean on touched files.

NOT covered here: option B (slicer-side webm->H.264 normalize in jr_be) is still required for browsers that can only emit WebM. Tracked on jits-kaf.1.2.

title: video-webhook auto-triggers legacy whole-video analyzer and wins the race, killing the chunked path
acceptance_criteria: A video that reaches status='ready' is sliced by the chunked pipeline (status walks ready -> slicing -> analyzing -> merging -> analyzed) and the legacy whole-video video-analyze function is NOT invoked. The slicer no longer logs 'slice skipped: status not ready' for a freshly-ready video. If the legacy path is kept behind a flag, the flag defaults to OFF and there is a test asserting the default.

title: Slicer aborts every chunk analysis at 30s: ANALYZE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS far below analyzer budget
description:
All code cited lives in the jr_be repo (~/code/EloRated/jr_be) unless noted.

The Cloud Run slicer aborts every chunk-analysis POST at 30 seconds, which is far shorter than the analyzer's own budget, so no chunk analysis can ever complete through the normal fan-out path.

Evidence:
- `workers/video-slicer/src/main.js:114` sets the fan-out timeout default:
  `const ANALYZE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = Number(process.env.ANALYZE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS ?? 30_000);`
  The comment above it (main.js:112-113) claims "The Edge Function has its own internal timeouts; this is just to keep one slow chunk from pinning the worker". That assumption is wrong, see below.
- `workers/video-slicer/src/main.js:711` uses that value as a hard AbortController deadline on the POST:
  `const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), ANALYZE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS);` inside `postAnalyze(url, chunkId)` (declared at main.js:709).
- `video-analyze-chunk` is fully synchronous. It does the Gemini work inside the request and only responds when analysis is done. Its own budgets are `GEMINI_TIMEOUT_MS_STANDARD = 60_000` and `GEMINI_TIMEOUT_MS_PREMIUM = 300_000` at `supabase/functions/video-analyze-chunk/index.ts:137-138`, plus up to roughly 150s of Gemini File API upload/poll before the model call even starts (`supabase/functions/video-analyze-chunk/index.ts:149-150`).

So worst case the analyzer legitimately needs about 150s + 300s = 450s for premium and about 150s + 60s = 210s for standard, while the slicer gives it 30s. The slicer aborts the connection on essentially every chunk.

Interaction with jits-ayj (do not duplicate that bug, it is a different defect): an AbortController abort DOES reject the fetch promise, so unlike the HTTP-status bug in jits-ayj these aborts land in the `failed` bucket of `fanOutAnalyze()`. With all chunks failing, the worker returns 500 and pg_net does not retry, so the video is stranded. Fixing jits-ayj alone will not fix this; fixing this alone will not fix jits-ayj.

Fix shape (either is acceptable):
1. Raise the `ANALYZE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` default to >= 420000 (7 minutes) so it exceeds the premium-tier worst case, and set the matching env var on the deployed Cloud Run service; or
2. Make the fan-out fire-and-forget (dispatch the POST without awaiting the analysis body) and rely on the chunk state machine plus the reaper/retry sweep for completion tracking. Note this changes what the worker can report about success/failure, so coordinate with jits-ayj's success/failure accounting fix.

Also update the stale comment at `workers/video-slicer/src/main.js:112-113`, which asserts the Edge Function's internal timeouts make this a mere safety net.
acceptance_criteria: A standard-tier chunk analysis completes without the slicer aborting the connection: postAnalyze() holds the connection long enough for video-analyze-chunk to return its result, the chunk lands in status 'completed', and the worker reports it as a success. Verified end-to-end against a real (non-trivial) chunk, not a stub. Premium-tier worst case (~450s) is also covered by whatever deadline is chosen, or the fan-out is fire-and-forget so no client-side deadline applies. The stale comment at workers/video-slicer/src/main.js:112-113 is corrected.

comments.text: STALE as filed (verified 2026-09-10): the 30s timeout is already fixed in code - workers/video-slicer/src/main.js:118 now reads '?? 480_000' and the comment at :108-117 is corrected (commit 00614ad). What remains is ONLY verifying/setting ANALYZE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS in the DEPLOYED Cloud Run env. Re-scope to that, or close and fold the env-var check into jits-kaf.1.1.

comments.text:

title: Persistent upload status indicator across match wizard steps (signals + retry)
description:
Requested by product owner during the 2026-06-10 on-device test, where it was impossible to tell from the phone whether the match recording uploaded. Today UploadProgressBanner lives only inside the live step; the moment the wizard advances to result/confirm/summary, all upload visibility vanishes, and a failed/stuck upload is invisible (also makes field debugging blind).

Spec: lift recorder/upload state out of live-step (wizard-level context or a small upload-manager module in apps/mobile/lib/video/) and render a compact persistent status chip on the result, confirm, and summary steps: recording / uploading / saved (with checkmark) / failed (with Retry CTA that re-runs uploadRecording against the SAME storage path). No percentage bar: FileSystem.uploadAsync emits no progress events for BINARY_CONTENT; state-based signals only (note resumable TUS upload as the future path to real progress). Animation must follow brand motion rules (reactive status spinner like the existing banner; no decorative motion). Also surfaces the diagnostic [video] log tags in dev. Mirrors web later (web has the same gap after match-recorded-step unmounts).
acceptance_criteria: After ending a match, every wizard step until summary shows the upload state; a failed upload shows Retry and retrying reuses the same storage path; success shows confirmation; covered by component tests for all four states.
notes:
ADOPTED 2026-09-18 into the mobile native build program (epic jits-tj5n, video epic jits-5tj9) as GAP 1, the worst defect in the record-upload-watch path. Bumped P1 -> P0 and reparented under the video epic.

WHY IT IS P0: the upload UI unmounts the moment the upload starts. UploadProgressBanner lives INSIDE LiveStep (live-step.tsx:155). Ending the match stops the recorder and calls onEnded in the same tick, LiveStep unmounts, and the upload begins AFTER that. So the user never sees uploading, never sees success, and never sees failure. Every other video fix in this epic is invisible to the user until this one lands: retry has nowhere to render its CTA, progress has nowhere to render its percentage, and a failed upload stays silent.

ALSO DEAD STATE: recorder.videoId (use-video-recorder.ts:439) has ZERO consumers. It is set and never read. Either wire it into the persistent state this issue introduces, or delete it; do not leave it.

DEPENDENCIES ADDED: blocked by the MatchFlowWizard sessionId decoupling (jits-3929), because both refactor the wizard's cross-step contract and doing them independently guarantees a conflict. This issue in turn blocks real upload progress (jits-l5eq), manual retry and persistence (jits-341p), and the sequence test coverage (jits-1yp1).

NOTE ON PROGRESS: the original spec correctly said no percentage bar, because FileSystem.uploadAsync with BINARY_CONTENT emits no progress events. That constraint is now addressed separately in jits-l5eq by moving to FileSystem.createUploadTask, which does expose progress. Build the state-based signals here; the percentage lands on top of them there.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). JS only.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-18 on branch impl-video-p0, commit 37e52ec (worktree .claude/worktrees/impl-video-p0). Recorder hoisted into MatchRecorderProvider (components/match-flow/match-recorder-context.tsx) above the step boundary; the status chip and the viewfinder are rendered by the wizard via match-recorder-surface.tsx. recorder.videoId now feeds a Watch Match Video action on the summary step, so jits-p75q's first half is covered here too. NOT DONE, deliberately out of scope per the implementation brief: the Retry CTA and the persisted file URI, which stay with jits-341p. The hoisted state is shaped so a retry action can be added without moving it again. Awaiting independent review; not closed.
REVIEW ROUND 2, commit 3b8e97f on impl-video-p0 (merged development e6ec219 first). Review of 37e52ec found the hoist alone was NOT enough: the wizard remounts on EVERY match, because the confirm step calls refresh() when the row goes terminal and useMatchDetails re-enters loading above the provider. That destroyed videoId, the success chip and the failure message deterministically, not as a race. Mobile was therefore strictly worse than apps/web, which loses its videoId only in a race window. FIX: match-scoped upload store at apps/mobile/lib/video/match-upload-store.ts, keyed on matchId, read via useSyncExternalStore; the recorder writes the outcome there unguarded by mountedRef. Closes the remount AND the late-completing-upload case that still defeats web. apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-banner-state.ts holds the precedence between the view-bound recorder and the durable store as one pure tested table. The wizard also no longer re-enters its loading branch for a revalidation of a match it already holds. The web session has offered to mirror this store; nothing was put in packages/shared. Retry is still jits-341p and the hook still needs lastFileUriRef plus a retry() for it (see correction on that issue). Awaiting re-review; not closed.
close_reason: Merged to development as b5b7d8c. Review rejected the first attempt: it routed the fix through component state, and refresh() at confirm-to-summary unmounted the recorder on EVERY match, so videoId, the chip and any failure were destroyed regardless of upload timing. The shipped fix keys the upload outcome on matchId in a module-scope store written with no mounted guard, so it survives a provider remount, a step transition, and an upload completing after the recorder is gone. Verified robust rather than layered: deleting the accompanying revalidating predicate leaves all five regression tests green, and all five are proven red against the pre-fix commit. maxDuration is now derived from the retry constants (1214s for a 600s match) with those constants moved beside it. NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE: the simulator has no camera.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text:
WEB HALF: the mobile design has landed and web should mirror it rather than invent a second one. Recording the shape here so it is not lost in a session transcript. Source: jr-be-73 session, 2026-09-19, mirrored back after I sent them the web comparison.

WEB'S CURRENT STATE IS DIFFERENT FROM MOBILE'S, and milder, but broken in the same way at the end.
- videoId is already WIZARD-level, not step-level: match-flow-wizard.tsx:38 holds it, the recorder lives in steps/timekeeper-live-step.tsx:36, and the id is lifted via handleNext (wizard:44) into match-summary (:73) and match-recorded (:75). So a step unmount does NOT destroy it.
- BUT the lift only happens ON ADVANCE. apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts deliberately lets the storage upload and the match_videos write finish after unmount, guarding only React state writes behind mountedRef, so setVideoId is skipped once the step is gone. If the athlete advances before the upload completes, the row IS written and the id NEVER reaches the wizard: summary and recorded render with no video although the video exists in storage.
- Severity note: web's window is bounded by upload duration vs tap speed, so it looks intermittent in testing and is near-certain on a slow gym connection with a short match. Mobile's was unconditional (use-match-completion refetches on completed OR disputed plus a 1s timer when the row is already terminal at mount), so EVERY mobile match hit it. Mobile really was strictly worse; that is now confirmed rather than assumed.

MOBILE DESIGN TO MIRROR (apps/mobile/lib/video/):
1. match-upload-store.ts, ~160 lines, no deps beyond React. Module-scope Map<matchId, entry> + listener Set. Entry { matchId, status: pending|uploading|uploaded|error, videoId, error, truncation, storagePath, updatedAt }. setMatchUpload(matchId, patch) merges and ALWAYS replaces the entry object so a useSyncExternalStore snapshot compares unequal exactly when something changed. Reads via getMatchUpload(matchId) and useMatchUpload(matchId) over useSyncExternalStore, which reads correctly on FIRST RENDER even when the write happened before the component existed. In-memory, dies with the JS context (persistence is a separate issue). Entries NOT cleared on success or failure, because a visible failure is correct. Bounded MAX_TRACKED_MATCHES = 8, oldest-by-updatedAt eviction. storagePath recorded so a retry reuses the same key; the temp file URI deliberately not held.
2. upload-banner-state.ts, a PURE deriveUploadBannerState(recorderState, recorderError, upload) with its own test. Precedence: recorder-stopping first, then the STORE's outcome, then recorder-only failures (no camera, no permission, stop watchdog), then hidden. Their note: trusting the recorder over the store in that middle slot is what made the failure silent, so it is one table with one test rather than conditions scattered through a component.

THE CRITICAL LINE FOR WEB: the store write must be UNGUARDED BY ANY MOUNTED CHECK. That single property is what fixes web's bug, because web's upload already completes; it is the React state write that is skipped.

AND DELETE, DO NOT ADD: mobile removed setVideoId, setTruncation and their mountedRef guards entirely and derives both from the store. The web equivalent is removing the wizard-level videoId useState (match-flow-wizard.tsx:38) and the handleNext lift (:44) rather than keeping them alongside a store. Two sources of truth with a precedence rule between them is how this bug survives a refactor.

SCOPE WARNING: the mobile store lives in apps/mobile/lib/video/ and deliberately NOT in packages/shared, to avoid colliding with concurrent queries.ts work. A web version should sit in apps/web/lib/video/ for the same reason unless someone deliberately unifies them later.

NOT STARTED ON WEB. Waiting on the user; other work is queued ahead of it.

title: Deploy + wire the video analysis pipeline: slicer Cloud Run, video_slicer_url GUC, bucket in migration
description:
The pipeline exists in code but is almost certainly not running: the slicer dispatch silently NO-OPs when the app.settings.video_slicer_url GUC is unset, and the Cloud Run worker (jr_be/workers/video-slicer, 1051-line ffmpeg slicer) is likely not deployed. Also, the match-videos bucket exists only in supabase/config.toml, not in a migration, so a prod db push would not create it (prod-push risk).

Work (repo: jr_be):
1. Deploy workers/video-slicer to Cloud Run (follow the worker's own README/specs under jr_be/specs/013-chunked-video-pipeline if present); capture the service URL and auth.
2. Set the app.settings.video_slicer_url GUC (and any companion auth GUC) in each target environment; document where it is set (migration vs dashboard vs infra script) so it is not lost on db reset.
3. Move match-videos bucket creation (+ its storage policies) into a migration so prod push creates it; keep config.toml in sync for local dev.
4. Verify the Gemini analyze-chunk + merge edge functions are deployed and the pg_cron sweeps are scheduled.
5. End-to-end verification: insert/upload a real video, watch status walk ready→slicing→analyzing→merging→analyzed, and confirm get_video_analysis returns a payload (web timekeeper viewer or use-video-progress hook can be the probe).
6. Run npm run db:types in jits_web if any migration changed schema.
acceptance_criteria: A freshly-uploaded real video reaches status='analyzed' in a deployed environment with no manual poking. Bucket + policies are migration-managed (supabase db reset locally still creates them). GUC wiring documented. pgTAP suite green.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: Local portion done in jr_be (uncommitted, working tree): migration supabase/migrations/20260610000000_match_videos_bucket.sql + test supabase/tests/043_match_videos_bucket_test.sql (19 pgTAP tests). Reused auth_athlete_id(); is_match_video_participant()/is_video_visible() NOT usable here (they key on match_videos.id which does not exist yet at upload time and is not in the path; is_video_visible also has EXECUTE revoked from authenticated). Verified signed-URL creation IS gated by the SELECT policy on storage-api v1.37.7 via live local API probe (13/13 checks: upsert re-upload 200, cross-folder upload 400, participant sign 200, outsider sign 400, non-owner delete 400, owner delete 200). comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: LOCAL E2E VERIFICATION: PASS (2026-06-10). Proven on local stack: authenticated upload (storage RLS as real user JWT, x-upsert), match_videos INSERT RLS, AFTER INSERT trigger, pg_net delivery to host.docker.internal:8791, HMAC shared-secret auth (pos+neg), claim RPC, signed-URL download, ffmpeg copy-path slice, chunk upload, persist RPC atomic status flip (ready->slicing->analyzing, 289ms for 15s clip), idempotent replay, 4 cron sweeps registered.
