title: No Facebook App ID plumbing exists for the Reels handoff
description:
shareToReels() takes appId as a REQUIRED argument and nothing in the codebase
supplies it. Found by the adversarial review of 0f6ac9f, which grepped and
confirmed: no env var, no constant, no config entry for a Facebook App ID
exists anywhere in apps/mobile or packages/shared.

This is not filed on any existing slice. jits-s6mi.8 covers registering the
Meta app and obtaining the ID; this covers getting that value into the running
app.

## Why it matters more than it looks

Meta requires the App ID for the Reels handoff (and for Stories, since
January 2023). Without it the share fails with a user-facing "The app you
shared from doesn't currently support sharing to Stories"-class error, and
the failure is SILENT from our side: we cannot detect client-side that the
ID was rejected.

The device test (jits-s6mi.6) is the first place a real, possibly-undefined
App ID flows through the module. Note the related one-line fix already in
the current fix round: two guards in index.ts sit OUTSIDE the try block, so
an undefined appId throws a TypeError rather than returning the module's
normal result object. The App ID arriving as string | undefined from config
is exactly the live shape that would hit it.

## Scope

- Decide where it lives. EXPO_PUBLIC_* follows the existing env convention
  (see apps/mobile/lib/env.ts, which reads Constants.expoConfig.extra first
  and falls back to process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_*). It is not a secret: the App
  ID is public by design and ships in the binary either way.
- Add it to .env.example so it is discoverable.
- Surface a clear, early error when it is absent, rather than letting an
  empty string reach the pasteboard and fail opaquely at Instagram.
- Note the bundle ID / package name must ALSO be registered against that App
  ID in the Meta dashboard, or sharing fails with the same undetectable
  error. That half belongs to jits-s6mi.8.

Blocks jits-s6mi.6 (on-device test).
notes:
RECOMMENDED MECHANISM (from the Reels module implementer, 2026-09-25):

  EXPO_PUBLIC_FACEBOOK_APP_ID
    -> apps/mobile/app.config.js writes it into extra.FACEBOOK_APP_ID
    -> apps/mobile/lib/env.ts reads it

That is the exact hardening path already used for SUPABASE_URL,
SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and SENTRY_DSN. The docblock in app.config.js explains
why it exists: relying on Metro's EXPO_PUBLIC_* inlining for release
bundles previously shipped two launch-crashing TestFlight builds.

A Facebook App ID is not a secret (it ships in the binary either way), so
EXPO_PUBLIC_* plus an EAS environment entry is the right class of config.

## THE TRAP

Do NOT add it to app.config.js's REQUIRED_ENV array. That list THROWS and
fails the EAS build when a value is missing. The App ID does not exist yet
(blocked on the Meta registration issue), so adding it there would break
every build until registration completes.

Its absence must stay soft and surface at share time as the existing
`missing-app-id` failure, which already has user-facing copy.

## SEQUENCING

Blocked by: the Meta registration issue (obtaining the ID).
Needed by: the share-entry-point issue (first caller).

File as its own small slice rather than folding it into the entry-point
issue, because that one must not ship by accident and this is config-only
work that can land safely ahead of it.

title: Meta prerequisites: register a Facebook App ID, take it to Live mode, register the iOS bundle ID and Android package
description:
EXTERNAL PREREQUISITE WITH A LEAD TIME. Nothing in the Reels handoff works without it, and it is
not code, so it can and should start in parallel with Slice B rather than after it.

## WHAT IS REQUIRED

A registered Facebook App ID, in LIVE MODE, with the platform settings filled in. Required for
Sharing to Reels since January 2023.

Live mode requires, per Meta: display name, contact email, PRIVACY POLICY URL, TERMS OF SERVICE
URL, a 1024x1024 icon, app category, app purpose, and the iOS BUNDLE ID and Android PACKAGE
registered under platform settings.

WHAT IT DOES NOT REQUIRE: App Review. Business Verification. Neither applies to a share-only
integration with zero permissions. This is the entire reason the composer handoff was chosen over
the Graph API, where App Review runs 2-8 weeks by practitioner report and Business Verification has
no published turnaround at all.

CHOOSE THE "OTHER" APP TYPE for a share-only app with zero permissions. NOTE: use cases CANNOT BE
REMOVED after app creation, so pick correctly the first time.

## THE CRITICAL-PATH ITEM

The PRIVACY POLICY URL and TERMS URL must be PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE. Today they are not: TERMS.md and
PRIVACY_POLICY.md are repo files served nowhere, and they contain FOUR TBD PLACEHOLDERS
(TERMS.md:64 governing jurisdiction and venue, TERMS.md:68 legal contact email and address,
PRIVACY_POLICY.md:52 rights-request email, PRIVACY_POLICY.md:72 legal contact email and address).
That is tracked as its own issue and blocks this one.

## REGISTER A REAL ONE EVEN IF IT SEEMS OPTIONAL

Whether the Facebook App ID is validated against Meta's registry for the sharing handoff is
GENUINELY UNRESOLVED in both directions, and was investigated. Register a real one regardless: it
is free, it is unreviewed, and the failure mode of a fake or absent ID is a SILENT production break
that cannot be detected client-side.

## UNVERIFIED, WORTH WATCHING

Whether an "Other" type app in Live mode with zero permissions triggers Meta's annual Data Use
Checkup. Meta's own page contradicts itself on this. If it does, it is a recurring compliance task
that needs an owner, not a one-off.

## DELIVERABLE

The App ID, and whatever config surface the client reads it from, wired so that Slice B1 can send
it in the iOS pasteboard payload and the Android intent extra.
acceptance_criteria: A real Facebook App ID exists in LIVE mode under the Other app type, with display name, contact email, public privacy policy URL, public terms URL, 1024x1024 icon, category and purpose filled in, and with the iOS bundle ID and Android package registered under platform settings. The App ID is available to the client for the iOS pasteboard payload and the Android intent extra. Whether the annual Data Use Checkup applies is checked and, if it does, an owner is named.

title: Publish TERMS and PRIVACY_POLICY at public URLs and resolve the four TBD placeholders
description:
TERMS.md and PRIVACY_POLICY.md are repo files served at no public URL, and they contain four TBD
placeholders. Both facts block the Facebook App ID going to Live mode, which blocks the Instagram
Reels handoff entirely.

## THE FOUR PLACEHOLDERS

  - TERMS.md:64  governing jurisdiction and venue
  - TERMS.md:68  legal contact email and physical address
  - PRIVACY_POLICY.md:52  the email address for exercising data rights
  - PRIVACY_POLICY.md:72  legal contact email and physical address

Three of the four are "a legal entity's contact details", which is one decision, not three. The
jurisdiction clause is a real legal choice and is the one that needs a lawyer.

## THE HOSTING GAP

Meta's Live mode requires a public privacy policy URL and a public terms URL. Apple already
requires the same for App Store distribution, so this is not Instagram-specific work; it is
overdue work that Instagram happens to surface. Serve both from the marketing/web surface at
stable URLs.

## A SEQUENCING NOTE

jr_be-17f (the consent decision) is likely to REVISE the terms, because TERMS.md:38 currently
grants a licence to host, display and transmit content "within the app, solely as needed to provide
the service", FROM THE UPLOADER ALONE, and publishing athlete B's likeness to a public Instagram
audience is not covered by that under any reading. So expect to publish these, then publish them
again after that decision lands. Publish anyway; the URLs need to exist and be stable, and holding
them hostage to an unresolved legal decision blocks the App ID for no benefit.

## ADJACENT, NOT IN SCOPE HERE

jits-g27 (render waivers.body instead of the hardcoded TOS_TEXT/WAIVER_TEXT constants) is the
related problem that legal copy lives in four places that disagree, and the only one a
non-developer can edit is the one that is never displayed. Fixing that would make future policy
edits cheap. It is not required to publish a URL today.
acceptance_criteria: Both documents are served at stable public URLs. All four TBD placeholders are filled: governing jurisdiction and venue, the legal contact email and physical address (both occurrences), and the data-rights request email. The URLs are recorded in the Meta prerequisites issue.

title: Mobile: manual highlight segment picker, render trigger, progress and preview (first caller of the render endpoint)
description:
The first CALLER of the render endpoint, and the reason the endpoint takes [start, end] segments as
input rather than doing its own selection. This ships BEFORE automatic selection, deliberately: it
lets clip quality be evaluated before clip selection is trusted.

## SCOPE

  - On an athlete's own match video, a way to scrub and mark one or more [start, end] segments.
  - Shared-layer mutation to create the video_highlights row with those segments.
  - Progress UI driven by jr_be-15c.6's get_highlight_progress RPC and the realtime status flips.
    Expect roughly 40-70 seconds of wall time plus a possible cold start for something that feels
    to the user like a button press, so this needs a real progress state, not a spinner with no
    end.
  - Preview playback of the finished 9:16 clip.
  - A re-render affordance. NOTE the backend bounds re-renders with a never-reset counter
    (render_total), so the UI must handle "you have hit the re-render ceiling" as a real state
    rather than a generic failure.
  - Terminal failure surfacing: the row carries a scrubbed error_message, and NULL means "no reason
    available", which must render as absence rather than as an error string. Same contract as
    match_videos.error_message in get_video_progress.

## WHAT THIS ISSUE DOES NOT INCLUDE

No share affordance of any kind. Not Reels, not the system share sheet, not save-to-camera-roll.
Preview is in-app playback to a participant, which is the same audience that can already watch the
source. The moment a file leaves the app, jr_be-17f applies and the separate flagged share issue
owns it.

## CONSTRAINTS TO SURFACE IN THE PICKER

Reels accepts 3 to 60 seconds. A clip under 3 seconds is rejected outright. Enforce the bounds in
the picker rather than letting the render succeed and the handoff silently no-op.
acceptance_criteria: An athlete can mark one or more [start, end] segments on their own match video, trigger a render, see real progress driven by get_highlight_progress plus realtime status flips, and preview the finished 9:16 clip in-app. The picker enforces the Reels 3-60 second bounds. Re-render is offered and the render_total ceiling renders as its own explicit state, not a generic failure. A scrubbed error_message is surfaced, and a NULL error_message renders as absence rather than as an error string. NO share affordance of any kind is added by this issue.

title: Slice B4: share entry point, behind highlight_share_enabled, which MUST stay false while jr_be-17f is open
description:
THE ISSUE THAT MUST NOT BE SHIPPED BY ACCIDENT. Read it before wiring any button.

This is the entry point that makes the share path reachable: the button, the sheet, the copy, the
destination picker. It is the ONLY place in either epic where the consent blocker jr_be-17f
actually bites.

## THE RULE

Every outbound share affordance is behind feature_flags key highlight_share_enabled:
  - the Reels handoff
  - the generic system share-sheet fallback
  - save-to-camera-roll

Seeded FALSE. FAIL-CLOSED: a missing flag row means off, following the video_upload_enabled
precedent in jr_be migration 20260918010000. A network failure reading the flag means off, not
"assume on because we already rendered".

THE FLAG MUST NOT BE FLIPPED TRUE WHILE jr_be-17f IS OPEN. jr_be-17f's acceptance criteria now name
this flag explicitly.

Flag-off behaviour is that the affordance is ABSENT, not disabled-looking. A greyed-out "Share to
Instagram" button is a product promise we have not decided we can keep, and it invites someone to
"just enable it for testing" against production data.

## WHAT THE COPY MUST NOT SAY, WHENEVER IT DOES SHIP

The consent flow CANNOT promise revocation. Consent to an Instagram post is irrevocable by
construction, and even the revocable half cannot currently be honoured: there is no delete UI on
either platform, no delete RPC, and status='deleted' is in the CHECK constraint but is never
written (jr_be-umc.4). So the copy can only promise removal from ELO RATED, and it has to say that
at grant time, prominently. Per-clip grant, not blanket. The exact wording is jr_be-17f's output,
not this issue's invention.

## WHY THE RENDER PATH IS NOT BEHIND THIS FLAG

A clip shown only to the two match participants reaches exactly the audience that can already watch
the full source video under participant-scoped RLS. The render path has its own separate kill
switch (highlight_clips_enabled) for operational reasons, not consent ones. Do not conflate the two
flags and do not collapse them into one.
acceptance_criteria: Every outbound share affordance (Reels handoff, system share sheet, save-to-camera-roll) is gated by feature_flags key highlight_share_enabled, seeded FALSE and fail-closed on both a missing row and a failed read. Flag-off renders the affordance ABSENT, not greyed out. The flag is documented in this issue and in jr_be-17f as not-to-be-enabled while that decision is open. A test proves that with the flag off, no code path can reach the native module, expo-sharing, or expo-media-library from the highlight surface.

title: Slice B3: Instagram availability detection, generic share-sheet fallback, and share-funnel instrumentation
description:
The Reels handoff must degrade, not fail, and the fallback must be gated exactly as tightly as the
primary path.

## AVAILABILITY DETECTION

Before offering the Reels action, check that Instagram is installed and can receive the intent
(canOpenURL on iOS, package visibility query on Android). This requires the config plugin
declarations to be in place; without them the check returns a confident false on a device where
Instagram is installed.

## FALLBACK

Fall back to the generic system share sheet via expo-sharing, which is ALREADY a dependency
(apps/mobile/package.json). No Meta involvement at all, but it cannot target a specific app, so
Instagram may be buried in the list. That is an acceptable v1 fallback and it is what the research
recommends keeping.

## THE GATE APPLIES TO THE FALLBACK TOO

The generic share sheet is an outbound share to an arbitrary destination. In consent terms it is
identical to the Reels path: it hands the other athlete's likeness outside the two-participant
scope. It sits behind the SAME highlight_share_enabled flag. Do not treat it as the "safe" option
that can ship early.

Same for save-to-camera-roll (expo-media-library is already a dependency). Saving athlete B's
likeness into athlete A's photo library is an outbound share. Same flag.

## INSTRUMENTATION

Instrument the funnel: action offered -> availability check result -> handoff invoked -> app
returned to foreground. The handoff itself gives no success signal (Instagram never tells us
whether the athlete posted), so foreground-return timing plus a lightweight post-return prompt is
the only observability available. Build it now; it is the only way to measure the iOS 16 pasteboard
prompt's drop-off later.
acceptance_criteria: Availability is checked before the Reels action is offered and falls back to the generic system share sheet (expo-sharing, already a dependency) when Instagram is absent or the handoff is unavailable. The fallback AND save-to-camera-roll sit behind the SAME highlight_share_enabled flag as the Reels path; neither ships as an unflagged convenience. The funnel is instrumented at four points: offered, availability result, handoff invoked, app returned to foreground. Verified on a device with Instagram uninstalled.

title: Slice B2: config plugin for LSApplicationQueriesSchemes (iOS) and Android queries package visibility
description:
Both halves of the Reels handoff are invisible to the app without platform declarations, and both
fail SILENTLY when missing, which is the expensive part.

iOS: instagram-reels (and instagram, for the fallback) must be listed in LSApplicationQueriesSchemes
in Info.plist, or canOpenURL returns false and the availability check reports Instagram as not
installed on a device where it is.

Android: the Instagram package must be declared in the <queries> element of AndroidManifest.xml, or
package visibility filtering (Android 11+) hides it from queryIntentActivities and resolveActivity,
with the same consequence.

Both are expressed through an Expo CONFIG PLUGIN, following the existing local-plugin precedent at
apps/mobile/plugins/with-android-backup-rules.js which is already wired into app.json's plugins
array. Do not hand-edit native project files; they are generated.

THIS IS A NATIVE CONFIG CHANGE (app.json plugins), which per the workspace mobile-deploy policy
means TestFlight, not OTA. An OTA cannot carry it and will silently ship without it.
acceptance_criteria: An Expo config plugin (following apps/mobile/plugins/with-android-backup-rules.js) adds instagram-reels and instagram to LSApplicationQueriesSchemes and declares the Instagram package in the Android <queries> element. A prebuild produces both declarations. Availability detection returns TRUE on a physical device with Instagram installed, on both platforms, which is the actual test. No native project files are hand-edited. The change is flagged in the PR as TestFlight-only, not OTA-eligible.

title: Slice B1: custom Expo native module for Meta Sharing-to-Reels (iOS pasteboard + instagram-reels://share, Android ADD_TO_REEL intent)
description:
react-native-share does NOT support Reels. Its targets are INSTAGRAM and INSTAGRAM_STORIES only.
There is no Expo module for this either. A small custom native module is required on both
platforms, and it is the largest single line item in this epic, roughly 3-5 days including expected
iOS pasteboard debugging.

## THE MECHANISM

Meta's documented "Sharing to Reels" integration, opened from alpha to ALL developers in October
2023. It has been open to third parties since F8 in May 2018 and has not changed in eight years
apart from the 2023 App ID requirement, so it is a stable target.

iOS:
  - Write the video to UIPasteboard under the documented backgroundVideo key, along with the
    Facebook App ID. THE backgroundVideo KEY IS DOCUMENTED ON META'S REELS PAGE (unlike the Stories
    page, where it is absent despite the page stating video specs, which is one of the reasons
    Reels was chosen over Stories).
  - Open instagram-reels://share.
  - Use an expiry on the pasteboard item so the payload does not linger.

Android:
  - Build an Intent with action com.instagram.share.ADD_TO_REEL, the content URI, the MIME type and
    the Facebook App ID extra.
  - GRANT URI PERMISSION. The clip is served from a FileProvider content:// URI and Instagram is a
    different app; without FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION (and, for the chooser path, an explicit
    grantUriPermission call) Instagram receives a URI it cannot read and the handoff fails in a way
    that looks like "Instagram ignored us".

## MEDIA CONSTRAINTS TO ENFORCE BEFORE HANDING OFF

3 to 60 seconds. A clip under 3 seconds is REJECTED. 1080p recommended, under 50MB recommended.
Validate client-side and surface a real message rather than letting Instagram silently do nothing;
a silent no-op is the default failure mode of this whole mechanism and is very hard to debug from a
user report.

## THE iOS 16 PASTEBOARD PROMPT

Since iOS 16 the system can prompt before one app reads pasteboard data written by another, and
this handoff works BY pasteboard. A vendor support doc updated 2026-03-31 confirms iOS may prompt
for paste permission and for photo access mid-handoff. Spotify, Strava and Peloton all live with
it, so it is not a blocker, but it sits squarely in the conversion funnel. TEST ON DEVICE EARLY:
this cannot be verified in a simulator, and the frequency and conversion impact of the prompt are
explicitly unverified in the research.

## PREREQUISITE

A registered Facebook App ID in Live mode is required for this to work at all (since January 2023).
See the Meta prerequisites issue. Whether the App ID is validated against Meta's registry is
genuinely unresolved in both directions, so register a real one regardless: it is free, unreviewed,
and the failure mode of a fake one is a silent production break that cannot be detected
client-side.
acceptance_criteria: A custom native module hands a local video file to Instagram Reels on both platforms. iOS writes the documented backgroundVideo pasteboard key plus the Facebook App ID with an expiry and opens instagram-reels://share. Android fires com.instagram.share.ADD_TO_REEL with a FileProvider content URI, the MIME type, the App ID extra AND a read-URI-permission grant. Duration (3-60s) and size are validated client-side with a real user-facing message, never a silent no-op. Verified ON A PHYSICAL DEVICE on both platforms, with the iOS 16 pasteboard prompt observed and its behaviour documented in this issue. react-native-share is NOT used for this path.

title: [epic] Highlight clips (client): manual clip picker, Reels share handoff, Meta prerequisites
description:
Client half of the highlight-clip feature. Backend epic is jr_be-15c; the investigation that
produced both is jr_be/research/instagram-highlight-clips.md (2026-09-23). READ THAT DOCUMENT
BEFORE TOUCHING ANY CHILD ISSUE.

## Product shape

An athlete finishes a match, opens the video, picks (or is offered) a few seconds of it, gets a
9:16 clip back in under a minute, and hands it to Instagram Reels.

## Decisions already made (2026-09-24, owner). Do not reopen.

  - ATHLETE Instagram accounts, not gym accounts. This settles the mechanism as Meta's composer
    handoff rather than the Graph API, permanently.
  - Meta "Sharing to Reels": instagram-reels://share on iOS, com.instagram.share.ADD_TO_REEL on
    Android, with the generic system share sheet as fallback. REELS ONLY for v1, not Stories.
  - react-native-share DOES NOT SUPPORT REELS (its targets are INSTAGRAM and INSTAGRAM_STORIES
    only). A small CUSTOM NATIVE MODULE is required on both platforms. This is the largest single
    line item in the estimate, roughly 3-5 days including expected iOS pasteboard debugging.
  - NATIVE CHANGE, so this ships via TestFlight, NOT OTA. An OTA can never carry a native change;
    it silently ships without it.
  - The render job takes [start, end] segments as input, so manual picking and automatic selection
    are both just callers. Manual picking ships FIRST, deliberately, so clip quality can be judged
    before clip selection is trusted.

## BUILT BUT NOT ENABLED

The share path is gated by jr_be-17f, the consent decision, which is unresolved. Every outbound
share affordance in this epic sits behind feature_flags key highlight_share_enabled, seeded false,
fail-closed (missing row = off), and THAT FLAG MUST NOT BE FLIPPED TRUE WHILE jr_be-17f IS OPEN.

"Outbound share affordance" is broader than Instagram and this matters: the Reels handoff, the
generic system share-sheet fallback, AND save-to-camera-roll all hand the OTHER athlete's likeness
to a destination outside the two-participant scope. All three are behind the same flag. Do not ship
a "just save it to my photos" button as an unflagged convenience; it is the same disclosure.

The RENDER path is NOT gated, because a clip shown only to the two match participants reaches
exactly the audience that can already watch the full source video. See jr_be-17f for the full
reasoning and the one condition it rests on.

## What is impossible, so nobody designs around it

  - PREFILLED CAPTIONS. Instagram stopped honouring third-party captions in August 2015 by explicit
    policy. The industry answer, used by Strava and Peloton, is to render the information into the
    frame.
  - LINK STICKERS / attribution URLs. No programmatic mechanism on either path. An open Meta iOS
    SDK issue requesting attribution-URL support has sat untriaged since March 2025, and Strava
    ships a documented five-tap manual paste ritual instead.

## Explicitly NOT in scope

  - Sharing to Stories (20s video cap; the iOS backgroundVideo pasteboard key is UNDOCUMENTED on
    Meta's Stories page despite the page stating video specs, and react-native-share has unresolved
    reports of it silently failing on iOS).
  - The Graph API content-publishing path.
  - jits-kaf.3, the in-app community feed. Different product surface, not a prerequisite.
acceptance_criteria: An athlete can select segments of their own match video, trigger a render, watch progress, and preview the resulting 9:16 clip. The Reels handoff and the share-sheet fallback are code-complete, on-device verified, and UNREACHABLE behind highlight_share_enabled until jr_be-17f is resolved. The app ships to TestFlight, not OTA. A registered Facebook App ID exists in Live mode with the iOS bundle ID and Android package registered.

title: Capture athlete_left_id at record time to ground per-athlete attribution
description:
Every per-athlete attribution the AI pipeline produces is currently an
ungrounded guess. The fix is one tap, and the backend plumbing already exists.

## The problem

match_videos.athlete_left_id is a USER-TAGGED field by design ("which athlete
is on the left in the opening frame", 20260313000000_video_tables.sql:26).
Neither client ever writes it, so it is NULL on every row.

The shared mutation layer already supports it:
packages/shared/src/api/mutations.ts:645-689 declares optional cameraAngle,
athleteLeftId, recordedBy, recordingType and conditionally sets each. But both
callers pass a fixed four-field set that omits athleteLeftId and cameraAngle:
  - apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts:248-255
  - apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-recording.ts:285-292

## What that costs

The chunk analyzer builds its participant block from athlete_left_id at
supabase/functions/video-analyze-chunk/index.ts:846-856. With it NULL the
prompt degrades to "- Alice (Athlete 1)" / "- Bob (Athlete 2)" and camera_angle
renders as "unknown (auto-detect from video)" (:870). Gemini is then handed
both real UUIDs (:858-860, "use these exact UUIDs in your JSON output") and
asked to attribute every scoring_moment, recommendation, technique_tag,
key_frame and biomechanical_timeline entry to one of them with NO visual
grounding.

It guesses. Per chunk. Independently. With no cross-chunk anchor, so chunk 3
can swap the two athletes relative to chunk 2 and nothing detects it.

## This already degrades live surfaces

That guess is not hypothetical or future-facing. It already drives:
  - get_athlete_profile_stills, which filters
    still->>'athlete_id' = p_athlete_id (20260313300000:136) to build an
    athlete's profile stills
  - avatar-generate, which reads the same array to pick a portrait frame

So an attribution error today puts the wrong person's frames on someone's
profile. A highlight-clip generator would be the third consumer, and the first
where being wrong means publishing the wrong person's face to a PUBLIC audience
captioned with the wrong name.

## Scope

Add a "who is on the left?" selection at record or upload time and pass the
existing athleteLeftId param. Both platforms. No backend change required; the
column, the mutation param and the prompt consumption all exist already.

Consider also writing camera_angle if it can be asked cheaply in the same
interaction, since it degrades the same way.

## Related

jr_be-bhd (P3, deferred) proposes the richer version: anchoring identity across
chunks via gi/rashguard colour, belt, build. It is blocked on product because it
needs upload-time capture of gi colour "which product has said is not
supportable yet". Two ideas from it worth carrying into any implementation: a
merge-time contradiction check (chunk N says athlete_1 is in blue, chunk N+1
says white, flag the swap), and an explicit low-confidence flag when both
athletes wear the same colour rather than silently guessing.

This issue is the cheap 80% of that, and it is a prerequisite for trustworthy
per-athlete highlight clips.

Found during the Instagram clip-sharing investigation, 2026-09-23.
notes:
=== 2026-09-24: THIS IS NOW A HARD PREREQUISITE OF AUTOMATIC HIGHLIGHT SELECTION ===

The highlight-clip epics jr_be-15c (backend) and jits-s6mi (client) opened on 2026-09-24. Slice C
of the backend epic, jr_be-15c.9 (automatic per-athlete highlight segment selection), is BLOCKED ON
THIS ISSUE and says so in its own body. Cross-repo, so the dependency is textual rather than a bd
edge; it is still a hard one.

WHY: automatic selection picks segments "for athlete X" out of scoring_moments and technique_tags,
both of which carry hard athlete UUIDs that Gemini assigned WITHOUT VISUAL GROUNDING because
athlete_left_id is NULL. Getting it wrong on a profile still is embarrassing. Getting it wrong on a
clip means the wrong person's face goes to a public audience captioned with the wrong name.

MANUAL segment picking (jits-s6mi.5) does NOT depend on this, because the athlete picks their own
moments. That is one of the reasons the render endpoint was designed to take [start, end] segments
as input: it decouples clip rendering from clip attribution entirely.

A GAP WORTH RECORDING HERE, because it is not this issue's job to fix but it IS this issue's
consequence: shipping athlete_left_id capture fixes attribution GOING FORWARD ONLY. Every
already-analysed video keeps its NULL athlete_left_id and its ungrounded attribution baked into the
stored video_analyses row. So automatic selection remains untrustworthy for the entire existing
corpus unless it is re-analysed, or unless selection is restricted to rows where athlete_left_id IS
NOT NULL. jr_be-15c.9 carries that decision.

title: Exclude match-uploads/ from iCloud backup
description:
Decided: add a config plugin rather than accept the backup.

## Problem

1587740 moves pending match clips out of the purgeable camera cache into
<document>/match-uploads/<matchId>.<ext> so they survive an app kill, which
is what makes resume-after-kill work. But Paths.document resolves to
<app>/Documents/ (expo-file-system ios/FileSystemModule.swift:11-12), and iOS
backs that directory up to iCloud by default. Only Library/Caches and files
flagged NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey are exempt.

So a 300-600 MB clip parked while the user is offline becomes a backup
candidate every night, against a 5 GB free iCloud tier. It also brushes
Apple's iOS Data Storage Guidelines 2.5.2, which is a live App Review risk
once every match is recorded.

Moving back to Paths.cache is NOT the answer -- it reopens the purge problem
the file exists to solve. Library/Application Support is backed up too.

## Why a plugin is required

expo-file-system@19.0.22 exposes no backup-exclusion API. Verified across its
Swift, Kotlin and .d.ts surface; Paths exposes only cache, document and
friends. Nothing in apps/mobile sets the flag today.

## Scope

- Expo config plugin (or small native module) setting
  NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey on <document>/match-uploads/.
- Set it on directory creation in recording-file.ts, not just once, so a
  recreated directory stays excluded.
- Android has no equivalent problem, but confirm auto-backup rules do not
  sweep it either.

## Sequencing

This is a native change, so TestFlight not OTA. It does NOT block the merge
of the upload work; it blocks the first TestFlight build that ships it.
Bundle it with the device test of the RN file source, which has to happen
before this feature ships anyway.

title: Build the in-app delete path for match recordings
description:
Part 2 of the privacy-policy decision. e79b93b corrected the text to describe
what exists (retained indefinitely, removal by email). This builds the thing
the policy originally promised, after which the policy gets updated again.

## Why it is not just a button

There is no delete path on either platform today, and the backend pieces are
partial and leaky:

- match_videos_delete_own (jr_be 20260313000000_video_tables.sql:284) DOES let
  a client hard-DELETE their own row via PostgREST. No UI calls it.
- Deleting that row orphans every storage object permanently. There is no
  AFTER DELETE trigger on match_videos, and cleanup_orphaned_chunk_objects
  requires a parent row to exist, so the sweep can never see them.
- status='deleted' is in the CHECK constraint but nothing anywhere writes it.
- The policy as corrected says EITHER participant can request removal, but
  match_videos_delete_own is uploader-only, so the opponent currently has no
  route even at the API level.

## Scope

1. Decide soft vs hard delete. Soft (status='deleted') keeps the row for
   audit and lets the analysis rows cascade cleanly; hard delete needs the
   storage cleanup below regardless.
2. A jr_be RPC that deletes the row AND its storage objects (original,
   normalized, poster, chunks) in one transaction, or marks them for a sweep.
   Coordinate with jr_be-2vc, which adds the source-object sweep.
3. Decide whether the non-uploading participant can delete footage of
   themselves. The corrected policy says they can request it; making that
   self-service is a product call. Relevant: they can already WATCH it, since
   the SELECT policy is participant-scoped.
4. UI on mobile and web.
5. Update PRIVACY_POLICY.md again once it lands, replacing the "no in-app
   delete today, email us" language.

## Related

Blocks nothing, but the policy stays in its interim wording until this ships.
jr_be-umc.4 is the decision record. jr_be-2vc is the storage-sweep half.

title: P1: mobile elo-system RankRow renders the brand red as TEXT (text-cta), failing AA like web did
description: Web half fixed this session: a new --accent-cta-text token (#EC6A74 dark / #AC2B34 light) was added and the four app call sites plus components/ui/elo-system/rank-row.tsx:38,54 were moved onto it. Mobile still renders the untuned brand red as text: apps/mobile/components/ui/elo-system/rank-row.tsx:46 uses text-cta for the leader ELO. accentCta is #E63946 and measures ~4.05:1 dark / ~3.21:1 light on a plate, below AA for text. Needs a ctaText token in apps/mobile/lib/tokens.ts plus a text-cta-text utility in tailwind.config.js, mirroring the web values, then the rank-row call site. Note mobile already carries those exact hexes as stateNegative, but reusing a negative-semantics token for a leader highlight would be wrong. Keeps the documented web/mobile elo-system parity.

title: P1: CLAUDE.md contradicts the code in three places, including a dead backend path
description: CLAUDE.md:123 says 'Mobile nav still has Gyms' (false: mobile tabs are now Home/Arena/Rankings/Profile). :124 says the challenge handshake is not built on mobile (false: lib/arena/use-arena-challenge.ts is 487 lines). :13 points at /Users/msponagle/code/experiments/jr_be/ which is NOT a git repo (1 migration, last touched May 26); the real backend is /Users/msponagle/code/EloRated/jr_be (90 migrations). Supersedes jits-og2 and raises it from P3: this actively misled a review agent into believing a required migration was missing. IN PROGRESS this session.
close_reason: Fixed in 46fb344. Corrected four CLAUDE.md claims: the backend path (experiments/jr_be is not a git repo at all, 1 migration, vs EloRated/jr_be with 90), Mobile nav still has Gyms (false), the challenge handshake not built on mobile (false), and the match-video storage key. Also documented that Next 16 renamed middleware.ts to apps/web/proxy.ts, which exists and is load-bearing for auth. Added a Known gap bullet so no future agent assumes the challenge handshake is complete. Supersedes jits-og2.

title: P1: Playwright e2e gate has never run; suite red ~4 months, enforced by nothing
description: CLAUDE.md mandates 'cd apps/web && npm run test:e2e' for web route changes. Playwright browsers were never installed, so the suite failed before executing. After 'npx playwright install chromium': 8 failed, 2 passed. Failures are real (jits-rvy: the login page renders only Google/Apple SSO and Register with Email, no email/password form, so the spec's text=Login never appears). Login form last changed 2026-05-15, smoke spec 2026-04-27, so this predates the Arena work. .husky/pre-commit runs only typecheck+test; .github/workflows/ci.yml has no Playwright step. Decide: fix jits-rvy and add e2e to CI, or drop the mandate from CLAUDE.md. Do not add a red suite to CI.
notes: PARTIAL as of 46fb344: the suite itself is now GREEN (12 passed / 0 failed, verified cold and with --repeat-each=2). Root cause was jits-05xx.19 (no email/password login form) plus stale text=Login selectors that never matched anything on that page; selectors are now role-based. Playwright browsers also had to be installed locally (npx playwright install chromium) before the suite could execute at all. STILL OPEN: nothing enforces it. .husky/pre-commit runs only typecheck+test and .github/workflows/ci.yml has no Playwright step, so it can rot again silently. Decide: add e2e to CI now that it is green, or drop the mandate from CLAUDE.md.

title: P1: a complete match clip is reported to the user as cut short
description: match-upload-store.ts:104-123 merges and nothing ever clears 'truncation' per attempt, so a second recording on the same matchId inherits the first attempt's interrupted warning over a clip covering the whole match. Same root cause leaves a stale videoId, so the summary can show an error banner and a working Watch Match Video button at once. Both reproduced. IN PROGRESS this session.
close_reason: Fixed in 46fb344. Added beginMatchUploadAttempt(matchId) which REPLACES the entry rather than merging; every field except matchId is now explicitly per-attempt, documented in the store docblock. Called at the moment start() commits past every guard, so a start that never reaches the camera leaves the previous outcome intact. Also fixes the stale videoId that let the summary show an error banner and a working Watch Match Video button simultaneously.

title: P1: mobile background path awaits a 10s untrack before the durable looking_for_ranked write
description: use-arena-live.ts:138-144 awaits leaveLobby() (a presence send that buffers and resolves 'timed out' after 10s on a dead socket) before writeLookingFlag(id,false). iOS suspends the process first, so the athlete stays flagged live and unreachable. Presence lapses on its own; the flag does not. This is the failure the hook header claims to prevent and the CHANGELOG advertises as fixed. IN PROGRESS this session.
close_reason: Fixed in 46fb344. The untrack is still issued first but is no longer awaited ahead of the durable write, so the looking_for_ranked clear goes out in the same tick instead of queueing behind up to 10s of buffered presence push. Applied uniformly, not only on the background path. Tests now model the timing with a hand-released deferred, and one asserts the flag write lands while the untrack is still in flight. A foreground re-assert was added that only undoes the defensive clear, never a deliberate toggle-off.

title: P1: mobile lobby presence dies for the whole session on an unconfirmed channel release
description: use-lobby-presence.ts:184-214: when removeChannel does not return 'ok' the channel stays registered, ensure() adopts it, and channel.on() throws on a joined channel. Reproduced: channelRef never assigned, identity guard always bails, joinLobby produces zero track calls, no Challenge button renders anywhere. Reachable via a null athlete from a failed getCurrentAthlete read. The existing test mocks away the very throw production raises. IN PROGRESS this session.
close_reason: Fixed in 46fb344. An unconfirmed removeChannel now bails out of ensure() and retries with backoff (1s/2s/4s) instead of adopting the still-joined channel and calling .on() on it, which throws. The dishonest test mock was made honest: on() now throws when the channel is joined, matching RealtimeChannel, which turns the suite red against the old code with the exact production error at use-lobby-presence.ts:199.

title: P1: Rankings gym memberCount, averageElo and gym ordering all derived from a LIMIT 50 athlete scan
description: leaderboard/page.tsx:45-51 limits athletes to 50, then :80-99 groups that slice into per-gym memberCount/averageElo/totalElo and ranks gyms by totalElo. leaderboard-content.tsx:211-212 renders it as fact. With >50 active athletes the numbers and the ordering are wrong by construction. Same defect class jits-icei.2 removed from getGymsWithSessions. IN PROGRESS this session.
close_reason: Fixed in 46fb344. Replaced the top-50 client-side grouping with the existing get_gym_ladder RPC, which aggregates over every active athlete and returns an exact athlete_count and avg_elo in one round trip. get_gym_member_counts was rejected because it would have fixed only the count and left the average a slice artefact. totalElo is derived as round(avg x count), within under 1 ELO for a 15-member gym. No prop consumed by leaderboard-content.tsx changed. Side effect: the gym board now lists every active gym with at least one member, not only gyms represented in the global top 50.

title: P1: web Arena presence only re-partitions a frozen server snapshot; newly-live athletes never appear
description: arena-content.tsx:457-458 intersects live presence with the server-rendered looking_athletes, so presence can reclassify rows but never add one. Go live while someone watches /arena and you stay invisible, while they keep seeing EmptyLobby 'You are live, but nobody else is yet'. Nothing calls router.refresh() on a presence change.

title: P1: web declineChallenge/cancelChallenge Results discarded; UI reports success on a failed write
description: use-arena-challenge.ts:209,223 await the mutations and never check .ok. A failed decline dismisses the prompt, tells the challenger 'X declined', and leaves the row pending for 7 days consuming a cap slot. Mobile already fixed this at use-arena-challenge.ts:441-470; web did not.

title: Review remediation: Arena/video/token defects from the 2026-09-21 adversarial review
description: Umbrella for the defects found by the four-agent adversarial review of c40dba9..HEAD (43 commits, 123 files). Three P0s: /arena crashes on any read failure; the challenge handshake strands users on both platforms with no inbox; web still ships the WCAG AA failures that closed P0 jits-anbc reports as zero. Plus a P1 cluster and a set of process gaps (e2e gate never runs, CLAUDE.md contradicts the code).

title: [bug] Web signup discards the gyms read error, making an RLS denial look like an empty gym table
description:
FRONTEND HALF of jr_be-qhp, which blocked real account creation on PROD tonight. The backend half is fixed (jr_be migration 20260919000000_gyms_anon_select_for_signup.sql, anon may SELECT active gyms; applied to prod by hand by the owner).

THE REMAINING DEFECT IS OURS. apps/web/app/(auth)/signup/page.tsx:16 does:
  const { data: gyms } = await supabase.from('gyms').select('id, name, city').eq('status','active').order('name');
It destructures ONLY data and discards error, then every downstream use is . So an RLS denial, a PostgREST 500 and a genuinely empty gyms table are indistinguishable, and all three render an empty Home Gym selector. validateSignupForm requires gymId, so submit is blocked with no explanation and no error surfaced anywhere.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE FOR SO LONG, worth recording because it generalises: the city list has its OWN fallback (cityList = cities.length > 0 ? cities : ['Toronto','Vancouver']), so a total read failure still rendered a plausible-looking city dropdown and only the gym selector looked wrong. A partial fallback disguised a total failure.

SAME CLASS as jits-rygr (getCurrentAthlete collapsing a failed read to null) and the four shapes in the jr_be shared-query audit, but this is the most damaging instance found: it blocks account creation entirely rather than showing something false.

FIX: surface the error. Either inspect it and render an explicit 'could not load gyms, try again' state rather than an empty selector, or adopt the Result sibling pattern the shared layer now has. Do NOT rely on the backend policy alone: the page will fail this same silent way for any future read failure (network blip, PostgREST 500, a policy change), and the next person will debug it from an empty dropdown again.

PROVENANCE, recorded deliberately: I found this RLS behaviour on 2026-09-10 while trying to complete signup locally, diagnosed it correctly (gyms_select_all granted TO authenticated only, so anon reads zero rows), reported it in conversation, and added a LOCAL-ONLY policy to unblock my own testing. I never filed it. It lived in a chat message, the session moved on to other work, and it reached production. The local workaround also made local strictly more permissive than prod (USING(true) vs the real active-only policy), which is what kept it invisible locally. I have now dropped that local policy so local matches prod.

title: getMatchDetails collapses a failed read into null, and the web match pages REDIRECT on it
description:
Found by the queries.ts audit for jits-icei.5, consequence identified in review of that work. This is the highest-impact remaining instance in the file.

packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:341 (getMatchDetails) does:

    if (error || !data) return null;

No log, no distinction. supabase-js never rejects, so a dropped connection, an expired JWT or a PostgREST 5xx on get_match_details is indistinguishable from 'this match does not exist'.

WHY THIS ONE IS WORSE THAN THE EMPTY-STATE CASES: the web call sites do not render an empty state, they REDIRECT. apps/web/app/(app)/match/[id]/results/results-content.tsx:17-18 and apps/web/app/(app)/match/[id]/live/live-match-content.tsx:18-19 both redirect to /match/pending on null. A transient read failure therefore throws an athlete OUT OF THEIR LIVE MATCH, mid-match, with no error and no way back except navigating in again.

FIX SHAPE: getMatchDetailsResult sibling, same strictly-additive pattern as jits-icei.5 (loader returns payload plus error, legacy wrapper keeps returning null). The call sites then redirect only on a genuine not-found and show a retryable error otherwise.

COORDINATE: the two call sites are in apps/web, owned by another session.

title: [bug] Web video viewer bypasses normalized_path, so option B never reaches web playback
description:
MY GAP, introduced in 5b90ff1 / jr_be 6f51d99. I implemented jits-kaf.1.2 option B (slicer writes a normalized H.264/AAC MP4 for non-MP4 uploads, match_videos.normalized_path records it) and made getMatchVideoSignedUrl prefer normalized_path over storage_path. I assumed that helper was the web playback path. It is not.

apps/web/components/domain/video-analysis-viewer.tsx:138-148 does its OWN inline query and signs the original directly:
  await supabase.from('match_videos').select('storage_path').eq('id', videoId).maybeSingle()
  ... createSignedUrl(data.storage_path, 3600)
It never selects normalized_path. Verified: grep for normalized_path across apps/web returns NOTHING. getMatchVideoSignedUrl has zero web callers (only apps/mobile/app/(app)/video/[id].tsx and the shared test), so my change to it did not reach web at all.

CONSUMER: the viewer is rendered on a live surface, apps/web/.../steps/match-recorded-step.tsx:62, in the match wizard.

ACTUAL SCOPE, narrower than 'option B is inert' but exactly the case option B existed for. Since option A now makes web record MP4/H.264 wherever the browser supports it, most web recordings have an MP4 storage_path and play fine, and the slicer never normalizes them. The break is the residual cohort: a browser with no MP4 encoder records WebM, the slicer DOES write normalized_path, and the web viewer still signs the WebM. Opened on iOS Safari that is unplayable, which is the precise failure option B was built to remove.

SECONDARY: this is also a raw .from() in a component, violating the project rule that both apps use the typed wrappers in packages/shared.

FIX: have the viewer select 'storage_path, normalized_path' and prefer normalized_path, or better, call getMatchVideoSignedUrl (or the getMatchVideoSignedUrlResult sibling currently in review on the jr-be-73 branch) so the preference lives in one place. Prefer the wrapper: two copies of the preference rule is how this drifts again.

PROCESS NOTE: I verified option B end to end at the STORAGE and DB layer (artifact probed as h264/yuv420p/mp4 with faststart, normalized_path set) and never checked which web component consumes it. Changing a shared helper is not the same as changing the surface. Same class as the recompute-dont-inherit rule, applied to call sites rather than numbers.

title: getCurrentAthlete collapses a failed read into null, and the web guard redirects an active athlete to /signup
description:
Found by the queries.ts audit for jits-icei.5.

getCurrentAthlete (packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:95) logs the PostgREST error and returns null. apps/web/lib/guards.ts:29-33 reads that null as 'no athlete row exists' and redirects to /signup. supabase-js never rejects, so a dropped connection, an expired JWT or a PostgREST 5xx on this one read bounces a fully activated athlete into the signup wizard, on EVERY authenticated web page load. getActiveAthlete (guards.ts:82) has the same collapse and returns null, which callers read as 'not activated'.

Mobile is milder: AuthProvider (apps/mobile/lib/auth/auth-context.tsx:99,123) keeps athlete null until refresh rather than redirecting.

FIX SHAPE: the additive sibling pattern landed in jits-icei.5 applies directly. Add getCurrentAthleteResult returning Result<AthleteGuardRow | null> where ok:true/data:null is a genuinely absent row and ok:false is a failed read, then have requireAthlete distinguish them (an error page or a retry, not /signup). Leave getCurrentAthlete itself alone: it is the shared athlete guard and both apps consume it.

NOTE: apps/web is owned by another session, so coordinate before editing guards.ts.

title: Token mirror drift guard: brand canonical + web pending state
description:
Add a mobile jest guard that detects divergence between apps/mobile/lib/tokens.ts (source of truth) and the other design-token mirrors.

Mirrors:
1. apps/mobile/lib/tokens.ts - source of truth
2. apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js - already covered by tokens-contrast.test.ts lockstep, do not duplicate
3. apps/web/app/design-system/tokens.css - STALE, owned by jits-ozvd
4. apps/web/public/design/tokens.css - STALE, owned by jits-ozvd
5. outside_assets/Jits Arena SharePoint/Brand/design-system/tokens.css - BRAND CANONICAL, gitignored, SharePoint-synced

Behavior:
- Brand file: skip cleanly with an explanatory message when absent; MUST match mobile when present, divergence fails.
- Web files: known stale today; recorded as an explicit named PENDING divergence baseline so the suite is green now but the pending entries become obviously removable once jits-ozvd lands.
- Resolve var() indirections through CSS primitives before comparing.
- Explicit token-name mapping table; unmapped tokens are reported, not silently dropped.
close_reason: Merged to development as e6ec219. Review rejected v1 for the exact failure the guard exists to prevent: its at-rule check covered only the 17 semantic names, so a brand file regenerated with @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) redefined the primitives underneath and the guard certified agreement in green. v2 parses a real block tree and watches the transitive closure of every primitive a mapped token resolves through, computed from the file. Because the brand file is absent from CI, fresh clones and every worktree, a resolved palette snapshot is checked in and asserted against lib/tokens.ts everywhere, plus a separate AA assertion proven load-bearing (all three files agreeing on a sub-AA value still fails).

title: Shared queries discard postgrest errors, so callers cannot tell a failed read from an empty one
description:
Raised by re-review of c277f11, referenced from the fix commit. This is option (a) of the two fix shapes offered for that blocker; option (b) was taken to keep the change inside apps/mobile while another session owns web.

THE SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM: supabase-js does not reject on a failed request. postgrest-js defaults shouldThrowOnError to false (PostgrestBuilder.ts:82) and its outer handler converts even a hard fetch error into a resolved { data: null, error } (:372). Several shared query functions then destructure only 'data' and throw the error away, e.g. getGymDetail at packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:547-553 ('const { data: gym } = await ...single(); if (!gym) return null;').

CONSEQUENCE: a dropped connection, an RLS denial, an expired JWT and a PostgREST 5xx are all indistinguishable from a legitimately empty result at every call site. Any caller that tries to handle failure with try/catch or .catch is writing dead code. The mobile dashboard hit this exactly: the discovery surface told athletes 'Nothing scheduled at your gym right now' whenever the read failed, on the app's only path to a session.

WHAT DONE MEANS: the query functions surface an explicit error signal rather than folding it into null/[]. Keep it strictly ADDITIVE so web callers are unaffected (e.g. a sibling getGymDetailResult returning { data, error }, or an options flag), then migrate callers. apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/(home)/index.tsx settleGymDetail currently infers the failure from a null primary-gym read and should move onto the real signal once it exists.

AUDIT the other exported queries for the same pattern while here; getGymDetail is unlikely to be the only one.

COORDINATE: packages/shared is shared with apps/web.
close_reason: Merged to development as 96fb41e. Audit of all 49 exported queries found the error-discard pattern in FOUR distinct shapes; three additive Result siblings added with the legacy functions byte-identical so web is unaffected. Review caught a regression this change introduced (capability booleans classified fatal discarded a successfully-read live session); fixed by returning the partial payload with the capability booleans typed OUT, so the compiler refuses a caller reading an authorization decision off a failed read. Unbounded athlete scan replaced by the get_gym_member_counts RPC. DEPLOY ORDER: jr_be 06397fa must reach prod BEFORE this ships, or the gym finder renders '0 members' everywhere. Follow-ups filed: jits-k4tu (P1), jits-b7e5, jits-somt, jits-rygr, jits-osnx, jits-tydo, jits-ku9l, jr_be-9vj.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text:
SCOPE NOTE from the re-review of e18bf43: this issue is the COMPLETION of the dashboard fix, not optional polish. Do not deprioritise it.

The mobile-side mitigation (settleGymDetail in app/(app)/(tabs)/(home)/index.tsx) is PARTIAL BY CONSTRUCTION. It infers failure from getGymDetail returning null, and getGymDetail only returns null when its FIRST query fails, the gym row lookup. The mechanism:

- getGymDetail query 1 (the gyms row) fails -> data null -> 'if (!gym) return null' -> mobile infers failed -> error plate. COVERED.
- getGymDetail query 1 SUCCEEDS and query 2 (the sessions SELECT, queries.ts around :556-564) then fails -> that error is discarded too, sessions comes back as null and is coalesced to [] -> getGymDetail returns a truthy GymDetail with sessions: [] -> mobile sees detail truthy, failed false -> the surface says 'Nothing scheduled at <gym> right now'. NOT COVERED. Same false claim as the original bug, just needing a mid-sequence failure (connection dies between the two waves, per-table RLS denial, PostgREST 5xx on one request) rather than a dead connection.

The same applies to every other discarded-error query inside getGymDetail (participants, rsvps, creators).

ALSO: getGymsWithSessions never rejects either, for the same postgrest reason. So the free-agent branch's 'failed' flag is always false in production today, which makes the free-agent error plate in components/dashboard/session-discovery-section.tsx unreachable and its test an exercise of dead code. It is decorative until this issue lands, and becomes live once these queries surface a real error signal. Wire it up as part of this work rather than treating it as already working.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text:
Implemented on branch impl-shared-queries, commit 6fc2a8c (worktree .claude/worktrees/impl-shared-queries, based on development e6ec219). NOT pushed and NOT merged, per the instruction for this session.

WHAT LANDED: three additive Result siblings in packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts, getGymDetailResult / getGymsWithSessionsResult / getMatchVideoSignedUrlResult, each sharing one internal loader with its legacy counterpart so the originals keep byte-identical behaviour. Mobile Home now reads the real signal instead of inferring failure from a null gym, which closes the mid-sequence hole described in the scope note: a gym row that loads followed by a sessions read that fails is now reported as a failure instead of as 'Nothing scheduled'. The free-agent error plate is live rather than dead code. The match-video screen separates absence from failure and gained a retry.

NOT DONE HERE, filed separately from the full audit: jits-rygr (getCurrentAthlete, P1, web guard redirects an active athlete to /signup), jits-osnx (getActiveSession, same screen as Home), jits-tydo (getSessionForJoin, waiver step silently skipped), jits-ku9l (getArenaData returns null cast as ArenaData).

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text:
REVIEW FIX landed as 2d01ace on top of 6fc2a8c, then development (83626c1) merged in as e3dbf48 with the CHANGELOG conflict resolved.

The review caught an availability regression 6fc2a8c introduced: the FATAL set promotes isMemberGym and isGymManager, Home consumes neither, and settleGymDetail discarded the payload before showLoadError could use it. Nine reads succeeding including a live session, plus one failed gym_managers read, hid that session behind an error plate where the old lenient function rendered it.

Took option (b): loadGymDetail hands the payload back alongside the error as PartialGymDetail, offered only while the session list is trustworthy, with the two capability booleans typed out of it so no caller can read an authorization answer off a failed read. GymDetailResult stays assignable to Result<GymDetail>.

Filed from the same review, not fixed: jits-k4tu (P1, getMatchDetails, the web match pages REDIRECT on a transient failure, bouncing an athlete out of a live match), jits-b7e5 (getGymManagerStats false zeroes on a page any athlete can read), jits-somt (the athlete's own RSVP list wants an explicit UNKNOWN third state rather than a reclassification).

Noted for whoever picks up the manager surfaces: the isGymManager protection is forward-looking only today, because mobile lib/gym-manager/use-gym-hub.ts:63, use-gym-sessions.ts:42 and app/(app)/gyms/[id].tsx:61, plus all of web, still call the LEGACY getGymDetail and still silently demote. No test covers the isMemberGym fatal case.

title: Home landing screen ships every active athlete row: unbounded athletes scan in getGymsWithSessions, plus getGymDetail's ten serial queries
description:
DEFERRED FROM THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF THE NAVIGATION SURGERY DIFF. Real performance defect, made materially worse by the nav change, held out of that diff to keep it reviewable.

WHY THIS EXISTS. getGymsWithSessions in packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts (around lines 463 to 495) issues:

  supabase.from("athletes").select("primary_gym_id").eq("status", "active")

with NO LIMIT. That ships EVERY active athlete row to the device for the sole purpose of building a client-side member-count map. It is an unbounded table scan whose payload grows linearly with the whole athlete population, and it runs on a phone over mobile data.

The nav surgery made this a first-run problem. Home now owns gym and session discovery, so getGymsWithSessions runs on the Home LANDING SCREEN for every athlete with no primary gym. That is exactly the first-run cohort: the athletes with the least patience and the least reason to wait. What used to be a cost paid on a deliberate visit to a discovery screen is now a cost paid on the first screen after sign-in.

ALSO IN SCOPE, same load. getGymDetail (around packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts lines 542 to 666) is not a single RPC. It is roughly ten queries arranged in three serial waves. The nav change added it to every MEMBER's Home load, where it will usually be the long pole in the Promise.all that Home issues. Even after the athlete scan is bounded, Home's time-to-content will be governed by getGymDetail's serial waves.

WHAT DONE MEANS. The Home landing screen stops issuing an unbounded table scan. The preferred fix is to move the member-count aggregation SERVER SIDE into an RPC that returns counts per gym (a grouped count, not rows), rather than bounding the client query, because a bound alone produces wrong counts. If a bound is chosen instead, the counts must remain correct or be explicitly labelled as approximate in the UI. getGymDetail's serial waves should be collapsed (parallelised, or folded into a single RPC) so it stops dominating Home's load.
acceptance_criteria: The Home landing screen issues NO unbounded table scan: the `athletes` select with `eq("status","active")` and no limit is gone from the Home path, verified by inspecting the queries the screen actually fires. Member counts are produced by a server-side aggregate (an RPC returning counts per gym) or by an equivalent bounded mechanism whose counts are still correct, or are explicitly presented as approximate. Payload size for the Home load no longer grows linearly with the total active athlete population. getGymDetail's three serial waves are reduced so it is no longer the long pole in Home's Promise.all, and its query count is recorded before and after in the change description. Home renders the same information as before for both cohorts (athlete with a primary gym, athlete without one). Typecheck and the full mobile and shared test suites stay green.
notes: Deferred from the independent review of the navigation surgery diff. Pre-existing query shape, but the nav change put it on the first-run path (Home, athlete with no primary gym), which is why it is P1 now rather than a background cleanup.

title: Home discovery query cost: unbounded athlete scan in getGymsWithSessions, serial waves in getGymDetail
description:
Raised by review of c277f11 (F3). Home now runs a discovery read on every dashboard load, so two pre-existing query-shape problems moved onto the landing screen.

1. getGymsWithSessions (packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:463) issues an unbounded SELECT primary_gym_id over EVERY active athlete with no limit, purely to build a member-count map client side. It now runs on Home for free agents, which is exactly the FTUE cohort (see jits-r75). This should be a count aggregate or an RPC, not a full-table read.

2. getGymDetail is roughly ten queries in three serial waves, so it will usually be the long pole in the dashboard Promise.all. The comment in (home)/index.tsx claiming the discovery read costs latency only where it overlaps the others is optimistic and should be revisited with the fix.

Measure first on a realistic athlete count, then decide between an RPC and narrowing the reads.
close_reason: Merged to development as 96fb41e. Audit of all 49 exported queries found the error-discard pattern in FOUR distinct shapes; three additive Result siblings added with the legacy functions byte-identical so web is unaffected. Review caught a regression this change introduced (capability booleans classified fatal discarded a successfully-read live session); fixed by returning the partial payload with the capability booleans typed OUT, so the compiler refuses a caller reading an authorization decision off a failed read. Unbounded athlete scan replaced by the get_gym_member_counts RPC. DEPLOY ORDER: jr_be 06397fa must reach prod BEFORE this ships, or the gym finder renders '0 members' everywhere. Follow-ups filed: jits-k4tu (P1), jits-b7e5, jits-somt, jits-rygr, jits-osnx, jits-tydo, jits-ku9l, jr_be-9vj.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text:
Implemented on branch impl-shared-queries, commit 6fc2a8c, alongside jits-icei.5. NOT pushed and NOT merged.

The unbounded SELECT primary_gym_id over every active athlete is gone. getGymsWithSessions now calls a new RPC, public.get_gym_member_counts(), which returns one row per gym that has active members. Local dataset: 19 athlete rows down to 2 gym rows. Backend lives in jr_be as jr_be-p33, migration supabase/migrations/20260918030000_gym_member_counts.sql plus supabase/tests/056_gym_member_counts_test.sql (11 assertions), committed on the jr_be branch worktree-agent-a99a3951b29b7dfd6 at f2449d0. SECURITY INVOKER on purpose so RLS still applies and the counts match what the client-side aggregate produced.

DEPLOY ORDER: the jr_be migration must be applied before this frontend change ships. A missing RPC degrades member counts to 0 with a logged error rather than failing the gym list.

Web is a first-class consumer here (apps/web/app/(app)/gyms/gyms-content.tsx calls the same wrapper server-side), which is why this went server side rather than being bounded client side in two places.

NOT DONE: part 2 of this issue, getGymDetail's roughly ten queries in three serial waves. It is still the long pole in Home's Promise.all. The waves are genuinely dependent (session ids come from wave 1, counts from wave 2), so collapsing it means a get_gym_detail RPC, which is a bigger backend slice than this pass. The unbounded scan was the part that grew with the user table; the wave count does not.

title: Match wizard first-load failure spins forever: error branch is checked after the loading fallback
description:
DEFERRED FROM THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF jits-3929. PRE-EXISTING defect: it predates the sessionId decoupling work and the review verified the decoupling did not change it. Held out of that diff to keep the decoupling behaviour-preserving.

WHY THIS EXISTS. A first-load failure in the match wizard shows a spinner forever. The athlete never sees an error, never gets a retry, and has nothing to act on except force-quitting.

The mechanism is an ordering bug plus a null fallback:
1. apps/mobile/components/match-flow/match-flow-wizard.tsx runs `if (isLoading || !match || !step) return <WizardLoading />` BEFORE it ever runs `if (error)`. Any state where match is null short-circuits to the spinner, whatever the error state says.
2. apps/mobile/lib/match-flow/use-match-details.ts:46 sets match to null on the "Match not found" path.

Together these mean even a FAILED REFRESH falls back to the spinner. The only way to reach the "Match unavailable" splash at all is a THROWN error during refresh, because a throw leaves the previously fetched match populated so the early return does not fire. In other words the error UI exists but is reachable only on the least likely path, and the most likely path (first load fails) is the one with no UI.

WHAT DONE MEANS. Error state is checked before the loading fallback, so a first-load failure renders "Match unavailable" (or an equivalent actionable error state with a retry) instead of an indefinite spinner. The "Match not found" path is distinguishable from a still-loading state rather than collapsing into it.
acceptance_criteria: In apps/mobile/components/match-flow/match-flow-wizard.tsx the error branch is evaluated before the `isLoading || !match || !step` loading fallback, so no error state can render a spinner. A simulated first-load failure (including the "Match not found" path in apps/mobile/lib/match-flow/use-match-details.ts) renders the error splash with a way forward (retry or exit), not an indefinite spinner. A genuine in-flight load still renders the spinner, so the fix does not flash an error during normal loading. Tests cover three cases: first-load failure, failed refresh, and thrown-error refresh, all reaching the error UI. Mobile typecheck and the full mobile and shared test suites stay green.
notes: Deferred from the independent review of jits-3929. Pre-existing: it predates the sessionId decoupling and the review verified the decoupling left it unchanged. It was kept out of that diff so the decoupling stayed behaviour-preserving.

title: Accessibility token repair, WEB half of jits-anbc: apply the AA fixes to both apps/web tokens.css mirrors
description:
WEB HALF of jits-anbc. jits-anbc fixed the WCAG AA contrast failures on MOBILE ONLY (apps/mobile/lib/tokens.ts and apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js). That two-file scope was deliberate: a separate Claude session owns apps/web and is actively editing there, so a concurrent web edit would have collided. This issue is the other half.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Two web files are hand-mirrored copies of the same token set and both still carry every failure jits-anbc repaired:
1. apps/web/app/design-system/tokens.css (the known mirror, named in the original jits-anbc description).
2. apps/web/public/design/tokens.css (a near-identical copy that was previously unknown; its dark block is `:root` only, and it has a trailing utility-resets section). The mirror count is therefore FOUR files, not the three jits-anbc claims.

Because mobile moved and web did not, mobile and web have now DIVERGED on 9 or more variables per theme where they previously agreed. Until this lands, the design system is not a single source of truth and any web screen built against it inherits the failing values.

WHAT DONE MEANS. Apply the deltas below to BOTH web files. MATCH BY TOKEN NAME, NOT BY LINE NUMBER: the two files are near-identical but not line-aligned, and the public copy's dark selector differs.

DARK block (`:root, [data-theme="dark"]` in app/design-system/tokens.css; `:root` only in public/design/tokens.css):
- `--color-plate`: #1A1D24 to #1E222B
- `--color-plate-bright`: #242832 to #262A34
- `--text-tertiary`: from var(--color-data-gray) to #8D929D
- `--state-neutral`: from var(--color-data-gray) to #8D929D
- `--text-on-accent`: from var(--color-terminal-white) to var(--color-void)
- `--state-negative`: from var(--color-signal-red) to #EC6A74
- `--accent-cta-text`: NEW token, #EC6A74
- `--accent-cta-hover`: #F0556B, unchanged
- `--border-hairline`: rgba(107,114,128,0.25) to rgba(107,114,128,0.45)
- `--border-hairline-faint`: alpha 0.12 to 0.20
- `--border-hairline-strong`: alpha 0.40 to 0.62

LIGHT block (`[data-theme="light"]`):
- `--color-paddock`: #F2F4F7 to #F8FAFC
- `--color-gain-green-dark`: #15803D to #116A33
- `--text-tertiary`: to #575C68
- `--state-neutral`: to #575C68
- `--text-on-accent`: to var(--color-void)
- `--state-negative`: to #AC2B34
- `--accent-cta-text`: NEW token, #AC2B34
- `--accent-cta-hover`: from var(--color-signal-red-dark) (#C42939) to #F0556B
- `--border-hairline`: rgba(13,15,20,0.14) to rgba(13,15,20,0.22)
- `--border-hairline-faint`: alpha 0.07 to 0.11
- `--border-hairline-strong`: alpha 0.25 to 0.34

EXPLICITLY UNCHANGED, do not touch: `--color-signal-red` #E63946 (the brand red stays), `--accent-cta` in both themes, `--text-primary`, `--text-secondary`, dark `--state-positive` #22C55E, `--color-void`, `--color-panel`, `--color-terminal-white`, `--color-data-gray-bright`, and the paddock panel / plate / plate-bright primitives.

THREE TRAPS, each one a way to get this wrong:
TRAP 1. Do NOT edit the `--color-data-gray` primitive. It looks like the obvious single place to fix tertiary text, but it is wrong twice over: dark and light now need DIFFERENT tertiary values (#8D929D and #575C68), and that same primitive is also the literal ink of the dark hairline rgba(107,114,128,...), so moving it would drag the borders with it. Override the SEMANTIC tokens per theme instead, exactly the way `--color-gain-green-dark` already exists as a light-only primitive.
TRAP 2. Web also needs the text/fill split that mobile got. Four `color: var(--accent-cta)` TEXT call sites must move to `var(--accent-cta-text)`: app/(app)/page.tsx:341, app/(app)/settings/settings-content.tsx:56, app/(app)/profile/profile-hero.tsx:151, and app/design/web-layouts/concepts/strava-feed.tsx:420. The two borderColor uses STAY on `--accent-cta`: app/(app)/settings/feedback/feedback-form.tsx:148 and app/(app)/gyms/[id]/gym-rsvp-action.tsx:69. Fill and border keep the brand red; only text moves to the lightened or darkened variant.
TRAP 3. Setting light `--accent-cta-hover` to #F0556B leaves the `--color-signal-red-dark` primitive with no remaining references. Either delete it or leave it in place with a comment saying it is intentionally unreferenced. Do not leave it silently dangling.
acceptance_criteria: Both apps/web/app/design-system/tokens.css and apps/web/public/design/tokens.css carry every delta listed in the description, matched by token name, with the public copy's `:root`-only dark selector and trailing utility-resets section preserved. Every text-on-surface pair in both web themes measures at least 4.5:1 for normal text, verified by computed contrast and not by eye. `--color-signal-red` #E63946 and `--accent-cta` are unchanged in both themes. `--accent-cta-text` exists in both themes in both files. The `--color-data-gray` primitive is NOT modified; tertiary and neutral are overridden per theme on the semantic tokens. The four `color: var(--accent-cta)` text call sites are moved to `var(--accent-cta-text)` and the two borderColor uses are left on `--accent-cta`. `--color-signal-red-dark` is either deleted or commented as intentionally unreferenced. A side-by-side diff of the four mirrors (two mobile, two web) shows the same values for every shared token, so mobile and web no longer diverge. Web typecheck, lint and the full test suite stay green.
notes:
COORDINATION REQUIRED BEFORE STARTING. A different Claude session owns apps/web and was actively working in that tree when jits-anbc shipped, which is the sole reason the web half was split out. Whoever picks this up must coordinate with that session (or confirm it has finished and its work is committed) before touching either tokens.css, otherwise the edits will collide the same way they would have the first time.

The second mirror, apps/web/public/design/tokens.css, was unknown when jits-anbc was written. Its existence is why jits-anbc's "all three token files" acceptance criterion is wrong: there are four.
close_reason: Done as part of jits-05xx.3 in 46fb344. Both web mirrors now measure 4.60:1 minimum with zero failing text pairs in both themes; all four token mirrors agree and pending-web-drift.json is empty. A new --accent-cta-text token was added for the brand red used as TEXT (it cannot pass AA at the locked brand value) and applied to the five web call sites. The mobile half of that last piece is jits-05xx.20.
