When jits-ozvd updates a web token the mobile suite turns RED on purpose, with the exact ledger lines to delete. Deleting them is the intended cleanup step, not a test bug.

title: Test coverage for the record, upload, watch sequence
description:
WHY: the existing tests cover the two units in the middle and nothing at the seams, which is exactly where every gap in this epic lives. Covered today: `__tests__/lib/video/upload-recording.test.ts` (9 cases), `use-video-recorder.test.ts` (13 cases), `step-router.test.ts`, `ready-step.test.tsx`, plus packages/shared `match-video.test.ts` and `athlete-videos.test.ts`. NOT covered at all: LiveStep, CameraOverlay, UploadProgressBanner, `video/[id].tsx`, PastMatchVideos, the normalized_path-over-storage_path preference in getMatchVideoSignedUrl, and the whole record to upload to watch sequence as one flow. There is no mobile e2e harness.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- Component coverage for LiveStep, CameraOverlay, UploadProgressBanner (all four banner states), `video/[id].tsx` (all error states), and PastMatchVideos.
- A test asserting getMatchVideoSignedUrl prefers `normalized_path` and falls back to `storage_path`. Mobile records MP4 so normalized_path is null and storage_path is signed; that behavior is correct on prod and must not silently invert.
- An integration-level test of the sequence: match ends, recorder stops, upload starts, banner persists across step changes, success, playback reachable.
- Say explicitly whether a mobile e2e harness is worth standing up for this, and file it separately if so. Do not quietly start building one inside this issue.

ORDERING: after the two P0 fixes, so the tests encode the corrected behavior rather than the broken one.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (tests).
acceptance_criteria: Every surface listed above has coverage. The normalized_path preference is asserted. One test walks the full end-to-upload-to-playable sequence. The suite is green in the standard mobile test command and the coverage gap list in this issue is empty or the remainder is filed.

title: Relocate the gym-manager entry point onto /gyms/[id] and keep all 7 manager routes alive
description:
WHY: the manager portal is currently reachable only by tapping the manager-gated tab. That tab is coming out, so the entry point has to exist somewhere else BEFORE it does, or seven routes and two directories of code become unreachable.

WHERE IT GOES: `/gyms/[id]` already has manager affordances (Start Session, SessionTemplates, EditGymSheet) gated on an `isGymManager` flag that comes from `getGymDetail`. That flag is already computed and already correct. Add a "Manage gym" entry to that screen behind the same flag, mirroring web's `/gyms/[id]/manage` link that shipped in 5b90ff1.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- `/gyms/[id]` shows a manager entry point when `isGymManager` is true and nothing when it is false.
- Tapping it lands on `/gym-manager` (the hub) with the gym in context.
- All seven manager routes still resolve: /gym-manager, /gym-manager/sessions, /roster, /athlete/[id], /stats, /stats-by-elo, /ladder.
- No file under `lib/gym-manager/` or `components/gym-manager/` is deleted in this issue.
- SessionEditSheet is still reachable (it is the only way to edit an existing session on mobile).

NOTE, worth a follow-up not a change here: the gym ladder is NOT manager-scoped data (`lib/gym-manager/use-gym-ladder.ts:17` has no manager predicate). It is a general feature stranded behind a manager tab. It should probably surface for everyone on the gym detail screen. File that as a separate issue rather than widening this one.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). JS only.
acceptance_criteria: A gym manager can reach /gym-manager from /gyms/[id] with no tab bar involvement. A non-manager sees no manager entry and gets no route they should not have. All seven manager routes load and render. SessionEditSheet opens and saves. Verified on device for both a manager and a non-manager account.
close_reason: Merged to development as 7e2da39. Both gym tabs removed, routes relocated not deleted with every URL verified unchanged, discovery moved to Home, manager entry on /gyms/[id], gyms[0] hard-wiring fixed with the gym id validated against managed gyms. Independent review rejected the first discovery fix (routed through a .catch that supabase-js never fires) and the corrected version is proven by a test that fails against the old implementation. jits-icei.5 completes the error-signal work.

title: A failed upload is a dead end: persist the recording and offer a manual retry
description:
GAP 4. WHY: today a failed upload gets exactly ONE automatic retry (`lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:178-231`), and then the file URI is discarded along with the hook. No persistence, no queue, no manual retry. The user recorded their match and the footage is gone, with no action available. `lib/network/mutation-queue.ts` exists but covers only result and confirm writes, not video.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- The local recording URI plus the metadata needed to upload it (match id, uploader athlete id, intended storage path) survive the hook unmounting and survive an app restart.
- A failed upload is retryable by the user from the persistent upload banner, and the retry reuses the SAME storage path so a partial or duplicate does not appear.
- Decide and state whether video joins `lib/network/mutation-queue.ts` or gets its own queue. Video is large, file-backed, and has different retry economics from a small JSON mutation, so a separate video queue is probably right; say which you chose and why.
- A recording that can never be uploaded (file gone, match deleted) is cleaned up rather than retried forever.

ORDERING: after the persistent banner, which is where the Retry CTA lives.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: Kill the app mid-upload, reopen it, and the pending upload is still there and retryable. A retry after a failure succeeds and produces exactly one match_videos row at the original storage path. A permanently unresolvable recording is cleaned up and stops asking. Covered by tests including the restart path.
notes:
CORRECTION to the note left on jits-od3 at commit 37e52ec, which claimed the state was 'shaped so a retry action can be added without moving it again'. The LAYER is now right (commit 3b8e97f puts the upload outcome in a match-keyed store at apps/mobile/lib/video/match-upload-store.ts, which survives remounts and late completions, and records storagePath so a retry reuses the same key per jits-voh). But the hook retains nothing to retry WITH: fileUri exists only as a parameter of handleUpload and the storage path is a local inside it, neither held in a ref. This issue still needs lastFileUriRef, and an exported retry() on useVideoRecorder that re-drives uploadRecording against the stored path. No second hoist required, but not free either. clearMatchUpload(matchId) exists for this issue to reset an entry it is about to replace.
N3 from the b5b7d8c review, and it belongs here because storagePath is what this issue needs. The match-upload store (apps/mobile/lib/video/match-upload-store.ts) evicts the oldest entry past MAX_TRACKED_MATCHES=8. If an entry is evicted while its upload is STILL IN FLIGHT, the late write re-creates the entry from defaults, which loses two things: truncation, so a clip the OS cap cut short renders the GREEN CHECKMARK that jits-2zpe explicitly forbids, and storagePath, so a retry has no key to reuse and would strand the failed attempt's object at a stale path (the jits-voh double-orphan). Unreachable in practice: it needs nine matches in one JS context with an upload still running across the other eight, roughly an 80-minute upload. Cheap fixes when this issue lands: never evict an entry whose status is 'uploading', or carry truncation and storagePath on the write that re-creates it. Reviewer confirmed the ordinary eviction tie-break is sound (a freshly-written entry survives); this is only the in-flight case.

title: DECISION: mobile design-direction proposal for user approval (gates all style code)
description:
WHY THIS IS FIRST AND BLOCKING: the user has explicitly said the team owes them a design-direction PROPOSAL for approval BEFORE any style code is written. Writing style code first and asking after is not an option here. Every other issue in this epic is blocked on this one.

WHAT THE PROPOSAL MUST CONTAIN:
- A concrete direction, not a menu of adjectives. Show it: screens rendered in the proposed direction, not a token table.
- What changes and what explicitly does NOT. Dark-first stays. Flat stays (no shadows is an explicit brand rule, not an oversight).
- The typography story, because it is the expensive one. There are ~440 hardcoded `text-[Npx]` classes and only 25 uses of the default scale. Any type refresh either adds a fontSize scale first or pays a ~440 call-site migration. Say which, and what it costs.
- The token story: three hand-mirrored token files (mobile tailwind.config.js, mobile lib/tokens.ts, web design-system/tokens.css) with nothing enforcing sync. Say whether this direction fixes that or lives with it.
- What needs a NATIVE REBUILD versus what ships OTA, in a single explicit list, so the user is approving a delivery plan and not just a look.
- The ELO token family (surface/ink/cta/hairline) is the live system with ~1300 usages; the legacy shadcn family has ~34 left. The proposal should assume the ELO family wins.

DELIVERY: proposal, no code.
acceptance_criteria: A rendered proposal has been presented to the user and either approved, approved with changes, or rejected, and the outcome is recorded on this issue. No style implementation issue was started before that outcome exists.
notes: USER DECISION 2026-09-18: Direction A (Instrument) APPROVED. Keep the ELO identity, fix the execution: named type scale, legible floor, hairlines that draw a real card edge, Bebas header titles, CTA-colored active tab icon, palette moves only where it fails contrast. ALSO APPROVED: (1) the accessibility repair ships FIRST, ahead of the nav and Arena work, as a standalone token-only change; (2) the text floor RISES from 10px to 11px, which is the ~163 call site migration. CORRECTION to the design proposal, verified by independent computation: the proposed CTA deepening to #D22736 yields 4.37:1 against label #E8EDF2, NOT the claimed 5.14:1, so it still fails AA. Do NOT change the brand red. Instead keep accentCta #E63946 and darken the BUTTON LABEL to the existing Void token #0D0F14, which measures 4.60:1 and passes AA. This removes the only native-rebuild item from the style plan, so the entire refresh is now OTA shippable and jits-5cg4 is no longer forced by the contrast work.
close_reason: Direction A approved by user, with an a11y-first phase and an 11px floor. Correction to the CTA remedy recorded in notes.

title: Mount MatchFlowWizard at a sessionless /match/[matchId] so an Arena match gets recording for free
description:
WHY: this is where Arena and the video work meet, and it is the payoff for doing the wizard decoupling first. Once MatchFlowWizard no longer requires `sessionId`, an Arena match can mount it with an Arena exit, and because the wizard's live step is where the camera lives (`steps/live-step.tsx:67` useVideoRecorder, `:135` CameraOverlay), the Arena match inherits the ENTIRE record, upload, watch pipeline with zero Arena-specific video code. Every fix from the video hardening epic applies to it automatically.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- A route `apps/mobile/app/(app)/match/[matchId].tsx` that loads the match and mounts MatchFlowWizard with `exitHref` pointing back at Arena and `exitLabel` reading "Back to Arena".
- Both parties reach it from the match_started broadcast.
- The wizard derives its initial step from `matches.status` exactly as it does for session matches (`lib/match-flow/step-router.ts`), so a party who backgrounds and returns resumes at the right step.
- A sessionless match completes end to end: ready, live, end, result, confirm, summary, and Done returns to Arena.

ASSUMPTION TO VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING: the exact mobile route shape. This spec proposes `/(app)/match/[matchId]` by analogy with web's `/arena/match/[matchId]` from 5b90ff1. Confirm against the actual mobile routing tree and say in the PR what you chose.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: An Arena match runs the full wizard with no session, records video on the live step, uploads it, and Done returns to Arena with the label "Back to Arena". Backgrounding and reopening mid-match resumes at the correct step. A session match is unaffected. Verified on two devices on prod including the resulting video being watchable.
notes:
Implemented on branch impl-arena-core at 2afeaa4 (worktree .claude/worktrees/impl-arena-core), not yet merged. Code complete and green through typecheck plus 543 mobile tests in 41 suites; six guards mutation-tested. Left in_progress on purpose: the acceptance criteria for jits-y1lg and jits-xg50 require verification on two physical devices against prod, which has not been done, and jits-54km asks for a watchable video from a real sessionless match. Close only after that device pass.
Review round 1 addressed in fbdc24e (branch impl-arena-core, merged with development e6ec219). Fixed: the second-accept dead latch (A1), going live then backgrounding leaving you live forever (A2/A5), the lobby channel zombie on remount (A3), the cap misattribution when an opponent leaves (A4), the iOS 'inactive' false positive (A6), and a dead MATCH_ALREADY_EXISTS retry plus its fictional test (A7). Product change applied: stay live until you leave the Arena TAB. Gate: typecheck clean, 201 shared, 578 mobile in 43 suites. Still in_progress pending the two-device prod pass.
close_reason: Merged to development as 64b6f60 (Arena). Implementation complete and independently reviewed with all four must-fix defects closed and mutation-proven. NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE: needs a two-device pass against prod for the live handshake, plus the tab-focus walk against a real navigation tree and the Arena exit replace from a pushed match route.

title: Move gym and session discovery onto the Home dashboard
description:
WHY: this is the hard prerequisite of removing the Gyms tab. Session discovery today runs ONLY through the Gyms tab: Gyms, then /gyms/[id], then join session. Home has an active-session card but NO way to find a NEW session. Pull the Gyms tab without this and a user with no active session has no path to one.

WHAT DONE MEANS: Home gains a discovery surface that covers both jobs the Gyms tab did.
- Find a gym: reach `/gyms` (the list) and `/gyms/[id]` (detail) from Home.
- Find a session: surface joinable sessions directly on Home so the common case ("I want to train now") does not require knowing which gym to open first. At minimum: sessions at the athlete's primary gym. If that is empty, the surface must say so and still offer the gym list rather than rendering nothing.
- The existing active-session card keeps its current behavior and priority. A user already in a session should see that first, not discovery.
- Zero-state: an athlete with no primary gym (free agent) still gets a usable path. See the FTUE epic jits-r75 for the established zero-state copy direction; do not invent a competing empty state.

DO NOT: delete the /gyms routes, change the gym detail screen, or move manager affordances here. Manager relocation is its own issue.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). JS only.
acceptance_criteria: From Home alone, with the Gyms tab hypothetically gone, a user can: see joinable sessions, join one, browse gyms, and open a gym detail page. A free agent with no primary gym sees a non-empty, actionable surface. An athlete with an active session still sees the active-session card first. Verified on device.
close_reason: Merged to development as 7e2da39. Both gym tabs removed, routes relocated not deleted with every URL verified unchanged, discovery moved to Home, manager entry on /gyms/[id], gyms[0] hard-wiring fixed with the gym id validated against managed gyms. Independent review rejected the first discovery fix (routed through a .catch that supabase-js never fires) and the corrected version is proven by a test that fails against the old implementation. jits-icei.5 completes the error-signal work.

title: Delivery gate: local expo run:ios plus EAS Update only, no cloud build or TestFlight without an explicit go
description:
WHY: this program ships iteratively onto hardware the user already has. EAS cloud builds are slow, cost money, and this repo has a documented history of cloud-build-only failures that do not reproduce locally (see the `eas-cloud-build-env-vars` and `eas-pod-drift-appcheckcore` memories). TestFlight adds an Apple review round trip on top. The user has explicitly withheld approval for both.

WHAT DONE MEANS: a written, followed rule for this program. Every implementer classifies their change before opening a PR. JS-only and asset-only changes go out over EAS Update. Anything that touches the compiled app stops and comes back to the user.

THE RULE:
1. Default to OTA (EAS Update). It reaches already-installed builds in seconds.
2. Verify on device with `npx expo run:ios --device <udid>` (recipe in the `on-device-dev-build-recipe` memory; Matt's iPhone udid 00008120-001E64AE1147401E).
3. STOP and ask the user before any `eas build` or TestFlight submission. A native change silently ships WITHOUT its native half if pushed as an OTA, so misclassification is a data-loss-grade mistake, not a cosmetic one.
4. Never bump `expo.version` for an OTA release: `runtimeVersion.policy` is "appVersion", so a bump orphans the update.

NATIVE-REBUILD TRIGGERS in this codebase: any new native dependency; app.json changes to icon, splash, adaptive icon, notification accent color, userInterfaceStyle, edgeToEdgeEnabled, scheme, bundle id, plugins, or updates config; an Expo SDK bump; a marketing version bump.

DELIVERY: policy issue, no code.
acceptance_criteria: Every issue in this program carries an explicit OTA-vs-native-rebuild line. No `eas build` or TestFlight submission has been run during this program without a recorded explicit user approval. At least one OTA update has been published and verified reaching the device.

title: [epic] Arena on mobile: full web parity plus a swipe surface
description:
WAVE 2a. Depends on the wizard decoupling (1a) and the tab slot (1b).

Full spec, including all screen states, the realtime channel contract, the swipe options and the open questions, is in the design notes on this epic and saved at scratchpad/ARENA-MOBILE-SPEC.md.

WHY: mobile has ZERO Arena surface. No route, no tab, no lobby presence, no challenge-issuing path. The only challenge affordance is a DISABLED button on the athlete profile (`apps/mobile/app/(app)/athlete/[id].tsx:127-137`) whose onPress is `toast.info('Challenges coming soon')`. Meanwhile mobile already CONSUMES the other half: `usePendingChallenges` drives the bell badge and `notification-item.tsx` renders challenge_received / accepted / declined. The app can tell you that you were challenged and gives you no way to challenge anyone. Arena closes that loop.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE: the entire data layer is in `packages/shared` and is platform agnostic. `createChallenge` (mutations.ts:28), `acceptChallenge` (:61), `declineChallenge` (:82), `cancelChallenge` (:102), `startMatchFromChallenge` (:122, idempotent), `toggleMatchPreferences` (:755), `getArenaData` (queries.ts:126). NO shared-package change is needed for the data path. The new code is an RN port of two web-local hooks plus the screens.

NAMING WARNING: "Jits Arena" is the RETIRED product name (now ELO RATED, see jits-1ho). The Arena feature has nothing to do with it. Do not let copy, analytics event names, or channel names reintroduce the old brand.

DELIVERY: all children are OTA-safe (EAS Update) as specced. If an implementer needs a gesture or animation package that is not already in apps/mobile/package.json, that flips the classification to native rebuild and must come back to the user first.
design:
ARENA MOBILE SPEC (condensed; full version at scratchpad/ARENA-MOBILE-SPEC.md).

NAV ENTRY: Arena is a first-class tab, second slot. Route `apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/arena/` with `index.tsx` (lobby) and `swipe.tsx` (deck). A header action toggles between them: two presentations of one roster, not two features. Secondary entry is the athlete-profile Challenge button.

PRODUCT FLOW, mirroring web exactly: the go-live toggle writes `looking_for_ranked = true` and clears `looking_for_casual` (ranked only), then joins the `lobby:online` Presence channel. The list splits into "Online now" (present in lobby:online) and "Open to challenges" (flagged looking but not present). Challenge buttons appear on ONLINE rows only. Challenge fires `createChallenge`; the opponent gets a live incoming prompt via a filtered postgres_changes INSERT on `challenges` (channel `arena-incoming:${athleteId}`); Accept runs `acceptChallenge`, then `startMatchFromChallenge`, then BROADCASTS `match_started` on `arena-challenge:${challengeId}` BEFORE navigating, so both parties land together. There is NO inbox, and mobile must not invent one: the prompt is live, and anything missed falls back to the existing notification bell.

QUERY LIMIT: `getArenaData` is called with limit 100, NOT the RPC default of 20. Web learned this the hard way; a low limit silently hid live athletes and under-reported the online count.

DOUBLE-TAP: blocked by a synchronous `busyRef`, not by React state, which settles too late.

STATES: loading (skeleton rows, not a blank screen), empty roster, nobody online (the Online section carries its own empty copy while Open to challenges still lists), not-live-yourself (Challenge buttons disabled WITH the reason, not hidden), outgoing pending (row flips to "Challenge sent" plus Cancel), incoming prompt (bottom sheet, self-dismissing if the challenger cancels), already challenged (row disabled, "Pending"), declined (toast, row returns to challengeable), error (inline plate with Retry inside the affected section, never a bare toast over a lying list).

REALTIME, three channels, all plain supabase-js:
1. `lobby:online` Presence, payload {athlete_id, display_name, current_elo}; presenceState drives the split.
2. `arena-incoming:${athleteId}` postgres_changes, filtered INSERT on challenges server side, not client-side discard.
3. `arena-challenge:${challengeId}` broadcast `match_started`.
`lobby:online` is a SECOND channel alongside the existing app-wide `app:online`. They are not the same channel and must not be merged.

PRESENCE PORT HAZARD: mobile presence has a known failure mode (jits-a8y.1, memory `mobile-qa-sweep-jits-a8y`) where a per-mount channel never syncs. The lobby channel must be created once and survive re-render.

VIDEO FOR FREE: an Arena match reaches MatchFlowWizard, whose live step mounts the recorder (`steps/live-step.tsx:67` useVideoRecorder, `:135` CameraOverlay). So Arena inherits record, upload, and watch with ZERO Arena-specific video code, including every fix from the video hardening epic. That shared integration point is why 1a is sequenced first and why Arena and video can then run in parallel.

SWIPE: web's /arena/swipe is DECORATIVE (local useState tally, zero Supabase writes, no persistence, not even linked from /arena; lineage is the abandoned Figma Make prototype at ~/code/EloRated/Jitsarena). There is nothing to port. Recommendation is Option A, swipe to challenge, with a confirm sheet. See the swipe decision issue.
acceptance_criteria: From the Arena tab a user can go live, see who else is live, challenge someone, be challenged, accept, and land in the match wizard alongside their opponent, with the match recording automatically. The swipe surface ships whatever behavior the swipe decision issue settles on. All states from the spec (loading, empty, nobody online, outgoing pending, incoming prompt, already challenged, declined, error) are implemented and verified. Two physical devices tested against each other on prod.
notes:
ORCHESTRATOR DECISIONS 2026-09-18, resolving the PM's open questions 2 through 7 so Arena is unblocked. These are defaults chosen to mirror shipped web behavior; raise them with the user only if implementation shows one is wrong.

Q2 must you be live to send a challenge: YES. Challenge affordances appear on ONLINE rows only, mirroring web (arena-content.tsx:196-201). The handshake is realtime, so an offline opponent cannot answer a live prompt. Offline rows show a status tag and no button. Design the not-live state as a nudge to go live, not as a dead button.

Q3 Arena match exit: back to ARENA. exitLabel 'Back to Arena'. This is what web passes and it keeps the loop tight (finish a match, immediately find the next opponent).

Q4 ranked vs casual: RANKED ONLY, mirroring web. The go-live toggle writes looking_for_ranked true and clears looking_for_casual. Casual was removed in 47f166b. Do not expose a segmented control.

Q5 does live persist: NO, CLEAR THE FLAG ON EXIT. This is a real bug, not just a preference: Presence drops automatically on channel teardown but the looking_for_ranked DB column does not, so athletes linger in the 'Open to challenges' list forever after closing the app. Clear the flag when leaving Arena and on app background. Verify the paired case: presence join and flag write must not drift apart, or the two lists lie.

Q6 push on challenge: the trigger EXISTS. on_challenge_created (AFTER INSERT ON public.challenges) runs notify_push_function, which POSTs to the push edge function via pg_net (jr_be 20260220000000_push_subscriptions.sql:181-185). BUT it depends on the app.settings.service_role_key and edge function URL GUCs, and jits-kaf.1.8 records that no migration sets them and all four fail silently. So assume challenge push is DEAD on prod. Arena does not care, its handshake is realtime. Mutual-match swipe notifications WOULD care, so do not design swipe around a push that does not fire. Confirm GUC state on prod before relying on it.

Q7 swipe deck contents: ELO-PROXIMITY BAND, not online-only. Swipe is the asynchronous path (see jits-oz0s), so gating it on presence would collapse it into Arena. Note the web deck is not a model to copy: it uses a raw supabase.from('athletes') call, which violates the project rule that both apps go through the typed wrappers in packages/shared, and its comment claims ELO proximity while the code orders by absolute current_elo descending, so it returns the top 30 players rather than anyone near your rating. Mobile needs a real typed proximity wrapper in packages/shared. Another session owns that file, so coordinate before adding it.

title: [epic] Mobile navigation surgery: 4-up tab bar, gym and session discovery on Home, manager entry relocated
description:
WAVE 1b. Runs in parallel with the wizard decoupling (they touch disjoint files).

WHY: the mobile tab bar currently registers five tabs (`apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx`): (home) Home, gyms Gyms, leaderboard Rankings, gym-manager Gym (manager-only), profile Profile. The custom bar (`components/layout/elo-tab-bar.tsx`) is hand-rolled and its own comment claims a 4-up grid, so it is already mis-specified against what it renders. Arena has no slot. Two of the five tabs are gym surfaces, one of which most users never see.

THE CENTRAL CONSTRAINT: this is a RELOCATE, not a DELETE. The gym-manager tab owns seven routes (/gym-manager, /sessions, /roster, /athlete/[id], /stats, /stats-by-elo, /ladder) plus `lib/gym-manager/` (13 files) and `components/gym-manager/` (11 components). Capabilities that exist ONLY there and would be destroyed by deletion: the ELO-ordered gym roster, per-member drill-down, the 30d/90d/all stats dashboard, ELO-bracket stats, the cross-gym ladder, and SessionEditSheet, which is the ONLY edit-an-existing-session UI on mobile. Deleting the routes would silently remove all of it with no replacement. Keep every route alive and reachable.

WHAT MAKES THIS TRACTABLE: nothing outside `gym-manager/` navigates into it. Zero inbound `router.push` or `Link` from anywhere in the app. It is entered solely by tapping the tab. No expo-router typed routes are enabled, so there is no generated route-type file to update (nav calls are cast `as never`). No deep link or push payload targets a gym route: the Android intentFilters register only /athlete and /session. So the surgery is genuinely contained.

THE ONE REAL RISK: session discovery today runs ONLY through the Gyms tab (Gyms, then /gyms/[id], then join session). Home has an active-session card but no way to find a NEW session. Removing the Gyms tab without first putting discovery on Home would strand every user who is not already in a session. That is why the Home work is a hard prerequisite of the tab removal in this graph.

DELIVERY: all children are OTA-safe (EAS Update). The tab bar and every app header are custom JS.
acceptance_criteria: The tab bar renders exactly four tabs: Home, Arena, Rankings, Profile. From a cold start a user can still reach: a gym, a session to join, the gym manager portal (if they manage a gym), the roster, per-member drill-down, both stats screens, the ladder, and session editing. No route was deleted. No dangling back-navigation target remains.

title: Verify stop-then-unmount on real hardware: the stop re-issue loop races CameraView teardown
description:
GAP 11. WHY: the stop path is the last unverified piece of the capture sequence, and if it loses, it loses the whole clip silently.

CONTEXT, READ IT BEFORE TOUCHING CODE: jits-a8y.13 already fixed and CLOSED the logical half of this (pending-stop intent, stop re-issued on a 250ms interval up to 8 attempts over a ~2s window, stale-closure guard via a state ref). But its own closing note carries an explicit caveat: the JS contract was verified against a FAKE camera, and both feared native behaviors have been observed live on hardware (recordAsync rejecting with "Camera is not ready yet" even after onCameraReady, and stopRecording being silently ignored). The remaining exposure is the race between that up-to-2s re-issue loop and React tearing down CameraView in the SAME commit. If recordAsync rejects during teardown, the clip is silently lost.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- Exercise the stop-then-unmount sequence on physical iOS hardware (and Android if available) across: a normal end, an end within the first second of recording, an end during the camera-not-ready retry window, and an end while the app is backgrounding.
- Add instrumentation good enough to tell, from a device log, WHICH branch a lost clip took. The `[video]` log tags already exist and are athlete-id prefixed per device (see the `on-device-dev-build-recipe` memory); extend them rather than inventing a parallel scheme.
- If the race is real, fix it: hold the camera mounted until the record promise settles rather than racing teardown.
- If it is NOT reproducible, say so explicitly and record what was tested, so the next person does not re-litigate it.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update) unless the fix requires a camera-library change, which would be a native rebuild.
acceptance_criteria: All four end-timing scenarios exercised on physical hardware with the outcome recorded per scenario. No scenario loses a clip silently: every loss is either fixed or logged with an identifiable cause. The result (race real and fixed, or not reproducible with evidence) is written onto this issue and onto jits-a8y.13.

title: DECISION: define what Arena swipe does on mobile (challenge / mutual-intent / discovery)
description:
WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A TASK: web's `/arena/swipe` writes nothing. It is a card stack tallying liked and passed counts in local `useState`, with zero Supabase writes, no persistence, and it is not linked from `/arena`. Its lineage is the abandoned Figma Make prototype at `/Users/msponagle/code/EloRated/Jitsarena` (SwipeMatches.tsx, last commit 2026-01-23, mock data, no Supabase). The user has asked for swipe on mobile, so the behavior has to be DEFINED, not ported. Nothing can be built until this is answered.

OPTION A, SWIPE TO CHALLENGE (recommended). The deck is the "Online now" roster one card at a time. Right swipe opens a confirm sheet ("Challenge <name>?", Send / Cancel) and Send runs the exact same createChallenge handshake as the list. Left swipe passes and suppresses that athlete from your deck for 24h in AsyncStorage, not the database. Card face: avatar, display name, ELO, weight division, gym, record, online dot.
Cost: zero new backend, zero tables, zero RLS. It is a second input modality over a handshake that already exists.
Why the confirm sheet and not send-on-swipe: an accidental right swipe would fire a real challenge at a real person, and cancelChallenge stops working the moment the opponent accepts. An undo toast is not a safe substitute for a social action you cannot fully retract.

OPTION B, SWIPE TO DECLARE INTENT (Tinder-style mutual match). Right swipe records an interest row; when two athletes have both swiped right, the system auto-creates a challenge and notifies both. This is what most people picture, and it is the better long-term product. It is also the expensive one: a new `match_interests` table in jr_be, RLS for it, a mutual-match trigger or RPC, a notification path, and pgTAP coverage. That is explicitly outside this program's "prod, no new backend" constraint and moves work into a second repo.

OPTION C, PURE DISCOVERY. Right swipe opens the athlete profile, left swipe passes, nothing is written, nothing persists. Cheapest, and it ships a surface that does strictly less than the list sitting next to it. Not recommended: it is the current web behavior and the current web behavior is a prototype artifact.

RECOMMENDATION: Option A. Real usable behavior for zero backend work, degrades gracefully (the deck is the online list in another shape), and leaves Option B available later as an additive feature rather than a rewrite. Ship A now; file B as a post-launch candidate.

DELIVERY: decision, no code. Option A and C are OTA-safe. Option B adds jr_be migrations and is a different program.
acceptance_criteria: The user has picked A, B, or C, and the choice is recorded on this issue. If B, a separate jr_be backend epic is filed and this program's swipe issue is deferred behind it.
notes: USER DECISION 2026-09-18: swipe is MUTUAL INTEREST, not swipe-to-challenge. Right swipe records interest silently with no opponent-visible effect. A challenge is created only when BOTH athletes have swiped right on each other. The PM's Option A (right swipe opens a confirm sheet that sends a real challenge) is REJECTED, because can_create_challenge() enforces a hard server-side cap of 3 non-expired pending outgoing challenges in the challenges_insert RLS policy (jr_be 20260204034400 as amended by 20260220200000), so a swipe deck that sends challenges dies on the fourth right swipe. Mutual interest is the only model that respects that cap, since only mutual pairs ever become challenges. USER ALSO APPROVED backend work in jr_be (migrations included), so the match_interests table, RLS, the atomic mutual-detection RPC, and pgTAP coverage are IN SCOPE. The PM note that this is outside a no-new-backend constraint is obsolete. Product split to build to: Arena is the ONLINE instant path (presence gated, no inbox), swipe is the OFFLINE asynchronous path (no presence required, resolves later), so the two do not compete.
close_reason: Decided by user: mutual interest, with jr_be backend work approved. Build detail recorded in notes and carried into jits-ryel.

title: No way to watch it back from the match flow, and a disputed match's video is unreachable
description:
GAP 6. WHY: SummaryStep offers Share Result, Back to Lobby, and Done, and nothing else. The user just recorded a match and cannot watch it from the screen that concludes that match. The ONLY entry to playback is Profile, then Past Match Videos, and that list requires `matches.status = 'completed'`, so a DISPUTED match's video is unreachable entirely. Disputes are exactly when video matters most.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- The match summary offers a "Watch it back" affordance when a video exists for that match, routing to `/video/[id]`.
- When the upload is still in flight, the affordance reflects that rather than 404ing or disappearing.
- A disputed match's video is reachable. Decide where from (the dispute surface is the natural home) and say so; the requirement is that it stops being unreachable.

ORDERING: depends on the wizard decoupling, because the summary step's exit contract changes there and these two edits collide otherwise.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: After a match with a successful upload, the summary screen offers playback and it plays. With an upload still running, the affordance shows the pending state instead of failing. A disputed match's video is reachable from the app without going through Profile. Verified on device on prod.
notes: PARTIALLY COVERED 2026-09-18 by commit 37e52ec on impl-video-p0 (landed alongside jits-od3, since both needed the recorder state above the step boundary). The match summary now offers Watch Match Video routing to /(app)/video/<id> once the upload lands, shows a disabled Video Uploading... state while it is still in flight, and is not gated on outcome or status, so a DISPUTED match's video is reachable from the summary. STILL OPEN: the dispute surface itself (confirm-step / dispute-form) has no playback entry, and the Profile Past Match Videos list still filters on matches.status='completed'. Keep this issue open for those two.

title: Port use-lobby-presence and use-arena-challenge to React Native
description:
WHY: these two hooks are the whole Arena runtime and they are currently web-local: `apps/web/hooks/use-arena-challenge.ts` (238 lines) and `apps/web/hooks/use-lobby-presence.ts`. Neither has a web-specific dependency beyond `next/navigation` and `sonner`. The realtime logic underneath is plain supabase-js, which runs identically on React Native.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- An RN presence hook joining and tracking `lobby:online` with payload {athlete_id, display_name, current_elo}, exposing presenceState for the Online-now split.
- An RN challenge hook covering: create, the filtered incoming subscription on `arena-incoming:${athleteId}`, accept (acceptChallenge then startMatchFromChallenge then BROADCAST match_started on `arena-challenge:${challengeId}` then navigate), decline, cancel, and the synchronous `busyRef` double-tap guard.
- `expo-router` replaces `next/navigation`; the mobile toast replaces `sonner`.
- Channels are torn down on unmount and on sign-out.

CRITICAL PORT HAZARD: mobile presence has a known, already-shipped-and-fixed-once failure mode where a per-mount channel never syncs (issue jits-a8y.1, memory `mobile-qa-sweep-jits-a8y`). The lobby channel must be created once and survive re-render, not be re-created on every mount. Read how the existing mobile presence is wired before writing a second one, and do NOT merge `lobby:online` into the existing app-wide `app:online` channel; they are separate signals.

DECIDE AND STATE IN THE PR whether these live in `apps/mobile/hooks/` or get lifted into `packages/shared`. Shared is tempting but the hooks are now platform-coupled at the navigation and toast layer, so mobile-local with a shared core is the likely right answer. Say which you chose and why.

acceptance_criteria: Both hooks exist in the mobile app and are unit tested against a mocked supabase client: presence join/leave/sync, challenge create, incoming INSERT handling, accept broadcasting match_started before navigating, decline, cancel, and a double-tap that produces exactly one challenge. Channels are verifiably removed on unmount. No per-mount channel re-creation.

title: App backgrounding is entirely unhandled across record and upload, and keep-awake is released too early
description:
GAP 5. WHY: there is NO AppState listener anywhere in the video path. Phones background constantly: a notification, a call, the user checking the time. Today nobody knows what happens to an in-flight recording or an in-flight upload when that occurs, which means it is being discovered by users in the field rather than by us.

Compounding it: keep-awake is held during the live step and RELEASED exactly when the upload starts. So the screen is allowed to sleep during the single longest network operation in the app, which is precisely when it should be held.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- An AppState listener covers the record and upload path. Define and implement the intended behavior for background and foreground in each state (recording, stopping, uploading, retrying), rather than leaving it to chance. At minimum: backgrounding during an upload must not lose the upload, and returning to the foreground must show accurate state, not a stale banner.
- Keep-awake is held THROUGH the upload, not released at its start.
- Whatever the platform genuinely cannot do (for example iOS suspending a foreground-only upload) is handled explicitly and communicated, not ignored.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: On device: background the app mid-recording and return, and the state is correct and communicated. Background mid-upload and return, and the upload either completed or is retryable, never silently gone. The screen does not sleep during an upload. Covered by tests over the AppState transitions.

comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION NOTE, acceptance criterion amended.

The bar ships with THREE tabs (Home, Rankings, Profile) until Arena lands, not four. Arena's slot is a marked insertion point in (tabs)/_layout.tsx.

title: Arena challenge handshake: outgoing, incoming prompt, accept, decline, cancel, match_started broadcast
description:
WHY: this is the loop. Without it Arena is a list of names.

WHAT DONE MEANS, and the ordering here is load-bearing:
- Challenge on an ONLINE row calls createChallenge. The row immediately flips to "Challenge sent" plus Cancel. A synchronous busyRef blocks the double-tap before React state settles.
- The opponent gets a LIVE incoming prompt from the filtered postgres_changes INSERT on `challenges` (channel `arena-incoming:${athleteId}`). Presented as a bottom sheet over the Arena stack: opponent display name, ELO, weight division, Accept and Decline. It self-dismisses if the challenger cancels.
- Accept runs acceptChallenge, then startMatchFromChallenge (idempotent, so a retry is safe), then BROADCASTS `match_started` on `arena-challenge:${challengeId}`, and ONLY THEN navigates. The broadcast is what lands both parties in the match together. Skip it and the challenger sits on the lobby while the opponent is already in the wizard.
- Decline sends declineChallenge; the challenger gets a toast and the row returns to challengeable.
- Cancel sends cancelChallenge; the opponent's prompt disappears.
- Already-challenged rows (in either direction) show a disabled "Pending".
- There is NO inbox. Do not build one. Missed prompts fall back to the existing notification bell, which mobile already renders (usePendingChallenges, notification-item.tsx).

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: Two physical devices on prod: A challenges B, B sees the prompt live without refreshing, B accepts, BOTH devices land in the same match. A cancel removes B's prompt. A decline returns A's row to challengeable with a toast. Rapid double-taps on Challenge produce exactly one challenge row. Accept is safe to retry (no duplicate match). No inbox screen exists.

title: Camera permission is never auto-requested and a denied mic surfaces as a generic recording failure
description:
GAP 7. WHY: permission is never auto-requested. Auto-start requires an ALREADY-granted camera, so a first-run user's match runs against a "Grant Access" placeholder and records nothing. That is the worst possible first experience: the feature silently does not exist for exactly the users who have never used it. Separately, mic permission IS requested but never gated on, so an Android RECORD_AUDIO denial surfaces only as a generic "Recording failed", which is undebuggable for the user and for us.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- Camera permission is requested at a sensible, explained moment before the live step needs it, not discovered as a placeholder mid-match. Follow the established in-context primer pattern rather than a cold system prompt (the FTUE epic jits-r75.1 set that precedent for push).
- Mic permission is gated on, and a denial produces a specific, actionable message naming the microphone, not "Recording failed".
- A user who declines either permission gets a match that still works without video, and is told that is what is happening.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). The permission strings in app.json are unchanged; only the request timing and handling move. If any Info.plist usage string needs new copy, THAT part is a native rebuild and must be called out.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh install records video on its first match without the user having to discover a placeholder. Declining camera gives a clear explanation and a working no-video match. Declining the microphone on Android gives a message that names the microphone. Verified on a freshly installed app, not one with permissions already granted.

title: DECISION: define what Arena swipe does on mobile (challenge / mutual-intent / discovery)
description:
WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A TASK: web's `/arena/swipe` writes nothing. It is a card stack tallying liked and passed counts in local `useState`, with zero Supabase writes, no persistence, and it is not linked from `/arena`. Its lineage is the abandoned Figma Make prototype at `/Users/msponagle/code/EloRated/Jitsarena` (SwipeMatches.tsx, last commit 2026-01-23, mock data, no Supabase). The user has asked for swipe on mobile, so the behavior has to be DEFINED, not ported. Nothing can be built until this is answered.

OPTION A, SWIPE TO CHALLENGE (recommended). The deck is the "Online now" roster one card at a time. Right swipe opens a confirm sheet ("Challenge <name>?", Send / Cancel) and Send runs the exact same createChallenge handshake as the list. Left swipe passes and suppresses that athlete from your deck for 24h in AsyncStorage, not the database. Card face: avatar, display name, ELO, weight division, gym, record, online dot.
Cost: zero new backend, zero tables, zero RLS. It is a second input modality over a handshake that already exists.
Why the confirm sheet and not send-on-swipe: an accidental right swipe would fire a real challenge at a real person, and cancelChallenge stops working the moment the opponent accepts. An undo toast is not a safe substitute for a social action you cannot fully retract.

OPTION B, SWIPE TO DECLARE INTENT (Tinder-style mutual match). Right swipe records an interest row; when two athletes have both swiped right, the system auto-creates a challenge and notifies both. This is what most people picture, and it is the better long-term product. It is also the expensive one: a new `match_interests` table in jr_be, RLS for it, a mutual-match trigger or RPC, a notification path, and pgTAP coverage. That is explicitly outside this program's "prod, no new backend" constraint and moves work into a second repo.

OPTION C, PURE DISCOVERY. Right swipe opens the athlete profile, left swipe passes, nothing is written, nothing persists. Cheapest, and it ships a surface that does strictly less than the list sitting next to it. Not recommended: it is the current web behavior and the current web behavior is a prototype artifact.

RECOMMENDATION: Option A. Real usable behavior for zero backend work, degrades gracefully (the deck is the online list in another shape), and leaves Option B available later as an additive feature rather than a rewrite. Ship A now; file B as a post-launch candidate.

DELIVERY: decision, no code. Option A and C are OTA-safe. Option B adds jr_be migrations and is a different program.

title: Test coverage for the record, upload, watch sequence
description:
WHY: the existing tests cover the two units in the middle and nothing at the seams, which is exactly where every gap in this epic lives. Covered today: `__tests__/lib/video/upload-recording.test.ts` (9 cases), `use-video-recorder.test.ts` (13 cases), `step-router.test.ts`, `ready-step.test.tsx`, plus packages/shared `match-video.test.ts` and `athlete-videos.test.ts`. NOT covered at all: LiveStep, CameraOverlay, UploadProgressBanner, `video/[id].tsx`, PastMatchVideos, the normalized_path-over-storage_path preference in getMatchVideoSignedUrl, and the whole record to upload to watch sequence as one flow. There is no mobile e2e harness.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- Component coverage for LiveStep, CameraOverlay, UploadProgressBanner (all four banner states), `video/[id].tsx` (all error states), and PastMatchVideos.
- A test asserting getMatchVideoSignedUrl prefers `normalized_path` and falls back to `storage_path`. Mobile records MP4 so normalized_path is null and storage_path is signed; that behavior is correct on prod and must not silently invert.
- An integration-level test of the sequence: match ends, recorder stops, upload starts, banner persists across step changes, success, playback reachable.
- Say explicitly whether a mobile e2e harness is worth standing up for this, and file it separately if so. Do not quietly start building one inside this issue.

ORDERING: after the two P0 fixes, so the tests encode the corrected behavior rather than the broken one.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (tests).

title: Mount MatchFlowWizard at a sessionless /match/[matchId] so an Arena match gets recording for free
description:
WHY: this is where Arena and the video work meet, and it is the payoff for doing the wizard decoupling first. Once MatchFlowWizard no longer requires `sessionId`, an Arena match can mount it with an Arena exit, and because the wizard's live step is where the camera lives (`steps/live-step.tsx:67` useVideoRecorder, `:135` CameraOverlay), the Arena match inherits the ENTIRE record, upload, watch pipeline with zero Arena-specific video code. Every fix from the video hardening epic applies to it automatically.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- A route `apps/mobile/app/(app)/match/[matchId].tsx` that loads the match and mounts MatchFlowWizard with `exitHref` pointing back at Arena and `exitLabel` reading "Back to Arena".
- Both parties reach it from the match_started broadcast.
- The wizard derives its initial step from `matches.status` exactly as it does for session matches (`lib/match-flow/step-router.ts`), so a party who backgrounds and returns resumes at the right step.
- A sessionless match completes end to end: ready, live, end, result, confirm, summary, and Done returns to Arena.

ASSUMPTION TO VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING: the exact mobile route shape. This spec proposes `/(app)/match/[matchId]` by analogy with web's `/arena/match/[matchId]` from 5b90ff1. Confirm against the actual mobile routing tree and say in the PR what you chose.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).

title: DECISION: mobile design-direction proposal for user approval (gates all style code)
description:
WHY THIS IS FIRST AND BLOCKING: the user has explicitly said the team owes them a design-direction PROPOSAL for approval BEFORE any style code is written. Writing style code first and asking after is not an option here. Every other issue in this epic is blocked on this one.

WHAT THE PROPOSAL MUST CONTAIN:
- A concrete direction, not a menu of adjectives. Show it: screens rendered in the proposed direction, not a token table.
- What changes and what explicitly does NOT. Dark-first stays. Flat stays (no shadows is an explicit brand rule, not an oversight).
- The typography story, because it is the expensive one. There are ~440 hardcoded `text-[Npx]` classes and only 25 uses of the default scale. Any type refresh either adds a fontSize scale first or pays a ~440 call-site migration. Say which, and what it costs.
- The token story: three hand-mirrored token files (mobile tailwind.config.js, mobile lib/tokens.ts, web design-system/tokens.css) with nothing enforcing sync. Say whether this direction fixes that or lives with it.
- What needs a NATIVE REBUILD versus what ships OTA, in a single explicit list, so the user is approving a delivery plan and not just a look.
- The ELO token family (surface/ink/cta/hairline) is the live system with ~1300 usages; the legacy shadcn family has ~34 left. The proposal should assume the ELO family wins.

DELIVERY: proposal, no code.

title: [epic] Mobile navigation surgery: 4-up tab bar, gym and session discovery on Home, manager entry relocated
description:
WAVE 1b. Runs in parallel with the wizard decoupling (they touch disjoint files).

WHY: the mobile tab bar currently registers five tabs (`apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx`): (home) Home, gyms Gyms, leaderboard Rankings, gym-manager Gym (manager-only), profile Profile. The custom bar (`components/layout/elo-tab-bar.tsx`) is hand-rolled and its own comment claims a 4-up grid, so it is already mis-specified against what it renders. Arena has no slot. Two of the five tabs are gym surfaces, one of which most users never see.

THE CENTRAL CONSTRAINT: this is a RELOCATE, not a DELETE. The gym-manager tab owns seven routes (/gym-manager, /sessions, /roster, /athlete/[id], /stats, /stats-by-elo, /ladder) plus `lib/gym-manager/` (13 files) and `components/gym-manager/` (11 components). Capabilities that exist ONLY there and would be destroyed by deletion: the ELO-ordered gym roster, per-member drill-down, the 30d/90d/all stats dashboard, ELO-bracket stats, the cross-gym ladder, and SessionEditSheet, which is the ONLY edit-an-existing-session UI on mobile. Deleting the routes would silently remove all of it with no replacement. Keep every route alive and reachable.

WHAT MAKES THIS TRACTABLE: nothing outside `gym-manager/` navigates into it. Zero inbound `router.push` or `Link` from anywhere in the app. It is entered solely by tapping the tab. No expo-router typed routes are enabled, so there is no generated route-type file to update (nav calls are cast `as never`). No deep link or push payload targets a gym route: the Android intentFilters register only /athlete and /session. So the surgery is genuinely contained.

THE ONE REAL RISK: session discovery today runs ONLY through the Gyms tab (Gyms, then /gyms/[id], then join session). Home has an active-session card but no way to find a NEW session. Removing the Gyms tab without first putting discovery on Home would strand every user who is not already in a session. That is why the Home work is a hard prerequisite of the tab removal in this graph.

DELIVERY: all children are OTA-safe (EAS Update). The tab bar and every app header are custom JS.

title: Relocate the gym-manager entry point onto /gyms/[id] and keep all 7 manager routes alive
description:
WHY: the manager portal is currently reachable only by tapping the manager-gated tab. That tab is coming out, so the entry point has to exist somewhere else BEFORE it does, or seven routes and two directories of code become unreachable.

WHERE IT GOES: `/gyms/[id]` already has manager affordances (Start Session, SessionTemplates, EditGymSheet) gated on an `isGymManager` flag that comes from `getGymDetail`. That flag is already computed and already correct. Add a "Manage gym" entry to that screen behind the same flag, mirroring web's `/gyms/[id]/manage` link that shipped in 5b90ff1.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- `/gyms/[id]` shows a manager entry point when `isGymManager` is true and nothing when it is false.
- Tapping it lands on `/gym-manager` (the hub) with the gym in context.
- All seven manager routes still resolve: /gym-manager, /gym-manager/sessions, /roster, /athlete/[id], /stats, /stats-by-elo, /ladder.
- No file under `lib/gym-manager/` or `components/gym-manager/` is deleted in this issue.
- SessionEditSheet is still reachable (it is the only way to edit an existing session on mobile).

NOTE, worth a follow-up not a change here: the gym ladder is NOT manager-scoped data (`lib/gym-manager/use-gym-ladder.ts:17` has no manager predicate). It is a general feature stranded behind a manager tab. It should probably surface for everyone on the gym detail screen. File that as a separate issue rather than widening this one.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). JS only.

title: [epic] Arena on mobile: full web parity plus a swipe surface
description:
WAVE 2a. Depends on the wizard decoupling (1a) and the tab slot (1b).

Full spec, including all screen states, the realtime channel contract, the swipe options and the open questions, is in the design notes on this epic and saved at scratchpad/ARENA-MOBILE-SPEC.md.

WHY: mobile has ZERO Arena surface. No route, no tab, no lobby presence, no challenge-issuing path. The only challenge affordance is a DISABLED button on the athlete profile (`apps/mobile/app/(app)/athlete/[id].tsx:127-137`) whose onPress is `toast.info('Challenges coming soon')`. Meanwhile mobile already CONSUMES the other half: `usePendingChallenges` drives the bell badge and `notification-item.tsx` renders challenge_received / accepted / declined. The app can tell you that you were challenged and gives you no way to challenge anyone. Arena closes that loop.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE: the entire data layer is in `packages/shared` and is platform agnostic. `createChallenge` (mutations.ts:28), `acceptChallenge` (:61), `declineChallenge` (:82), `cancelChallenge` (:102), `startMatchFromChallenge` (:122, idempotent), `toggleMatchPreferences` (:755), `getArenaData` (queries.ts:126). NO shared-package change is needed for the data path. The new code is an RN port of two web-local hooks plus the screens.

NAMING WARNING: "Jits Arena" is the RETIRED product name (now ELO RATED, see jits-1ho). The Arena feature has nothing to do with it. Do not let copy, analytics event names, or channel names reintroduce the old brand.

DELIVERY: all children are OTA-safe (EAS Update) as specced. If an implementer needs a gesture or animation package that is not already in apps/mobile/package.json, that flips the classification to native rebuild and must come back to the user first.

title: Arena challenge handshake: outgoing, incoming prompt, accept, decline, cancel, match_started broadcast
description:
WHY: this is the loop. Without it Arena is a list of names.

WHAT DONE MEANS, and the ordering here is load-bearing:
- Challenge on an ONLINE row calls createChallenge. The row immediately flips to "Challenge sent" plus Cancel. A synchronous busyRef blocks the double-tap before React state settles.
- The opponent gets a LIVE incoming prompt from the filtered postgres_changes INSERT on `challenges` (channel `arena-incoming:${athleteId}`). Presented as a bottom sheet over the Arena stack: opponent display name, ELO, weight division, Accept and Decline. It self-dismisses if the challenger cancels.
- Accept runs acceptChallenge, then startMatchFromChallenge (idempotent, so a retry is safe), then BROADCASTS `match_started` on `arena-challenge:${challengeId}`, and ONLY THEN navigates. The broadcast is what lands both parties in the match together. Skip it and the challenger sits on the lobby while the opponent is already in the wizard.
- Decline sends declineChallenge; the challenger gets a toast and the row returns to challengeable.
- Cancel sends cancelChallenge; the opponent's prompt disappears.
- Already-challenged rows (in either direction) show a disabled "Pending".
- There is NO inbox. Do not build one. Missed prompts fall back to the existing notification bell, which mobile already renders (usePendingChallenges, notification-item.tsx).

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).

title: A failed upload is a dead end: persist the recording and offer a manual retry
description:
GAP 4. WHY: today a failed upload gets exactly ONE automatic retry (`lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:178-231`), and then the file URI is discarded along with the hook. No persistence, no queue, no manual retry. The user recorded their match and the footage is gone, with no action available. `lib/network/mutation-queue.ts` exists but covers only result and confirm writes, not video.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- The local recording URI plus the metadata needed to upload it (match id, uploader athlete id, intended storage path) survive the hook unmounting and survive an app restart.
- A failed upload is retryable by the user from the persistent upload banner, and the retry reuses the SAME storage path so a partial or duplicate does not appear.
- Decide and state whether video joins `lib/network/mutation-queue.ts` or gets its own queue. Video is large, file-backed, and has different retry economics from a small JSON mutation, so a separate video queue is probably right; say which you chose and why.
- A recording that can never be uploaded (file gone, match deleted) is cleaned up rather than retried forever.

ORDERING: after the persistent banner, which is where the Retry CTA lives.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).

title: No way to watch it back from the match flow, and a disputed match's video is unreachable
description:
GAP 6. WHY: SummaryStep offers Share Result, Back to Lobby, and Done, and nothing else. The user just recorded a match and cannot watch it from the screen that concludes that match. The ONLY entry to playback is Profile, then Past Match Videos, and that list requires `matches.status = 'completed'`, so a DISPUTED match's video is unreachable entirely. Disputes are exactly when video matters most.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- The match summary offers a "Watch it back" affordance when a video exists for that match, routing to `/video/[id]`.
- When the upload is still in flight, the affordance reflects that rather than 404ing or disappearing.
- A disputed match's video is reachable. Decide where from (the dispute surface is the natural home) and say so; the requirement is that it stops being unreachable.

ORDERING: depends on the wizard decoupling, because the summary step's exit contract changes there and these two edits collide otherwise.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).

title: App backgrounding is entirely unhandled across record and upload, and keep-awake is released too early
description:
GAP 5. WHY: there is NO AppState listener anywhere in the video path. Phones background constantly: a notification, a call, the user checking the time. Today nobody knows what happens to an in-flight recording or an in-flight upload when that occurs, which means it is being discovered by users in the field rather than by us.

Compounding it: keep-awake is held during the live step and RELEASED exactly when the upload starts. So the screen is allowed to sleep during the single longest network operation in the app, which is precisely when it should be held.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- An AppState listener covers the record and upload path. Define and implement the intended behavior for background and foreground in each state (recording, stopping, uploading, retrying), rather than leaving it to chance. At minimum: backgrounding during an upload must not lose the upload, and returning to the foreground must show accurate state, not a stale banner.
- Keep-awake is held THROUGH the upload, not released at its start.
- Whatever the platform genuinely cannot do (for example iOS suspending a foreground-only upload) is handled explicitly and communicated, not ignored.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).

title: Port use-lobby-presence and use-arena-challenge to React Native
description:
WHY: these two hooks are the whole Arena runtime and they are currently web-local: `apps/web/hooks/use-arena-challenge.ts` (238 lines) and `apps/web/hooks/use-lobby-presence.ts`. Neither has a web-specific dependency beyond `next/navigation` and `sonner`. The realtime logic underneath is plain supabase-js, which runs identically on React Native.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- An RN presence hook joining and tracking `lobby:online` with payload {athlete_id, display_name, current_elo}, exposing presenceState for the Online-now split.
- An RN challenge hook covering: create, the filtered incoming subscription on `arena-incoming:${athleteId}`, accept (acceptChallenge then startMatchFromChallenge then BROADCAST match_started on `arena-challenge:${challengeId}` then navigate), decline, cancel, and the synchronous `busyRef` double-tap guard.
- `expo-router` replaces `next/navigation`; the mobile toast replaces `sonner`.
- Channels are torn down on unmount and on sign-out.

CRITICAL PORT HAZARD: mobile presence has a known, already-shipped-and-fixed-once failure mode where a per-mount channel never syncs (issue jits-a8y.1, memory `mobile-qa-sweep-jits-a8y`). The lobby channel must be created once and survive re-render, not be re-created on every mount. Read how the existing mobile presence is wired before writing a second one, and do NOT merge `lobby:online` into the existing app-wide `app:online` channel; they are separate signals.

DECIDE AND STATE IN THE PR whether these live in `apps/mobile/hooks/` or get lifted into `packages/shared`. Shared is tempting but the hooks are now platform-coupled at the navigation and toast layer, so mobile-local with a shared core is the likely right answer. Say which you chose and why.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). supabase-js is already a dependency; no native module.

title: Move gym and session discovery onto the Home dashboard
description:
WHY: this is the hard prerequisite of removing the Gyms tab. Session discovery today runs ONLY through the Gyms tab: Gyms, then /gyms/[id], then join session. Home has an active-session card but NO way to find a NEW session. Pull the Gyms tab without this and a user with no active session has no path to one.

WHAT DONE MEANS: Home gains a discovery surface that covers both jobs the Gyms tab did.
- Find a gym: reach `/gyms` (the list) and `/gyms/[id]` (detail) from Home.
- Find a session: surface joinable sessions directly on Home so the common case ("I want to train now") does not require knowing which gym to open first. At minimum: sessions at the athlete's primary gym. If that is empty, the surface must say so and still offer the gym list rather than rendering nothing.
- The existing active-session card keeps its current behavior and priority. A user already in a session should see that first, not discovery.
- Zero-state: an athlete with no primary gym (free agent) still gets a usable path. See the FTUE epic jits-r75 for the established zero-state copy direction; do not invent a competing empty state.

DO NOT: delete the /gyms routes, change the gym detail screen, or move manager affordances here. Manager relocation is its own issue.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). JS only.

title: Delivery gate: local expo run:ios plus EAS Update only, no cloud build or TestFlight without an explicit go
description:
WHY: this program ships iteratively onto hardware the user already has. EAS cloud builds are slow, cost money, and this repo has a documented history of cloud-build-only failures that do not reproduce locally (see the `eas-cloud-build-env-vars` and `eas-pod-drift-appcheckcore` memories). TestFlight adds an Apple review round trip on top. The user has explicitly withheld approval for both.

WHAT DONE MEANS: a written, followed rule for this program. Every implementer classifies their change before opening a PR. JS-only and asset-only changes go out over EAS Update. Anything that touches the compiled app stops and comes back to the user.

THE RULE:
1. Default to OTA (EAS Update). It reaches already-installed builds in seconds.
2. Verify on device with `npx expo run:ios --device <udid>` (recipe in the `on-device-dev-build-recipe` memory; Matt's iPhone udid 00008120-001E64AE1147401E).
3. STOP and ask the user before any `eas build` or TestFlight submission. A native change silently ships WITHOUT its native half if pushed as an OTA, so misclassification is a data-loss-grade mistake, not a cosmetic one.
4. Never bump `expo.version` for an OTA release: `runtimeVersion.policy` is "appVersion", so a bump orphans the update.

NATIVE-REBUILD TRIGGERS in this codebase: any new native dependency; app.json changes to icon, splash, adaptive icon, notification accent color, userInterfaceStyle, edgeToEdgeEnabled, scheme, bundle id, plugins, or updates config; an Expo SDK bump; a marketing version bump.

DELIVERY: policy issue, no code.

title: Remove both gym tabs and rebuild elo-tab-bar as a true 4-up (Home, Arena, Rankings, Profile)
description:
WHY: Arena needs a tab slot, and two of the five current tabs are gym surfaces (one of them invisible to most users). The custom bar `components/layout/elo-tab-bar.tsx` already has a comment claiming a 4-up grid while rendering five, so the layout is being fought rather than used.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- `apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` registers exactly four Tabs.Screen entries: (home) Home, arena Arena, leaderboard Rankings, profile Profile.
- The `gyms` and `gym-manager` Tabs.Screen entries are removed FROM THE BAR. Their route directories stay on disk and stay reachable (see the relocation issue and the Home discovery issue).
- The manager gating is removed from the tab layout: `useManagedGyms()` at `_layout.tsx:10-11` and the `tabBarButton` at `:46` both go. That hook call becomes dead weight in the layout once the tab is gone, and leaving it there means every app launch still pays for a managed-gyms query to decide the visibility of a tab that no longer exists.
- `elo-tab-bar.tsx` renders a real four-column layout, not a five-item layout squeezed into a grid that claims four. Icons, labels, active state, and safe-area behavior all verified.
- Note the current gating hides rather than unregisters the manager screen (it stays mounted). Removing the Screen entry outright is the correct fix, not another hidden tab.

ORDERING: this lands AFTER the Home discovery surface and AFTER the manager entry relocation. Both are hard blockers in this graph, because shipping this first strands users.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). The tab bar is custom JS.

title: Camera permission is never auto-requested and a denied mic surfaces as a generic recording failure
description:
GAP 7. WHY: permission is never auto-requested. Auto-start requires an ALREADY-granted camera, so a first-run user's match runs against a "Grant Access" placeholder and records nothing. That is the worst possible first experience: the feature silently does not exist for exactly the users who have never used it. Separately, mic permission IS requested but never gated on, so an Android RECORD_AUDIO denial surfaces only as a generic "Recording failed", which is undebuggable for the user and for us.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- Camera permission is requested at a sensible, explained moment before the live step needs it, not discovered as a placeholder mid-match. Follow the established in-context primer pattern rather than a cold system prompt (the FTUE epic jits-r75.1 set that precedent for push).
- Mic permission is gated on, and a denial produces a specific, actionable message naming the microphone, not "Recording failed".
- A user who declines either permission gets a match that still works without video, and is told that is what is happening.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). The permission strings in app.json are unchanged; only the request timing and handling move. If any Info.plist usage string needs new copy, THAT part is a native rebuild and must be called out.

title: Verify stop-then-unmount on real hardware: the stop re-issue loop races CameraView teardown
description:
GAP 11. WHY: the stop path is the last unverified piece of the capture sequence, and if it loses, it loses the whole clip silently.

CONTEXT, READ IT BEFORE TOUCHING CODE: jits-a8y.13 already fixed and CLOSED the logical half of this (pending-stop intent, stop re-issued on a 250ms interval up to 8 attempts over a ~2s window, stale-closure guard via a state ref). But its own closing note carries an explicit caveat: the JS contract was verified against a FAKE camera, and both feared native behaviors have been observed live on hardware (recordAsync rejecting with "Camera is not ready yet" even after onCameraReady, and stopRecording being silently ignored). The remaining exposure is the race between that up-to-2s re-issue loop and React tearing down CameraView in the SAME commit. If recordAsync rejects during teardown, the clip is silently lost.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- Exercise the stop-then-unmount sequence on physical iOS hardware (and Android if available) across: a normal end, an end within the first second of recording, an end during the camera-not-ready retry window, and an end while the app is backgrounding.
- Add instrumentation good enough to tell, from a device log, WHICH branch a lost clip took. The `[video]` log tags already exist and are athlete-id prefixed per device (see the `on-device-dev-build-recipe` memory); extend them rather than inventing a parallel scheme.
- If the race is real, fix it: hold the camera mounted until the record promise settles rather than racing teardown.
- If it is NOT reproducible, say so explicitly and record what was tested, so the next person does not re-litigate it.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update) unless the fix requires a camera-library change, which would be a native rebuild.

title: [bug] video-analyze-chunk 404s 'Chunk not found' for a valid chunk with a valid service-role key (local)
description:
REPRO (local stack, 2026-09-14): a real VP8 WebM was sliced successfully by the worker. The chunk row exists and is readable:

  video_chunks 552296f7-c6a8-4240-8527-2b635cc81027, video dda55b96-490e-4d53-935f-26376caf1228, idx 0, status 'ready'.

Calling the function directly with the SAME service-role JWT the slicer uses returns 404 {"error":"Chunk not found"}:

  curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:54321/functions/v1/video-analyze-chunk -H "Authorization: Bearer <SERVICE_ROLE_KEY from supabase status>" -d '{"chunk_id":"552296f7-..."}'

RULED OUT:
- The chunk does not exist. It does; PostgREST returns it 200 with the EXACT select list loadChunkContext uses (id, video_id, idx, start_s, end_s, duration_seconds, storage_path, file_size_bytes, status).
- The parent video is missing. It exists.
- No match_participants. There are 2, and the exact participants query with the athletes!inner join returns 200 with both rows.
- Missing duration_seconds column. It exists on video_chunks.
- Edge runtime down. It is up (it returns the function's own JSON error body, and 'supabase status' lists only imgproxy/pooler stopped).

SUSPECTED: decodeAuth() (index.ts:321-343) literal-compares the bearer against Deno.env SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY. If the value injected into the edge container differs from the one the slicer sends, isServiceRole is false, the caller falls to the user-JWT branch, userCanSeeVideo() fails, and index.ts:1229 returns the SAME 'Chunk not found' 404 as the missing-chunk branch at :1221. Note this CLI exposes two key formats (legacy JWT SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and new sb_secret_ SECRET_KEY); the sb_secret_ form is rejected at the gateway with 401, so the JWT form is the one in play.

Writing supabase/functions/.env with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY set to the slicer's key and restarting supabase_edge_runtime_jr_be did NOT clear it, so either the .env is not being read or the cause is elsewhere.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the last hop before Gemini. Every video parks at status='analyzing' with chunks 'ready' and no analysis, which is exactly the symptom jits-ayj / jits-kaf.1.6 describe from the other end. It also makes the two 404 branches indistinguishable in the field.

FIX DIRECTION: (1) give the two 404 branches distinct log lines (not distinct response bodies, to preserve the anti-enumeration property) so this is diagnosable at all; (2) log whether isServiceRole resolved true at entry; (3) confirm what SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY actually holds inside the edge container vs what the slicer sends, and pin them from one source.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND + LOCALLY RESOLVED (2026-09-14). Runtime-proven, not inferred.

CAUSE: the local stack has migrated to ASYMMETRIC (ES256) JWT signing keys, but 'supabase status' still prints the LEGACY HS256 key for backwards compatibility. decodeAuth() (video-analyze-chunk/index.ts:335) literal-compares the bearer against the platform-injected SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, so the two never match:

  edge container SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY : len 267, ES256, sha256[:16] ef7488bb8699f119
  npx supabase status SERVICE_ROLE_KEY     : len 164, HS256, sha256[:16] 70541e07fd4f900b
  DB GUC app.settings.service_role_key     : len 267, ES256  (matches the container)

Runtime proof (booleans/lengths only):
  repro   (status HS256): isServiceRole=false, hasUserJwt=true
  control (container ES256): isServiceRole=true

FAILURE CHAIN: isServiceRole=false -> user-JWT branch -> supabaseAdmin.auth.getUser(token) -> GoTrue 403 'bad_jwt: signing method HS256 is invalid' (GOTRUE_JWT_KEYS is now EC) -> userCanSeeVideo() line 397 returns false WITHOUT LOGGING -> index.ts:1229 returns the SAME 'Chunk not found' 404 as the genuine missing-chunk branch at :1221. Indistinguishable from outside, silent in the logs.

RULED OUT with evidence: PostgREST schema-cache staleness (all three loadChunkContext queries return 200 with the container key), video_chunks RLS / is_video_visible (never reached), kong:8000 vs 127.0.0.1 (SUPABASE_URL inside the container is http://kong:8000 and works).

MY EARLIER FIX ATTEMPT WAS A NO-OP: 'supabase start' does NOT read supabase/functions/.env (only 'supabase functions serve --env-file' does). Proof: my file set GEMINI_API_KEY empty yet the container holds a real 39-char key. Real injection is config.toml:387-389 [edge_runtime.secrets] resolved from supabase/.env. I have DELETED supabase/functions/.env as inert and misleading.

VERIFIED END TO END after calling with the container's key: chunk analyzed by gemini-3.6-flash, merge fired, match_videos reached status='analyzed' with chunks_completed=1 and normalized_path set. First time a WebM has traversed the whole pipeline.

PRODUCTION RISK (the important part): the same mechanism exists in prod and is a latent landmine, not a safe config. Correctness depends on THREE independently-managed copies of the key staying byte-identical: the platform-injected value, the GUC set by docs/deploy/video-pipeline-prod-deploy.md:214-215 (consumed by notify_chunk_analyze, migration 20260911000000:351), and the Cloud Run env at docs/deploy/...:402 (consumed by the slicer fan-out, main.js:984-985). It breaks silently with this exact 404 when: (1) the project migrates to the new JWT signing / API key system, which is EXACTLY what just happened locally; (2) an operator pastes sb_secret_... instead of the legacy JWT (locally that 401s loudly at Kong, but PROD's gateway accepts it, so it fails only at the literal compare = silent 404, every video stuck at 'analyzing'); (3) keys are rotated or the paste carries trailing whitespace. Same code in video-merge-analysis/index.ts:263, so merges fail identically.

RECOMMENDED FIX (before deploying): accept a configured SET of internal credentials rather than only the platform-injected key, compared without short-circuit; plus split the two 404 branches by LOG reason (keep the response body identical, the sameness is a deliberate anti-enumeration property); plus stop userCanSeeVideo:397 returning silently; plus a boot log of key length/alg presence.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text:
