FIX IMPLEMENTED (2026-09-14): internal dispatch now authenticates with the SLICER SHARED SECRET, reusing the existing x-slicer-secret pattern (plan.md R-09) rather than the platform service-role key.

CHANGES (jr_be):
- supabase/functions/video-analyze-chunk/index.ts + video-merge-analysis/index.ts: decodeAuth() checks x-slicer-secret against SLICER_SHARED_SECRET (constant-time) BEFORE the Authorization header, so a stale-but-present bearer cannot mask a correctly-configured secret. The service-role compare is retained as a fallback, so this is backwards compatible.
- workers/video-slicer/src/main.js postAnalyze(): sends x-slicer-secret on fan-out. Keeps the bearer + apikey so the request still routes through the gateway.
- migration 20260914010000_internal_dispatch_shared_secret.sql: notify_chunk_analyze() and notify_merge_function() both send x-slicer-secret from app.settings.slicer_secret, and RAISE WARNING when that GUC is empty (previously the dispatch just silently failed downstream).
- supabase/config.toml [edge_runtime.secrets]: SLICER_SHARED_SECRET = env(SLICER_SHARED_SECRET).
- docs/deploy/video-pipeline-prod-deploy.md: new REQUIRED section 3.0 with 'supabase secrets set SLICER_SHARED_SECRET', and a table making the three-byte-identical-copies requirement explicit.

DIAGNOSABILITY (the second half of the fix):
- The two 404 branches keep IDENTICAL response bodies (deliberate anti-enumeration) but now emit distinct logs: {event:chunk_not_found, reason:no_context|not_visible, chunk_id, is_service_role}.
- userCanSeeVideo()'s silent 'return false' now logs {event:user_jwt_unresolved, err}. That single unlogged line is what hid this entire class of failure.
- Boot log emits {event:boot, has_shared_secret, shared_secret_len, service_role_key_len, has_gemini_key} so a credential mismatch is visible at startup instead of as a 404 three hops later.

VERIFIED (local, auth matrix with a fake chunk id so no Gemini spend):
  C) wrong bearer (anon), no secret      -> is_service_role=false
  D) wrong bearer (anon) + CORRECT secret -> is_service_role=true   <- the fix
  E) wrong bearer (anon) + WRONG secret   -> is_service_role=false  <- no bypass
Boot log confirmed has_shared_secret=true, shared_secret_len=67, has_gemini_key=true.

INCIDENTAL CONFIRMATION OF THE ROOT CAUSE: across a single 'supabase stop/start' the container's injected SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY changed from 267 chars (ES256) to 164 chars (HS256). The platform key is demonstrably not a stable credential, which is exactly why internal auth should not depend on it.

NOT YET VERIFIED LOCALLY: the notify_chunk_analyze half of migration 20260914010000. The local supabase_migrations history is out of sync with the actual local schema (history stops at 20260610000000 while later objects exist owned by supabase_admin), so 'supabase migration up --local' fails on ownership and a direct psql apply cannot replace a supabase_admin-owned function. notify_merge_function DID apply and is verified. The migration file itself is CREATE OR REPLACE only and will apply correctly via 'supabase db push', which runs as the migration role. Resolving the local drift needs 'supabase db reset', which would destroy the demo data currently in use.

title: Protect main and development: require PR + review + the four CI checks (currently nothing blocks a direct push to production)
description:
Second prerequisite for granting repo access to anyone who should not be able to ship production.

VERIFIED CURRENT STATE (not inferred):
- gh api repos/Drozes/jits_web/branches/main returns "protected": false, "protection_url": null, and required_status_checks with empty checks/contexts and "enforcement_level": "off".
- All 8 remote branches report protected=false, including development.
- gh api repos/Drozes/jits_web/rulesets returns [].
- No CODEOWNERS anywhere in the repo. No .github/pull_request_template.md. .github/ contains only workflows/ci.yml.
- Both GitHub environments (Preview, Production) have "protection_rules": [] and "deployment_branch_policy": null.
- The repo is PUBLIC with allow_forking: true.

CONSEQUENCES:
1. Anyone with push access can push directly to main, which triggers a Vercel Production deploy with no approval step. PRs are used by convention (30 merged, nearly all into development) but nothing enforces them.
2. CI is advisory only. .github/workflows/ci.yml:3-6 runs on push to main/development and on all pull_request events, with four Node 22 jobs (typecheck, test, build:web, expo export). With zero required status checks, a red CI run blocks nothing. Worse, Vercel builds and promotes independently of GitHub Actions, so a failing CI job does not stop the deploy.
3. The strongest gate in the repo is the local Husky pre-commit hook (.husky/pre-commit: typecheck then test across workspaces). It is bypassable with --no-verify and does not exist at all for anyone editing through the GitHub web UI or a cloud agent.
4. main is 128 commits behind development (git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...origin/development returns 0 128, so main is a strict ancestor with no divergence). Production last deployed 2026-05-06 at main HEAD c151f33. A first accidental push to main would therefore release roughly four months of unreviewed drift in a single deploy.

WORK:
1. Add a ruleset or branch protection on main: require a pull request, require 1 approving review, require the four CI status checks to pass, and disallow force pushes. Branch protection is free on public repos.
2. Apply the same to development, with review requirements set to whatever suits solo work.
3. Add a CODEOWNERS file so review requests route automatically.
4. Decide whether the repo stays public. Preview URLs are posted as commit statuses on public commits, so every preview build of development is currently a publicly reachable site. Check whether Vercel Deployment Protection is enabled; this could not be verified because the Vercel CLI here is unauthenticated.
5. Separately decide whether to fast-forward main to development so production is no longer four months stale. Doing this before adding collaborators makes an accidental promotion far less damaging.

ENV HYGIENE NOTE: .gitignore:36-38 covers .env*.local, .env, and .env.demo. A file named .env.staging matches none of those three patterns and would be committed to a public repo. Consider widening the pattern to .env* before adding collaborators.

title: Stand up a second Supabase project and point Vercel Preview at it (web preview currently writes to live TestFlight data)
description:
Prerequisite for giving anyone outside the dev loop access to a deployed web environment.

CURRENT STATE: there is exactly one hosted Supabase project, rzowigdcdojlovlwwpkx. It is referred to as "staging" in jits-i1n, as "the hosted project" in jits-kaf.1.8, and as "prod" in jits-bxb. Whatever it is called, it holds the live TestFlight user data, so it is the de-facto production database. docs/environment-setup.md:7-11 describes a three-project dev/staging/prod split; that document is aspirational and does not describe reality.

WHY THIS BLOCKS PARTNER ACCESS: Vercel deploys automatically on push via the GitHub App (vercel.json:2-4). main maps to Production, development and every PR map to Preview. apps/web is not read-only: it calls recordMatchResult, confirmMatchResult, disputeMatchResult, createSession, createGym, updateGym, createChallenge, acceptChallenge, joinSessionLobby and createAdminCard/deleteAdminCard through packages/shared/src/api/mutations.ts. So any Preview deployment is a live, publicly reachable site whose writes land in the same rows real TestFlight users are writing to. A non-technical collaborator clicking through their own preview to check a copy change would be mutating production data.

STEP 0 (do this first, it is cheap and it determines the blast radius): open the Vercel dashboard for matthew-sponagles-projects/jits_web and read the Preview environment's NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL. Per-environment variables are dashboard-only and the Vercel CLI on this machine is unauthenticated (vercel whoami returns "No existing credentials found"), so this could not be verified from the repo. If Preview already points somewhere other than rzowigdcdojlovlwwpkx, most of this issue collapses.

WORK:
1. Stand up a second hosted Supabase project to serve as the non-production backend. Apply the jr_be migrations to it.
2. Point Vercel's Preview environment NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY at the new project. Leave Production pointing at the existing one.
3. Seed the new project with enough data that the app is not a wall of empty states: a few gyms, athletes, and a session. See jits-r75.11 for the cold-start seeding shape.
4. Add the elorated:// and preview-URL redirect URLs to the new project's auth allowlist so login works there.
5. Verify by loading a PR preview URL and confirming a write lands in the new project, not rzowigdcdojlovlwwpkx.

RELATED: jits-i1n covers the mobile/EAS half of the same split and should be reconciled with this. jits-by0 covers the deep-link redirect allowlist.

ALSO WORTH FIXING WHILE HERE: the root .env.example is stale and names a variable no code reads (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY); apps/web/.env.example is the accurate one. NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV is documented as required at docs/environment-setup.md:21 but no web source file reads it, and nothing in the web app branches on environment.

title: Rescue stranded jr_be branch feat/frontend-redesign-deps: migration timestamps and test numbers both collide
description:
Repo: jr_be (~/code/EloRated/jr_be). This is repo hygiene, not video pipeline.

The branch `feat/frontend-redesign-deps` in jr_be holds 4 unmerged commits that cannot be merged cleanly as-is. It branched before all of the June work, so both its migration timestamps and its test file numbers collide with what has since landed on `development` and on the hosted project.

What is stranded on the branch (4 commits):
1. kg weight canonicalization
2. `awaiting_timekeeper` status plus the `claim_timekeeper` RPC
3. opponent weight confirmation
4. a test comment fix

Two concrete conflicts:

(a) Migration ordering. The branch's migrations are stamped `20260515000001`, `20260515000002`, `20260515000003`. Those sort EARLIER than migrations already applied to the hosted project (20260516000000 onward), so `supabase db push` will not apply them in order. Supabase will either refuse or apply them out of sequence relative to what production already has.

(b) Test file number collisions. The branch adds:
  - 037_kg_canonicalization
  - 038_awaiting_timekeeper
  - 039_opponent_weight_confirmation
while `development` already has, at the same numbers:
  - 037_athlete_structured_names
  - 038_cancel_session_match
  - 039_gym_owner_portal

Fix shape:
1. Rebase `feat/frontend-redesign-deps` onto `development`.
2. Renumber the three migrations above `20260610000000` so they sort after everything already applied to the hosted project. Pick timestamps that also sort after the newest migration on `development` at rebase time.
3. Renumber the three test files above 043 (the current high-water mark on `development`) to avoid the collision.
4. Re-verify the migrations still apply cleanly in the new order, in particular that the kg canonicalization does not conflict with any weight-related change that landed on `development` in the meantime.
acceptance_criteria: feat/frontend-redesign-deps merges to development in jr_be with a green supabase db reset + supabase test db. Its three migrations are renumbered above 20260610000000 so they sort after everything already applied to the hosted project, and its three test files are renumbered above 043 so they no longer collide with 037_athlete_structured_names / 038_cancel_session_match / 039_gym_owner_portal. All four commits' functionality (kg weight canonicalization, awaiting_timekeeper + claim_timekeeper, opponent weight confirmation, test comment fix) survives the rebase.

title: jr_be pgTAP suite is not idempotent: hardcoded founder email gives a false red on a non-fresh DB
description:
Repo: jr_be (~/code/EloRated/jr_be). This is repo hygiene, not video pipeline.

The pgTAP suite is not idempotent. Running `supabase test db` against a database that already has data produces a false red, because one test hardcodes a real founder email and dies on a unique-constraint violation, and two other files then fail on founder-count assumptions.

Evidence:
- `supabase/tests/041_founder_allowlist_test.sql:178` inserts the hardcoded real founder email `matthew.spon@gmail.com` directly into `auth.users`. If that user already exists (which it does on any stack that has been used), the insert dies on `users_email_partial_key` and the whole file aborts.
- Cascading failures once 041 has run (or aborted) against non-fresh data:
  - `supabase/tests/014_weight_aware_elo_test.sql`, test 36
  - `supabase/tests/040_admin_platform_roles_test.sql`, tests 28 and 35
  Both depend on founder-count assumptions that leftover rows invalidate.

Verified 2026-07-24:
- `supabase test db` on a stack with leftover data: 4 failures across 3 files.
- After `supabase db reset`, then `supabase test db`: 43 files / 1329 tests, all pass.

Impact: anyone who runs the quality gate without resetting first gets a false red, which trains people to ignore the gate. It also means the gate cannot be run twice in a row, and cannot be run against a shared or long-lived dev database.

Fix shape:
- Make `supabase/tests/041_founder_allowlist_test.sql` generate a unique per-run email (for example a `gen_random_uuid()`-derived local part) instead of hardcoding `matthew.spon@gmail.com`, or have it clean up the row it inserts so a second run starts from the same state. If the test genuinely needs to assert behavior for the specific hardcoded allowlist address, it should assert against the allowlist configuration rather than by inserting that user.
- Re-check the founder-count assertions in `supabase/tests/014_weight_aware_elo_test.sql` (test 36) and `supabase/tests/040_admin_platform_roles_test.sql` (tests 28, 35) so they scope to rows the test itself created rather than to a global count.
acceptance_criteria: supabase test db passes twice in a row in jr_be without an intervening supabase db reset. 041_founder_allowlist_test.sql no longer inserts a hardcoded real email into auth.users (or cleans it up), and the founder-count assertions in 014_weight_aware_elo_test.sql test 36 and 040_admin_platform_roles_test.sql tests 28 and 35 are scoped so leftover rows cannot break them. Baseline to preserve: 43 files / 1329 tests passing after a fresh reset.

title: No migration sets the four pipeline GUCs, and all four fail silently (push notifications dead too)
description:
All code cited lives in the jr_be repo (~/code/EloRated/jr_be) unless noted.

No migration anywhere sets the four GUCs the video pipeline depends on, and all four fail silently when unset. Two of them no-op with only a RAISE WARNING, and two coalesce to the empty string and produce a silent 401/404.

The four required GUCs and where they are read:
- `app.settings.video_slicer_url`, read at `supabase/migrations/20260507000000_video_slicer_webhook.sql:45`
- `app.settings.slicer_secret`, read at `supabase/migrations/20260507000000_video_slicer_webhook.sql:55`
- `app.settings.merge_function_url`, read at `supabase/migrations/20260502000000_video_chunks.sql:365`
- `app.settings.service_role_key`, read at `supabase/migrations/20260502000000_video_chunks.sql:372`

Evidence:
- Grep confirms zero `ALTER DATABASE ... SET` statements anywhere under `supabase/migrations`. Nothing in the repo ever sets these values, so a `supabase db reset` or a fresh project starts with all four unset.
- Verified unset on the hosted project `rzowigdcdojlovlwwpkx` on 2026-07-24, alongside zero `match_videos` rows for all time. The pipeline has never run there.
- Failure behavior: the slicer-dispatch GUCs no-op with only a RAISE WARNING (invisible unless someone is tailing Postgres logs); the merge/service-role GUCs coalesce to `''` and produce silent 401/404 responses from the edge functions.

Related blast radius beyond video: `app.settings.edge_function_url` and `app.settings.service_role_key` being unset also means `notify_push_function()` falls back to the local-dev URL `http://host.docker.internal:54321/functions/v1/push`, see `supabase/migrations/20260307000000_fix_pg_net_extension.sql:16-19`. On the hosted project that host does not resolve, so PUSH NOTIFICATIONS are silently dead there too. The only pg_net response ever recorded on that project is "Couldn't resolve host name".

Fix shape:
1. Document and script the GUC wiring per environment (local, staging, prod), including where the values live (dashboard vs infra script vs sealed secret) so they survive a `db reset` and a new environment bring-up. Note this overlaps with jits-kaf.1.1 item 2, which asked for the `video_slicer_url` GUC to be set; this issue is the broader "all four plus push, and detect when they are missing" problem.
2. Add a health-check RPC (or a startup assertion) that reports which pipeline GUCs are unset, so a misconfigured environment is loud instead of silent. It must cover at minimum: `app.settings.video_slicer_url`, `app.settings.slicer_secret`, `app.settings.merge_function_url`, `app.settings.service_role_key`, `app.settings.edge_function_url`.
3. Consider promoting the current RAISE WARNING paths to something surfaced in-band (a row in an ops table, or a non-2xx from the dispatch path) so operators do not have to read Postgres logs to notice.
Add pgTAP coverage for the health-check RPC.
acceptance_criteria: An environment missing any pipeline GUC is detectable without reading Postgres logs: a health-check RPC (or equivalent startup assertion) reports the unset state of app.settings.video_slicer_url, app.settings.slicer_secret, app.settings.merge_function_url, app.settings.service_role_key, and app.settings.edge_function_url. Running it against the hosted project rzowigdcdojlovlwwpkx today reports all of them missing. The per-environment GUC wiring is documented and scripted so it survives a supabase db reset and a fresh environment bring-up. pgTAP covers the health-check RPC. Full gate green: supabase db reset + supabase test db.

title: RUNBOOK deploy command would 403 every slice request: --no-allow-unauthenticated vs pg_net shared-secret auth
description:
All code cited lives in the jr_be repo (~/code/EloRated/jr_be) unless noted.

The RUNBOOK's documented Cloud Run deploy command would make every pg_net slice request fail with a silent 403, and the RUNBOOK explicitly (and incorrectly) states that this is safe.

Evidence:
- `workers/video-slicer/RUNBOOK.md:119` deploys the service with `--no-allow-unauthenticated`.
- `workers/video-slicer/RUNBOOK.md:136-138` justifies it:
  "`--no-allow-unauthenticated`: the public endpoint is closed. Auth is via the `x-slicer-secret` header, which Supabase pg_net injects from the GUC configured below. The dispatch path does NOT use Cloud Run IAM."
- That last sentence is wrong. `--no-allow-unauthenticated` makes Cloud Run's front end require a Google-signed OIDC bearer token before the request is ever routed to the container. The shared-secret header is checked by our own code inside the container, which the request never reaches.
- The only headers pg_net sends are Content-Type and x-slicer-secret: `supabase/migrations/20260507000000_video_slicer_webhook.sql:65-68`. There is no Authorization header and no OIDC token.
- Failure mode is maximally quiet: Cloud Run returns 403 at the edge, so nothing is logged in the container, and pg_net's response is not surfaced anywhere in Postgres that anyone watches. Videos would simply never get sliced with no error anywhere obvious.

Fix shape (pick one and make the RUNBOOK match reality either way):
1. Deploy with `--allow-unauthenticated`, which is the intended v1 model where `x-slicer-secret` is the sole authenticator, and update `workers/video-slicer/RUNBOOK.md:119` plus the justification at `RUNBOOK.md:136-138`; or
2. Keep `--no-allow-unauthenticated` and add a Google-signed OIDC token to the pg_net call at `supabase/migrations/20260507000000_video_slicer_webhook.sql:65-68` (new migration; requires minting/refreshing an identity token from Postgres, which is nontrivial), then document the service-account and IAM binding steps in the RUNBOOK.

Option 1 is the smaller change and matches the shared-secret design already implemented. If option 1 is chosen, state explicitly in the RUNBOOK that the endpoint is publicly reachable and that `x-slicer-secret` plus `--max-instances` is the entire defense.
acceptance_criteria: Following workers/video-slicer/RUNBOOK.md verbatim produces a Cloud Run service that pg_net can actually reach: a slice dispatch from Postgres reaches the container and is authenticated by x-slicer-secret (positive case 2xx, wrong/missing secret rejected). The RUNBOOK no longer claims 'The dispatch path does NOT use Cloud Run IAM' while also using --no-allow-unauthenticated; whichever option is chosen, the deploy flags and the auth explanation at RUNBOOK.md:119 and RUNBOOK.md:136-138 agree with each other and with reality.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text:
RESOLVED IN CODE (verified 2026-09-14 by git archaeology). Recommend closing.

Timeline:
- 720f483 wrote the original RUNBOOK with '--no-allow-unauthenticated' and the note 'the public endpoint is closed'.
- This bead was filed 2026-07-24 against that text. Correct at the time.
- f0f0ced (2026-09-11, 'fix(slicer): webm re-encode, incremental chunk upload, capacity and failure reasons') flipped it to '--allow-unauthenticated' and rewrote the rationale to the accurate one: pg_net sends plain HTTPS with static headers and cannot mint Google ID tokens, so Cloud Run IAM would reject every dispatch before the worker saw it; auth for this hop is the worker's constant-time x-slicer-secret check, and unauthenticated probes get a 404 so the endpoint does not advertise itself.

grep for 'no-allow-unauthenticated' in workers/video-slicer/RUNBOOK.md now returns nothing. Following the RUNBOOK today produces a working service.

PROCESS NOTE worth acting on: f0f0ced also added the webm re-encode codec gate (decideEncodeMode + MP4_COPY_SAFE_VIDEO_CODECS), which invalidated the central premise of jits-kaf.1.2 at the same time. One commit three days ago made TWO open beads stale and neither was updated, which caused a downstream audit to confidently report a VP8 copy-path failure that the code no longer has. Worth a convention that slicer commits touching the encode path or the RUNBOOK sweep the jits-kaf.1.* children.

title: No retry for a failed chunk: one bad chunk hangs the video at 'analyzing' forever
description:
All code cited lives in the jr_be repo (~/code/EloRated/jr_be) unless noted.

There is no retry path for a chunk whose analysis failed. A single failed chunk hangs the whole video at 'analyzing' forever, even though every piece needed to retry already exists. There is simply no caller.

Evidence:
- The merger hard-requires every chunk to be completed: `supabase/functions/video-merge-analysis/index.ts:1042-1052` returns HTTP 409 when they are not.
- `finalize_pending_merges` requires `chunks_completed = chunk_count` before it will finalize: `supabase/migrations/20260502000000_video_chunks.sql:540`.
- The reaper flips stuck chunks from 'analyzing' to 'failed': `supabase/migrations/20260502000000_video_chunks.sql:488-492`. That is where the chunk stops. Nothing ever re-POSTs it to `video-analyze-chunk`.
- The retry capability is already implemented and unused:
  - `claimChunk` in `supabase/functions/video-analyze-chunk/index.ts:478-491` explicitly accepts a chunk in status 'failed' as claimable.
  - The DB-level guard permits the `failed -> analyzing` transition: `supabase/migrations/20260502000000_video_chunks.sql:287`.
- Net effect: `chunks_completed` can never reach `chunk_count`, `finalize_pending_merges` never fires, the merge never runs, and the video parks at 'analyzing' with no operator-visible signal.

Fix shape: add a pg_cron sweep (new migration, alongside the existing `reap-stuck-analyzing-chunks` / `finalize-pending-merges` / `request-pending-video-slices` jobs) that finds chunks in status 'failed' belonging to videos still in `status = 'analyzing'` and re-POSTs them to `video-analyze-chunk` via pg_net. Requirements:
- Bound the retries with an attempt counter / max-attempts so a permanently-bad chunk does not loop forever; on exhaustion, move the video to a terminal failed state that is visible to the client rather than leaving it at 'analyzing'.
- Respect the existing `failed -> analyzing` guard at `supabase/migrations/20260502000000_video_chunks.sql:287` rather than bypassing it.
- Note the dependency on the GUC wiring: the sweep needs `app.settings.service_role_key` and the chunk-analyzer function URL to be set, which is its own open bug in this cluster.
Add pgTAP coverage under `supabase/tests/` for the retry sweep and for the max-attempts terminal path.
acceptance_criteria: A video with exactly one chunk in status='failed' recovers to status='analyzed' with no manual intervention: the new sweep re-dispatches the failed chunk, video-analyze-chunk re-claims it, chunks_completed reaches chunk_count, finalize_pending_merges fires, and the merge runs. A chunk that fails repeatedly stops after the configured max attempts and moves the video to a terminal, client-visible failed state instead of parking at 'analyzing'. Both paths covered by pgTAP. Full gate green: supabase db reset + supabase test db.

title: match_videos status='slicing' is a state-machine dead end: no recovery path, stale-claim logic is dead code
description:
All code cited lives in the jr_be repo (~/code/EloRated/jr_be) unless noted.

`match_videos.status = 'slicing'` is a state-machine dead end: nothing can ever recover a row that is left there, so any Cloud Run OOM, scale-in, or deadline-exit during slicing strands the video permanently.

Evidence:
- `workers/video-slicer/src/main.js:834-845` flips `match_videos.status` to 'slicing' immediately after claiming the row.
- Both recovery paths filter on `status = 'ready'` and therefore skip 'slicing' rows:
  - The cron sweep query at `supabase/migrations/20260512000000_fix_slicer_grace_window.sql:62`:
    ```
    SELECT id
      FROM public.match_videos
     WHERE status = 'ready'
       AND chunk_count IS NULL
    ```
  - `claim_video_for_slicing` at `supabase/migrations/20260510000000_claim_match_video_rpcs.sql:69`:
    ```
     WHERE mv.id = p_video_id
       AND mv.status = 'ready'
       AND mv.chunk_count IS NULL
       AND (mv.slice_started_at IS NULL ...
    ```
- Consequence: the 30-minute stale-claim recovery described in the comment at `workers/video-slicer/src/main.js:596-602` is dead code. The `slice_started_at` staleness check it relies on can never be reached, because the row's status has already moved off 'ready' and both queries filter it out before the staleness predicate is evaluated.

Fix shape: relax both filters to `status IN ('ready','slicing')`, gated on the existing `slice_started_at` staleness check so an actively-slicing row is not stolen from a healthy worker. Specifically:
- `supabase/migrations/20260512000000_fix_slicer_grace_window.sql:62`, widen the sweep's status predicate; keep the existing trigger-race grace window for 'ready' rows and require a stale `slice_started_at` for 'slicing' rows.
- `supabase/migrations/20260510000000_claim_match_video_rpcs.sql:69`, widen `claim_video_for_slicing`'s predicate the same way, so the re-dispatched request can actually re-claim the row.
Do this in a NEW migration (do not edit applied migrations in place). Add pgTAP coverage under `supabase/tests/`.
acceptance_criteria: A video stranded in status='slicing' with a stale slice_started_at (older than the existing 30-minute window) is picked up by the request-pending-video-slices cron sweep, re-dispatched, successfully re-claimed by claim_video_for_slicing, and completes slicing. A video in 'slicing' with a FRESH slice_started_at is NOT stolen from the healthy worker holding it. Both behaviors covered by pgTAP. Changes ship as a new migration, not an edit to an applied one. Full gate green: supabase db reset + supabase test db.

title: Abandoned matches stay in_progress forever: no resume, timeout, or cleanup
description:
Proven live during the 2026-06-10 on-device video test: force-quitting or restarting the app mid-match strands the match at status='in_progress' with session_participants.current_match_id still set. There is no in-app re-entry surface (home match-tap is a 'coming soon' toast), no abandon/cancel path from the wizard, and no server-side timeout sweep, so stale 'running' matches accumulate and look active in lobby/home UIs. Hit 3 times in one ~30-minute test session (matches b7ad3126, 73dad1f3, 135bb274; manually deleted via psql).

Fix directions (decide in implementation): (a) mid-match resume: on app launch, if the athlete has a current_match_id pointing at an in_progress match, deep-link back into the wizard step derived from match state (step-router already derives step from DB status); (b) BE sweep: pg_cron job that auto-cancels in_progress matches with no activity past scheduled duration + grace (needs a cancel path that clears current_match_id and does NOT award ELO); (c) lobby UX: show the stranded match with a Resume / Abandon choice instead of blocking new matches. Related baseline gap: 'No mid-match resume after crash/force-quit' (research/015, Match Flow gap 3).
acceptance_criteria: Force-quit mid-match then relaunch: the user can resume the match or abandon it from the UI; abandoned matches transition to a terminal status (no ELO) and clear current_match_id; no in_progress match older than its duration + grace survives the BE sweep. Covered by pgTAP for the sweep + a mobile test for the resume path.

title: Slicer worker: analyze fan-out counts HTTP failures as successes; videos park forever at 'analyzing'
description:
Found during the local e2e pipeline verification (2026-06-10, PASS overall). Two coupled defects in jr_be workers/video-slicer/src/main.js:

1. postAnalyze() resolves resp.ok instead of throwing on non-2xx, and fanOutAnalyze() counts any fulfilled promise as success. Observed live: every POST to /functions/v1/video-analyze-chunk returned 503, yet the worker logged analyze_succeeded:1 analyze_failed:0 and replied 200, so the intended total-failure -> 500 -> pg_net-retry path (~line 969) can never fire for HTTP-level failures (only network throws/timeouts).

2. Missing recovery + stale comment: ~lines 962-968 claim a retried /slice re-fans-out, but the chunk_count fast-path (~line 776) returns {skipped:true} WITHOUT re-dispatch (verified live). Combined with (1), a video whose chunk-analyze dispatches all fail parks forever at status='analyzing' with chunks at 'ready': the request-pending-video-slices cron only re-POSTs ready+unsliced videos, and the reaper only flips chunks stuck in 'analyzing'.

Fix shape: make postAnalyze throw on non-2xx (or count resp.ok properly), and either make the already-sliced fast-path re-fan-out chunks still at 'ready', or add a cron sweep for analyzing-videos-with-ready-chunks. Repro recipe + logs: /tmp/video-slicer-run-20260610.log, agent report in session.
acceptance_criteria: A video whose analyze dispatches all fail (edge runtime down) does not park silently: either the /slice response is non-2xx so pg_net retries, or a sweep re-dispatches ready chunks for analyzing videos. Worker success/failure counts reflect HTTP status. pgTAP/worker test covers the all-503 case.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: PARTIALLY FIXED 2026-07-24 in jr_be commit 00614ad. Defect (1) is fixed: fanOutAnalyze now counts a fulfilled-but-false promise as a failure (workers/video-slicer/src/main.js), so an all-failure fan-out correctly reports succeeded:0 and returns 500 instead of a false 200. Verified live during an end-to-end local run: the worker reported 'succeeded:0 failed:2' on a real Gemini failure where the old code would have logged success. Defect (2) is STILL OPEN: the chunk_count fast-path still returns {skipped:true} without re-dispatching chunks left at 'ready', so there is still no recovery sweep for an analyzing-video-with-ready-chunks. Keep this issue open for that half (see also jits-kaf.1.6 for the failed-chunk retry sweep).

title: Mobile: community review screen (playback, AI analysis, timestamped comments, manual tagging)
description:
The heart of the community section: watch a published video and coach on it (repo jits_web, apps/mobile).

1. Reuses the Phase 2 player (jits-kaf.2.2) and analysis viewer (jits-kaf.2.3) for videos the viewer is NOT a participant of (RLS makes this just-work after publish; remove any client-side participant assumptions).
2. Comments thread via shared getVideoComments/addVideoComment (jits-kaf.3.5): list ordered chronologically, each timestamped comment shows mm:ss (font-mono) and tapping it seeks the player; composer with an 'attach current time' toggle (on by default when video is playing); delete own comments.
3. Manual technique tagging: 'Tag technique' action capturing current playback time + technique selection, via shared addManualTechniqueTag; manual tags render in the same timeline as AI tags, visually distinguished (e.g. outline vs filled), delete own.
4. Empty/edge states: video unpublished mid-view (RLS read starts failing → graceful 'no longer shared' state), no comments yet, unanalyzed video (badge absent, timeline shows manual tags only).
5. Likely the largest Phase 3 slice; split components aggressively (<80 lines), orchestrating screen <200.

JS-only → OTA-eligible.
acceptance_criteria: A non-participant active athlete can watch a published video, read its AI analysis, add/see/delete timestamped comments that seek on tap, and add/delete manual technique tags inline with the AI timeline. Quality gate green.

title: Mobile: community video feed screen (browse published videos)
description:
The browse surface for published videos (repo jits_web, apps/mobile).

1. New screen/section (placement judgment: a 'Community' entry; likely pushed from Home or a segment on an existing tab; bottom nav is locked at 4 tabs Home/Gyms/Rankings/Profile, do NOT add a 5th without product sign-off; propose placement in the PR).
2. Paginated list via shared getCommunityVideos (jits-kaf.3.5): infinite scroll with the keyset cursor, pull-to-refresh, empty state ('No community videos yet').
3. Row/card: uploader display name + avatar initials, relative publish date (formatRelativeDate), duration (font-mono tabular-nums), analysis badge when has_analysis, comment count.
4. Tap → community review screen (jits-kaf.3.8).
5. Fetch hook apps/mobile/lib/video/use-community-feed.ts with cancelled-ref pattern. Design rules: no decorative color, sharp corners, screens under ~200 lines.

JS-only → OTA-eligible.
acceptance_criteria: Active athlete can scroll the full published feed newest-first with working pagination, refresh, and empty state; rows show badge/count metadata correctly. Quality gate green.

title: Mobile: opt-in publish flow on own videos
description:
The uploader-facing half of the opt-in model (repo jits_web, apps/mobile).

1. On the playback screen (jits-kaf.2.2) for videos the athlete UPLOADED: a 'Share to community' affordance showing current state (private by default / published with date).
2. Publishing requires an explicit confirm dialog stating exactly who will see it ('Anyone on ELO RATED will be able to watch and comment'); default stays private; no pre-checked boxes, no publish-by-default.
3. Unpublish from the same surface, also confirmed (mention existing comments stop being visible to the community since visibility mirrors the video).
4. Wire via shared publishMatchVideo (jits-kaf.3.5); optimistic UI with rollback on Result error.
5. Only the uploader sees the control (uploaded_by === own athlete id); the other participant sees published-state as read-only metadata.

JS-only → OTA-eligible if the Phase 2 build is in the field.
acceptance_criteria: Uploader can publish and unpublish with explicit confirmation; non-uploader participant cannot; state survives reload; errors surface via mapped DomainError toasts. Quality gate green.

title: Shared layer slice for community review: publish mutation, feed query, comments CRUD, manual tag mutation
description:
The @jits/shared slice both apps consume for Phase 3 (repo jits_web, packages/shared; follows the Phase 2 wrapper conventions from jits-kaf.2.1).

1. Mutations (Result<T>, mapPostgrestError/mapRpcError): publishMatchVideo(videoId, publish: boolean) (RPC or guarded UPDATE per jits-kaf.3.1 outcome); addVideoComment({videoId, timestampSeconds?, body}); deleteVideoComment(commentId); addManualTechniqueTag(...); deleteManualTechniqueTag(...).
2. Queries: getCommunityVideos({limit, before}) wrapping get_community_videos with keyset cursor; getVideoComments(videoId) (direct select under RLS, ordered for thread + timeline use).
3. Types for the feed row + comment exported from shared; unit tests per match-video.test.ts pattern.
4. If a realtime comments channel is wanted later, note it; NOT in scope now (refresh-on-focus is fine at beta).

Blocked by the three BE issues (needs regenerated database.ts).
acceptance_criteria: All Phase 3 reads/writes go through typed shared wrappers returning Result<T>; zero raw .from()/.rpc() in app code; unit tests + typecheck green.

title: BE: community feed RPC get_community_videos (paginated, newest-first, published-only)
description:
The browse query for the community section (repo jr_be; one RPC + pgTAP).

SPEC (decided): published is ENOUGH for inclusion; do not require status='analyzed'. Analysis is an optional badge, so a freshly-published still-analyzing video appears immediately and gains the badge later.

RPC get_community_videos(p_limit int default 20, p_before timestamptz default NULL) SECURITY DEFINER (or SECURITY INVOKER relying on the new published SELECT policy; implementer picks; DEFINER matches the existing get_* video RPC family and lets the function enforce 'caller is an active athlete' once, explicitly):
- Keyset pagination: WHERE published_at < p_before ORDER BY published_at DESC LIMIT p_limit (uses the partial index from jits-kaf.3.1). No OFFSET.
- Returns per row: video_id, match_id, storage_path, duration_seconds, published_at, uploader (athlete id + display_name via fk join), both participants' display names if exposable, has_analysis boolean (EXISTS video_analyses row / status='analyzed'), comment_count (COUNT video_comments; cheap enough at beta scale, no denormalized counter).
- Guard: raise/return empty for non-active callers.
- Exclude status IN ('failed','deleted') rows even if published.

pgTAP: ordering, keyset boundary, active-athlete guard, unpublished exclusion, badge correctness.

After migration: npm run db:types in jits_web.
acceptance_criteria: RPC returns correct pages newest-first with stable keyset behavior; unpublished/failed/deleted never appear; has_analysis and comment_count accurate; pgTAP green; types regenerated.

title: BE migration: video_comments table (timestamped human comments) + RLS
description:
New table for human coaching comments on videos, timestamped into the footage (one migration set + pgTAP, repo jr_be).

TABLE SHAPE (spec'd):
video_comments (
  id uuid PK default gen_random_uuid(),
  video_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES match_videos(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  author_athlete_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES athletes(id),
  timestamp_seconds numeric NULL CHECK (timestamp_seconds >= 0),  -- NULL = general comment on the whole video
  body text NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(body) BETWEEN 1 AND 2000),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
)
Index: (video_id, created_at) for the per-video thread; consider (video_id, timestamp_seconds) for timeline rendering.

RLS:
- SELECT: visibility mirrors the video; author, match participants, or (video published AND requester is an active athlete). Reuse/extract the published-visibility predicate from the publish migration (jits-kaf.3.1) as a helper (e.g. can_view_match_video(video_id)) so the two policies cannot drift.
- INSERT: active athletes who can view the video; author_athlete_id must be the caller's own athlete row (WITH CHECK).
- DELETE: author only (no moderation tooling yet; uploader-moderation is future scope, note it, don't build it).
- UPDATE: none for now (no edit; delete + repost). Keep it simple.

No comment-count denormalization, no threading, no reactions; out of scope.

After migration: npm run db:types in jits_web.
acceptance_criteria: pgTAP: participant comments work pre-publish; non-participant blocked until publish; insert forging author_athlete_id rejected; delete restricted to author; cascade on video delete. Types regenerated.

title: BE migration: opt-in publish model (published_at on match_videos, community/storage RLS, publish UPDATE policy)
description:
Implement the decided opt-in visibility model in jr_be (one migration set + pgTAP).

DESIGN (spec'd here, implementer follows):
1. Column: ALTER TABLE match_videos ADD COLUMN published_at timestamptz NULL. CHOICE RATIONALE (published_at over a visibility enum): the model has exactly two states (private/published) so a nullable timestamp encodes it without enum-migration churn, doubles as the feed sort key (newest-first pagination needs it anyway), and records WHEN it was shared for moderation/audit. If a third state (e.g. unlisted, gym-only) ever appears, migrate to an enum then; do not pre-build it.
2. Partial index for the feed: CREATE INDEX ... ON match_videos (published_at DESC) WHERE published_at IS NOT NULL.
3. New SELECT policy alongside the existing match_videos_select_participant: published rows readable by any ACTIVE athlete (EXISTS athlete row for auth.uid() with status='active', published_at IS NOT NULL; consider status='analyzed' OR 'ready' guard so mid-pipeline rows don't leak). Participants keep full visibility regardless.
4. Publish/unpublish: UPDATE policy letting ONLY the uploader (uploaded_by = own athlete id) set/clear published_at, and ONLY that column; enforce column-restriction via trigger guard (house pattern: guard_athlete_columns) or a dedicated RPC publish_match_video(p_video_id, p_publish boolean) SECURITY DEFINER; implementer picks, RPC preferred for symmetry with existing video RPCs and easier column-guarding.
5. storage.objects: extend match-videos bucket read policy so authenticated active athletes can createSignedUrl/read objects whose match_videos row is published (path matches matches/{match_id}/%). Today reads are participant-only; without this the feed shows rows nobody can play. Depends on the bucket-in-migration fix (jits-kaf.1.1).
6. Widen get_video_analysis (and get_match_videos if visibility-checked internally) so analysis of a PUBLISHED video is readable by active athletes, not just participants; community review surfaces the AI analysis.
7. pgTAP: participant-only when unpublished; active-athlete read when published; pending/inactive athletes denied; non-uploader cannot publish; uploader cannot modify other columns through the publish path; storage policy honored.

After migration: npm run db:types in jits_web.
acceptance_criteria: pgTAP proves the matrix above. A published video row + storage object + analysis are readable by an unrelated active athlete; unpublishing revokes all three. Types regenerated.

title: Phase 2 TestFlight release: one build carrying expo-video + expo-media-library + expo-sharing
description:
Phase 2 adds three native modules and iOS permission strings; none of it can ride an OTA (an OTA would silently ship JS that calls native APIs the installed binary lacks → runtime crash).

Work (repo: jits_web, apps/mobile):
1. After jits-kaf.2.2/.2.3/.2.4 pass review + the full quality gate, run the testflight-release skill (eas build -p ios --profile production --auto-submit). Single build for all three deps; do NOT ship them across separate builds.
2. Pre-build gate: cd apps/mobile && npx expo export --platform ios --no-bytecode (native-module/metro resolution check), plus typecheck + test.
3. Verify EAS env vars resolve (see eas-cloud-build-env-vars memory; .env is not uploaded to EAS).
4. Post-build: smoke-test on TestFlight (playback, analysis, download permission flow). Subsequent Phase 2/3 JS tweaks can then ride OTA against this new build's runtime.

This issue is the ship-gate for the phase; it depends on every other Phase 2 child.
acceptance_criteria: TestFlight build containing the three native deps is live and smoke-tested: a participant device can play, view analysis, and save a video. Build/version notes recorded in CHANGELOG.md.
notes: Build itself SHIPPED early (2026-07-24): v0.2.0 build 21 submitted to TestFlight carrying expo-video + expo-media-library + expo-sharing + expo-video-thumbnails; runtime forked to 0.2.0 (AppCheckCore pinned 11.2.0 via expo-build-properties after build 20 pod-drift failure). Issue stays open only until siblings .2.2/.2.3/.2.4 land, which can now ship via OTA against runtime 0.2.0, no further build needed.

title: Web download button for own match videos
description:
Web participants currently have playback (timekeeper-flow video-analysis-viewer) but no way to save the file.

Work (repo: jits_web, apps/web):
1. Add a Download button to the video playback/analysis surface (apps/web/components/domain/video-analysis-viewer.tsx or its parent), using the shared signed-URL helper (jits-kaf.2.1) and an <a download> / programmatic anchor with the signed URL (createSignedUrl supports the download option to force Content-Disposition).
2. Filename: something human, e.g. elorated-match-{date}.{ext}; keep the real extension (.webm web recordings, .mp4 mobile).
3. One primary CTA per surface rule: Download is a secondary/outline button, not Signal Red.

Small, web-only, OTA-irrelevant. Per native-first directive this is the only web item in Phase 2; keep it minimal.
acceptance_criteria: A participant on web can download their full match video with a sensible filename. No raw storage calls (uses shared helper). Typecheck + test green; build:web green if routes touched.

title: Mobile download / save-to-phone: expo-media-library + expo-sharing
description:
Let participants keep their full match video on their phone.

Work (repo: jits_web, apps/mobile):
1. Add expo-media-library + expo-sharing (NATIVE DEPS + app.json permission strings NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription etc. → TestFlight, coordinate with jits-kaf.2.6; the config-plugin/permissions change makes this NOT OTA-eligible).
2. On the playback screen (jits-kaf.2.2): a Download action that (a) gets a signed URL (shared helper, jits-kaf.2.1), (b) FileSystem.downloadAsync to cache, (c) MediaLibrary.saveToLibraryAsync into the camera roll, with progress UI and success/failure toasts; plus a Share action via expo-sharing for the downloaded file.
3. Permission flow: request add-only photo permission at tap time; on deny, offer the share-sheet path (expo-sharing needs no photo permission) instead of dead-ending.
4. Clean up the cache file after save/share. Handle large files (multi-minute MP4s): progress callback, prevent double-tap re-downloads.

WebM caveat: saving .webm to an iOS camera roll will fail or produce an unplayable asset; gate the action on extension until jits-kaf.1.2 resolves.
acceptance_criteria: Participant taps Download on their video and the full MP4 lands in their photo library (or share sheet on permission denial), with visible progress. No orphaned cache files. Quality gate green; ships in the Phase 2 TestFlight build.

title: Mobile AI analysis viewer: summary, recommendations, scoring moments, technique timeline
description:
Port the web video-analysis-viewer (apps/web/components/domain/video-analysis-viewer.tsx, currently timekeeper-flow-only) to mobile, mounted on/with the playback screen (jits-kaf.2.2).

Work (repo: jits_web, apps/mobile):
1. Components under apps/mobile/components/domain/ (or lib/video/) rendering the get_video_analysis payload via the shared wrapper (jits-kaf.2.1): match summary text, recommendations list, scoring moments, technique-tag timeline.
2. Tap a scoring moment / technique tag → seek the expo-video player to timestamp_seconds.
3. Only render when status='analyzed'; otherwise the playback screen's progress UI (use-video-progress) owns the space. Analysis is optional: a video with no analysis still plays fine.
4. Design tokens: draws/pressure amber, losses Signal Red, gains Gain Green, ALL numbers font-mono tabular-nums, no decorative color. Component files under ~80 lines each, split sections.

No backend work; get_video_analysis already exists and is participant-readable.
acceptance_criteria: For an analyzed video, mobile shows summary, recommendations, scoring moments, and the technique timeline; tapping a timestamped item seeks the player. Unanalyzed videos degrade gracefully. Quality gate green.

title: Mobile playback screen: watch own match videos (expo-video)
description:
Mobile has NO video playback at all today. Build the screen participants use to watch their own match videos.

Work (repo: jits_web, apps/mobile):
1. Add expo-video (NATIVE DEP → TestFlight, coordinate with jits-kaf.2.6 release issue; do not OTA).
2. New route, e.g. apps/mobile/app/(app)/video/[id].tsx pushing on top of the (app) Stack, with a fetch hook apps/mobile/lib/video/use-match-video.ts following the use-match-details.ts cancelled-ref pattern.
3. Resolve the video via shared getMatchVideos/getAthleteVideos + getMatchVideoSignedUrl (jits-kaf.2.1); render expo-video player with native controls, landscape support, and status states (uploading/processing/slicing/analyzing → progress UI via existing use-video-progress hook; failed → error state; signed-URL expiry → refetch).
4. Entry points: match summary step (apps/mobile/lib/match-flow, summary step) and match history rows (profile) when a video row exists for the match. RLS already limits reads to participants, no client gating logic needed beyond empty-state.
5. Design rules: no drop shadows, sharp corners, numeric data font-mono tabular-nums, screens under ~200 lines (orchestrate via hooks).

WebM caveat: web-recorded .webm rows will not play in expo-video; show an 'unsupported format' state keyed on file extension until jits-kaf.1.2 resolves.
acceptance_criteria: A participant can open and watch their MP4 match video from match summary and match history. Non-ready statuses show progress, failed shows an error, webm shows unsupported. Quality gate green; ships in the Phase 2 TestFlight build.
notes: PARTIAL (2026-07-24, commit 975d35e): mobile playback shipped as Profile-tab 'Past Match Videos' section + pushed video/[id] player screen, deliberately on expo-av (already in the field build) so it OTA-ships without a TestFlight build. The expo-video swap remains with the Phase 2 build (jits-kaf.2.6). Pending on-device verification.

title: Shared video data slice: typed wrappers for get_match_videos / get_video_analysis / get_athlete_videos + signed-URL helper
description:
The shared layer currently has only createMatchVideo/upsertMatchVideo (mutations.ts:608-744) and the use-video-progress hook. There are NO typed query wrappers for the video read RPCs, and apps/web/components/domain/video-analysis-viewer.tsx:162 calls supabase.rpc('get_video_analysis', ...) RAW, violating the 'never raw .rpc()' rule.

Work (repo: jits_web, packages/shared):
1. Add to packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts (client-as-parameter, per house pattern): getMatchVideos(matchId), getVideoAnalysis(videoId), getAthleteVideos(athleteId) wrapping the existing BE RPCs; export the BE return-shape types (the viewer already mirrors get_video_analysis types at the top of video-analysis-viewer.tsx, lift them into shared).
2. Add getMatchVideoSignedUrl(client, storagePath, expiresIn) wrapping supabase.storage.from('match-videos').createSignedUrl(); return Result<T> with mapped errors (mutations convention) or a typed null-on-error query shape, match whichever queries.ts uses.
3. Refactor video-analysis-viewer.tsx to consume the shared wrapper (no behavior change).
4. Export via the package export map; unit tests alongside (see match-video.test.ts for the pattern).

Coordinate with jits-0lc (video mutations → Result<T>), same file region; sequence after it to avoid churn.
acceptance_criteria: No raw .rpc()/.from() video calls remain in either app for reads. Wrappers typed against database.ts, exported from @jits/shared/api, covered by unit tests. Typecheck + test green across workspaces.
notes: PARTIAL (2026-07-24, commit 975d35e): getAthleteVideos (get_athlete_videos wrapper) + getMatchVideoSignedUrl signed-URL helper shipped in packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts with tests. Still missing from this slice: get_match_videos + get_video_analysis wrappers.

title: DECISION: web records WebM but the slicer assumes MP4 and iOS Safari cannot play WebM
description:
Web recording (apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts, MediaRecorder) produces .webm uploads at matches/{matchId}/{uploaderAthleteId}/{ts}.webm. Two problems: (1) the jr_be ffmpeg slicer worker assumes MP4 input, so web-recorded videos may fail or misbehave in the analysis pipeline; (2) WebM will not play on iOS Safari or in the Phase 2 mobile player (expo-video), so web-recorded videos would be invisible to mobile users and to the Phase 3 community feed on iOS.

Options to evaluate (pick one, record rationale here, file the follow-up implementation issue under Phase 1 or as a Phase 2/3 dependency):
A. Record MP4/H.264 on web where supported (MediaRecorder mimeType video/mp4 works in Safari; Chromium support is partial/version-dependent) and fall back to WebM with a known-degraded badge.
B. Transcode server-side: the slicer/Cloud Run worker already wields ffmpeg; add a webm→mp4 normalize pass before slicing and store the normalized artifact for playback.
C. Accept WebM as web-only: exclude web-recorded videos from mobile playback + community feed until transcoding exists (cheapest, worst product).

Consider: storage cost of double artifacts (B), browser-matrix complexity (A), and that mobile recordings (the priority platform) are already MP4 and unaffected.

Repos: jits_web (web recorder) and/or jr_be (slicer worker).
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded with rationale, the chosen option has an implementation issue filed and dep-linked, and Phase 2/3 issues know whether they must handle WebM.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text:
AUDIT 2026-09-10 - the problem is worse than filed, and one option is now ruled out empirically.

VERIFIED by running ffmpeg locally against a real MediaRecorder WebM:
- VP8 WebM -> MP4 with '-c copy' (the slicer's fast path, main.js:487-489) is a HARD FAILURE: 'Could not find tag for codec vp8 in stream #0'. The slicer dies on chunk 0 and the video parks forever. This is not 'may misbehave'.
- VP9 WebM -> MP4 '-c copy' SUCCEEDS but produces VP9-in-MP4, which main.js:562 then mislabels contentType 'video/mp4'. iOS/AVFoundation cannot decode VP9-in-MP4, so the artifact is still unplayable on the priority platform.
- Additional likely failure BEFORE either: ffprobeDuration (main.js:338-353) THROWS when format=duration is not a finite positive number. MediaRecorder writes streaming WebM with an unknown Segment duration, which commonly probes as N/A.
- The bitrate re-encode fallback (main.js:889-895) is gated on >5Mbps or >60MB projected chunks; a 854x480 web recording is ~1-2Mbps so it NEVER triggers. The broken copy path is exactly the one that runs.
- No .webm row has ever been through the pipeline: all 4 local match_videos rows are .mp4. The green local e2e is MP4-only evidence and does not cover the web path.

Option C (accept WebM as web-only) is now untenable: the original .webm is also what playback signs (video-analysis-viewer.tsx:143-150), so web-recorded matches are unplayable on iOS in the web app too, not just on mobile.

RECOMMEND A+B, not either alone:
- A (record MP4 where supported) is required anyway to fix jits-rvc, the Safari recorder crash, and gives most users a directly-playable artifact with no server cost.
- B (normalise to H.264/AAC MP4 in the slicer before slicing, store the normalised artifact as the playback source) is the safety net for browsers that still only emit WebM, and fixes iOS playback for free.
A alone leaves WebM-only browsers broken; B alone leaves the Safari recorder crash and pays transcode cost on every web upload.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my 2026-09-10 comment on this bead. Part of that comment was WRONG and should not be acted on.

WHAT I GOT WRONG: I wrote that 'VP8 WebM -> MP4 with -c copy (the slicer's fast path) is a HARD FAILURE' and that 'the broken copy path is exactly the one that runs'. The raw ffmpeg result was real, but the conclusion about the SLICER was not: the slicer never takes the copy path for VP8. decideEncodeMode (main.js) gates on MP4_COPY_SAFE_VIDEO_CODECS = {h264, hevc, mpeg4} and MP4_COPY_SAFE_AUDIO_CODECS = {aac, mp3}, and anything else forces re-encode with trigger 'codec' REGARDLESS of the bitrate thresholds. That gate landed in f0f0ced (2026-09-11), before my comment; I was reasoning from this bead's original description instead of the current code. My claim that 'the bitrate re-encode fallback never triggers so the broken path runs' was therefore wrong in its premise.

VERIFIED 2026-09-14 by pushing a real VP8 WebM through the live local pipeline. Slicer logged:
  video_codec=vp8, audio_codec=null, format_name=matroska,webm, mode=reencode, trigger=codec
Chunks were produced and persisted correctly. No copy-mux failure occurred.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BROKEN, and is now fixed: the PLAYBACK half. Chunk re-encoding never helped the viewer because playback signs match_videos.storage_path, i.e. the ORIGINAL upload, which for a web recording is still WebM and unplayable on iOS Safari / expo-video. No normalized full-length artifact was ever written.

DECISION RECORDED: A+B, both implemented.
  A (jits_web): recorder now probes MP4/H.264 first and derives extension + contentType from recorder.mimeType. Also fixed jits-rvc (Safari recording was dead and reported 'Camera access denied').
  B (jr_be): migration 20260914000000 adds match_videos.normalized_path + set_match_video_normalized_path(); the slicer writes one full-length H.264/AAC MP4 when trigger=='codec', best-effort and AFTER chunks commit so analysis is never blocked; getMatchVideoSignedUrl prefers normalized_path.
Verified end to end locally: vp8 source -> normalized artifact probed as h264 / yuv420p / mp4, 18.56s, moov atom within the first 4KB (faststart). 48 pgTAP files / 1442 tests PASS.

Also corrected: ffprobeDuration now falls back to per-stream duration when the container reports N/A, so a live-muxed WebM with no Segment Duration is not rejected outright. The 'N/A duration' risk in my earlier comment was NOT reproduced on the samples available here, so it is hardening, not a fixed defect.

See bd memory key 'slicer-beads-drift-verify-code-first'.

title: Phase 3 (Community review): opt-in publish, community feed, timestamped comments, manual tagging
description:
The community review section. OPT-IN model (decided): videos remain visible only to the two match participants unless the uploader explicitly publishes; publishing makes the video readable by all active athletes in a community feed where they can watch, read the AI analysis, leave timestamped comments, and add manual technique tags.

Backend scope (jr_be): published_at column + RLS (community SELECT on published rows, uploader-only publish/unpublish UPDATE, storage.objects read extension), video_comments table + RLS, paginated feed RPC, technique_tags manual-INSERT policy widening for non-participant viewers.

Frontend scope (jits_web): shared-layer slice (publish mutation, feed query, comments CRUD, manual tag mutation), mobile publish flow + community feed screen + review screen, web community section (P2, native-first).

JS-only on mobile if Phase 2's native deps are already in the field → OTA-eligible.
acceptance_criteria: Uploader can publish/unpublish own video; unpublished videos stay participant-only (RLS-verified with pgTAP). Active athletes can browse a paginated newest-first feed of published videos, watch them, see an analysis badge, add/view timestamped comments, and add manual technique tags. Both platforms; web may trail mobile.
notes:
=== 2026-09-24: PARTIALLY REUSABLE BY THE HIGHLIGHT-CLIP EPICS, BUT ONE ASSUMPTION DOES NOT SURVIVE ===

Epics jr_be-15c (backend render pipeline) and jits-s6mi (client, Reels handoff) opened 2026-09-24.
This epic is NOT a prerequisite of either and must not be pulled onto their critical path, but the
overlap is worth stating so neither side duplicates the other.

REUSABLE: the published_at model on match_videos (jits-kaf.3.1), the publish RPC shape, the widened
storage RLS pattern, and the confirm-dialog UX that already forbids pre-checked boxes and
publish-by-default. That UX constraint in particular is exactly right and should be inherited by
any Instagram consent dialog.

NOT REUSABLE, and this is the fatal one: THE UPLOADER-ONLY CONSENT ASSUMPTION. Publishing to an
in-app feed of authenticated athletes and publishing to a public Instagram audience are different
disclosures, and TERMS.md:38 grants its licence FROM THE UPLOADER ALONE. Defensible for the former,
not for the latter. jr_be-17f owns that decision.

A HARD CONSTRAINT THAT RUNS THE OTHER WAY: jr_be-15c's entire premise is that a rendered clip
reaches no audience the source video does not already reach, which is why rendering is unblocked
while sharing is not. If jits-kaf.3.1's widened community storage RLS is ever applied to the
highlights/ prefix, that premise collapses and jr_be-17f becomes a blocker on the render path too.
The highlights/ prefix must stay participant-scoped independently of whatever this epic does to
match_videos.

title: Phase 2 (Mobile experience): playback of own videos + AI analysis viewer + download/save-to-phone
description:
Give participants a way to actually watch what they recorded. Mobile-first per the native-first directive.

Scope: shared typed wrappers for the video read RPCs + signed-URL helper; a mobile playback screen for own match videos (expo-video); a mobile AI analysis viewer (port of web video-analysis-viewer.tsx: summary, recommendations, scoring moments, technique-tag timeline with tap-to-seek); download/save-to-phone (expo-media-library + expo-sharing); a web download button.

NATIVE DEPS: expo-video, expo-media-library, expo-sharing are new native modules → this phase requires a TestFlight build, NOT OTA. Ship all three deps in ONE build.

Repos: jits_web only (packages/shared/src/api, apps/mobile, apps/web). Reads existing BE RPCs get_match_videos / get_video_analysis / get_athlete_videos; no backend changes expected.
acceptance_criteria: From a finished match (summary or history), a participant on mobile can open the video, watch it, see the AI analysis when status='analyzed', and save the MP4 to their camera roll or share sheet. Web participants get a download button on the existing viewer surface. Shipped via TestFlight build; full quality gate green.

title: [epic] Full video integration: record → upload → playback/download → community review
description:
Take match video from 'records and uploads (buggy)' to a complete product surface. Three phases that each ship independently, foundation first:

PHASE 1 (Foundation): fix the 6 open upload-path bugs (jits-1v6, jits-81l, jits-hu0, jits-voh, jits-0lc, jits-za8) and get the analysis pipeline actually running (slicer Cloud Run worker deploy + app.settings.video_slicer_url GUC + match-videos bucket in a migration), plus the WebM-vs-MP4 decision for web recordings.

PHASE 2 (Mobile experience): mobile playback of own match videos + AI analysis viewer + download/save-to-phone (new native deps expo-video / expo-media-library / expo-sharing → TestFlight build, NOT OTA) + a web download button.

PHASE 3 (Community review): OPT-IN publish flow (videos stay participant-only unless the uploader explicitly publishes; backend RLS change), community video feed on both platforms, timestamped human comments (new video_comments table), and manual technique tagging by viewers.

Visibility model (decided, do not relitigate): opt-in sharing. match_videos SELECT is participant-only today (match_videos_select_participant); a published row becomes readable by all active athletes.

'Coaching' in the review section = all three of: (a) surface the existing AI analysis (video_analyses: summary, recommendations, scoring moments, technique-tag timeline), (b) timestamped human comments, (c) manual technique tags by viewers (technique_tags already supports source='manual').

Current state: mobile records MP4 in the live match step and streams to private bucket match-videos via FileSystem.uploadAsync; web records WebM via MediaRecorder; upsertMatchVideo inserts at status='ready'. Backend (jr_be) already has match_videos / video_chunks / video_chunk_analyses / video_analyses / technique_tags, RPCs get_match_videos / get_video_analysis / get_athlete_videos / get_video_progress / get_scouting_report, a 1051-line ffmpeg slicer Cloud Run worker + Gemini analyze-chunk/merge edge functions, and pg_cron sweeps. Web has a playback/analysis viewer in the timekeeper flow only; mobile has NO playback; no download anywhere.
acceptance_criteria: All three phase children closed. An athlete can record a match, the pipeline analyzes it, both participants can watch + download it on mobile and web, the uploader can opt-in publish it, and the community can browse, comment (timestamped), and tag techniques on published videos.

title: Gym Finder city dropdown dead to touch (Select trigger active: variant on nested View)
description: ui/select.tsx SelectTrigger had active:opacity-70 on a View nested inside the Pressable. title: Mobile result step: submission allows empty finish time but BE requires it -> silent record failure
description:
FOUND during live simulator walkthrough (Nia Costa vs Demo Red NPC).

result-step.tsx canSubmit treated an EMPTY finish time as valid for submissions (isFinishTimeValid returns true for empty), and the field was labeled 'Finish Time (optional)'. But BE record_match_result REQUIRES finish_time_seconds for a submission (raises missing_fields). So RECORD RESULT was enabled with no finish time, the RPC was called, failed, and nothing recorded (silent 'couldn't record' toast, match stuck in_progress). Proven live: empty finish time -> no-op; '90' -> success (ELO applied).

FIX: result-step.tsx canSubmit now requires a non-empty AND valid finish time for submissions (finishTimeProvided && finishTimeValid); submission-fields.tsx label changed from 'Finish Time (optional)' to 'Finish Time'. Draw path unaffected. isFinishTimeValid + its 13 tests unchanged (empty stays field-valid; the non-empty requirement lives in canSubmit).
close_reason: Fixed: result-step.tsx canSubmit now requires a non-empty + valid finish time for submissions; submission-fields.tsx label 'Finish Time (optional)' -> 'Finish Time'. Found + reproduced live in simulator (empty finish time -> silent record failure; with value -> success). Typecheck + mobile 204 tests green.

title: Ready-Check has no Cancel/Leave — user stuck if opponent never readies
description:
TOP PRIORITY user request. In the match-flow 'ready' step (apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/ready-step.tsx), once the user taps Ready the UI shows 'Waiting for opponent...' (line 107-111) with NO cancel/leave/back affordance. The match screen header (apps/mobile/app/(app)/session/[id]/match/[matchId].tsx:14-17) intentionally HIDES the back button ('leaving mid-flow needs to go through dispute/cancel ctas'), so the user is fully stuck if the opponent never readies.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): A session match is created via create_session_match RPC in status='pending' and BOTH participants are locked to session_participants.status='in_match' with current_match_id set (jr_be 20260405000800_session_rpcs.sql:122-145). The ONLY ways those locks release are: match status -> 'completed' (trg_release_session_participants, lines 707-729) or dispute_match (requires status IN ('in_progress','completed'), lines 449-451). The matches.status CHECK constraint is ('pending','in_progress','completed','disputed') — there is NO 'cancelled' status (jr_be 20260204034401_create_matches_tables.sql:37). There is no cancel-match RPC. cancelChallenge() (mutations.ts:102) only touches the challenges table, not matches/session_participants. So a pending match cannot currently be aborted cleanly from the client, and the same gap exists on web (ready-check-step.tsx also has no cancel).

PROPOSED FIX (preferred, needs BE): add a cancel_session_match(p_match_id) RPC in jr_be (SECURITY DEFINER) that, when match.status='pending', sets it to a terminal state and releases BOTH session_participants (status->'available', current_match_id->NULL) so neither athlete is stranded. Either add 'cancelled' to chk_match_status (cleanest) or reuse 'completed' with a null outcome + a release trigger update. Then add a shared mutation cancelSessionMatch() in packages/shared/src/api/mutations.ts, and a Cancel affordance on the ready step that calls it, broadcasts a 'match_cancelled' event on session-match:{matchId} (so the opponent's ReadyStep also aborts), and routes the user back to the lobby (/(app)/session/[id]/lobby).

UX (brand): destructive secondary action in Signal Red as a text/outline button BELOW the primary Ready CTA (one primary CTA per surface — keep Ready primary). Label 'Cancel Match' / 'Leave'. Show a confirm dialog ('Cancel this match? Your opponent will be returned to the lobby.'). Place on both the pre-ready and waiting states. Opponent receives the broadcast and is auto-returned with a toast.

LOWEST-RISK INTERIM (frontend-only, if BE change is out of scope this sprint): add a 'Leave' button that calls leaveSessionLobby() (sets this athlete's participant status='left') and routes to lobby/home. CAVEAT: this does NOT clear the opponent's in_match lock or the pending match row, so the opponent stays stuck and the match row lingers — document this as a known limitation. The BE RPC is the correct fix.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Ready step shows a Cancel/Leave affordance in both the pre-ready and 'waiting for opponent' states.
- Tapping it (after confirm) aborts the pending match and returns THIS user to the lobby.
- (with BE RPC) The OPPONENT is also released (participant back to available) and auto-navigated out via broadcast; the pending match row is terminal.
- No regression to the happy path (both ready -> start_match -> live).
- Button uses Signal Red destructive styling, secondary to the primary Ready CTA.

RISK: med (touches match state machine + BE migration; participant-lock correctness). Frontend-only interim is low-risk but incomplete.
SCOPE: mobile + shared mutation + jr_be migration; WEB PARITY needed (ready-check-step.tsx has the same gap).
close_reason: Implemented + independently reviewed + quality gate green (typecheck, jits_web tests 389, web build, jr_be 038 test all pass).

title: Production backend cutover at App Store launch: repoint EAS production Supabase URL/key + flip APP_ENV
description:
TestFlight currently runs against the STAGING Supabase project (rzowigdcdojlovlwwpkx) on purpose — all three EAS environments (development/preview/production) share that one URL today, and the production build profile tags Sentry environment=staging (committed in 3ea3f9c).

GOTCHA: which backend the app talks to is controlled ONLY by EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL / EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, NOT by EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV (which is just the Sentry environment label; see apps/mobile/lib/env.ts + lib/supabase/client.ts, no branching on APP_ENV). So building with --profile production does NOT automatically point at a production backend. A public App Store release would silently ship against staging unless this is done.

Before promoting any build past TestFlight to the public App Store, do these together:
1. Stand up / confirm the real PRODUCTION Supabase project.
2. Update EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL + EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY in the EAS 'production' environment (eas env:update --environment production) to the prod project.
3. Flip apps/mobile/eas.json production profile env EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV back to 'production'.
4. Rebuild and VERIFY the build talks to prod (not staging) before submitting for App Store review.

Related: jits-by0 (add elorated:// deep-link redirect URLs to the PROD Supabase auth allowlist as part of the same cutover).

title: Brand the mobile toast appearance to the Void/Signal-Red system
description:

title: Make email confirmation recoverable in-app and build the missing reset-password screen
description:
PROBLEM: If Supabase requires email confirmation, signup hands the user a 'Check your email' wall with only 'Back to Sign In', no resend, no polling, forcing a leave-app/confirm/return/manual-relogin round trip mid-onboarding. Separately, the password-reset loop is BROKEN: the deep link routes the reset token to /login which never consumes it, so a forgotten password is unrecoverable in-app, a hard retention defect independent of FTUE.

EVIDENCE: signup.tsx confirm screen has no resend (verified); auth-context returns needsEmailConfirmation when no session; deep-links/handler.ts:42-44 routes reset-password token to /login with comment 'the dedicated reset-password screen does not exist yet'; auth-context has resetPassword but no resend/updateUser-with-token path

PROPOSED CHANGE: TWO parts, sequenced by a config check FIRST. (A) Check the Supabase project's email-confirmation setting. If it is OFF (cheapest, dominates building resend UI), the entire confirm dead-end disappears at zero engineering cost, but note it is a backend/ops toggle with a spam/throwaway-email tradeoff that pollutes the cold-start roster, so weigh it. If confirmation stays ON, add a 'Resend confirmation email' action (supabase.auth.resend) and prefer the deep-link return path the handler already has over a battery-draining getSession poll. (B) Regardless of the confirmation setting, BUILD the missing reset-password screen: consume the token the handler already forwards and call updateUser with the new password. Part B is the higher-value half and should ship even if confirmation is off.

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/app/(auth)/signup.tsx, apps/mobile/lib/auth/auth-context.tsx, apps/mobile/lib/deep-links/handler.ts, apps/mobile/app/(auth)/reset-password.tsx (new)

Group: Medium | Effort M | Impact Medium. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #12).
acceptance_criteria: The Supabase email-confirmation setting is checked and the decision (on/off) is documented ; If confirmation is on, the confirm screen offers a working Resend action ; A reset-password screen exists, consumes the deep-link token, and successfully calls updateUser to set a new password ; A user who forgot their password can fully recover in-app without leaving for a browser ; No getSession polling loop runs on a backgrounded screen

title: Remove stubbed/ghost surfaces so the app does not feel broken to a TestFlight reviewer
description:
PROBLEM: A prominent disabled Signal-Red 'Challenge' button on every athlete profile only toasts 'Challenges coming soon', a visible no-op that both violates the one-meaningful-primary-CTA rule and is exactly what the competitor persona says makes them abandon. Settings exposes CHAT and CHALLENGES toggles for features not shipped on mobile, and a realtime-test debug screen ships in the production settings stack.

EVIDENCE: athlete/[id].tsx:124-134 (disabled Challenge button toasts 'Challenges coming soon'); app/(app)/settings/realtime-test.tsx present in shipping settings dir (verified via ls); settings/notifications.tsx exposes CHAT/CHALLENGES toggles

PROPOSED CHANGE: Pure client hides/removals, zero backend, no build. (1) HIDE the head-to-head Challenge button until the flow exists (do NOT repoint it to the in-session-lobby path, that requires an active-session context the profile screen lacks and is M-effort with breakage risk). (2) Hide the CHAT and CHALLENGES settings toggles behind a not-built condition, after verifying they are purely cosmetic and do not orphan backend notification-preference rows. (3) Remove realtime-test.tsx from the production settings stack entirely (move behind a __DEV__ guard rather than dev-flag, so a wrong default cannot ship it).

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/app/(app)/athlete/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/notifications.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/realtime-test.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/_layout.tsx
