title: Make city optional/auto-derived in the activation wizard (the ONLY safe field to slim)
description:
PROBLEM: The wizard hard-blocks submit on a non-empty city even though the backend activation trigger does NOT require it, and the city dropdown is built only from cities that already have gyms with a hardcoded Toronto/Vancouver fallback. So an unserved user is forced to pick a city that isn't theirs and literally cannot complete activation honestly, the field-count cliff made worse by an impossible field.

EVIDENCE: validation.ts:62-69 (isTrainingComplete requires city.trim()); use-setup-data.ts:39-48 (city list gym-derived with Toronto/Vancouver fallback); CLAUDE.md trigger contract needs display_name + current_weight + gym/free_agent + gender + DOB, NOT city; research: every required pre-aha field costs signups (https://foundrycro.com/blog/form-conversion-rate-benchmarks-2026/)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Client-only one-line-plus change that does NOT touch the trigger and never writes guarded columns. Remove city from isTrainingComplete so it is optional for activation, AND auto-derive city from the selected gym's city (the gym join already carries city per CLAUDE.md FK notes) so most users never see a city picker at all. Keep weight + gym-or-free-agent as the activating step (load-bearing for weight-aware ELO). DO NOT defer or remove gender/DOB, the critique verified these are TRIGGER-REQUIRED; removing them would silently break activation (the classic guard/trigger no-op loop) since use-setup-submit.ts:112-121 only shows a generic 'activation failed' with no field-level diagnosis. If free-text city is wanted later, it needs normalization (Toronto/toronto/TO fragments the gym-city dropdown), defer that.

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/lib/profile-setup/validation.ts, apps/mobile/lib/profile-setup/use-setup-data.ts, apps/mobile/components/profile-setup/training-step.tsx, apps/mobile/lib/profile-setup/use-setup-submit.ts

Group: QuickWin | Effort S | Impact Medium. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #6).
acceptance_criteria: A user can complete activation without manually selecting a city ; When a gym is selected, the athlete's city is auto-populated from the gym's city ; gender and date_of_birth remain required in the wizard gate (NOT deferred) ; Activation still flips pending->active for both gym-affiliated and free-agent users (verified end-to-end) ; No write occurs to any guarded column (id, auth_user_id, current_elo, highest_elo, status, created_at, role)
notes: NUANCE (CHANGELOG 2026-06-02, build 8): city was JUST made a REQUIRED native picker that AUTO-FILLS from the chosen gym. So 'auto-derive from gym' is already shipped; the remaining friction is only the FREE-AGENT case (no gym to derive from). Do NOT blindly revert the required-city decision; scope this to: make city optional ONLY when free_agent, or auto-fill always. ALSO: resolve the gender/DOB activation-requirement conflict (CLAUDE.md says required; bd memory athlete-column-guard-trigger + recon say the trigger does not enforce them) against handle_athlete_activation BEFORE touching anything but city.

title: Add Google SSO to the signup screen
description:
PROBLEM: 'Continue with Google' is the single fastest activation path, it skips three credential fields AND the entire email-confirmation detour, but it lives only on /login. A first-timer who taps 'Register' lands on a credential form and never sees the one-tap option, so the fastest path is invisible to exactly the users who need it.

EVIDENCE: login.tsx:60-64,130-132 (onGooglePress + 'Continue with Google'); auth-context.tsx exposes signInWithGoogle; signup.tsx has zero SSO (grep found no Google/Apple/SSO references); research: SSO lifts signups 20-40%, ~60% of mobile users prefer it (best-practice findings)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Render the existing 'Continue with Google' button as the primary fast path at the TOP of the signup screen, with the email/password form as a secondary 'or sign up with email' section below. signInWithGoogle already exists in auth-context, so this is a pure UI wire-up reusing login's onGooglePress pattern, no new auth code, no build. Adjacent micro-win: add a show/hide toggle to the password fields. HONEST CAVEAT per critique: SSO skips credential entry but the user STILL hits the activation wizard, so do not oversell it as a fast path to a rated profile, only to an account. SEQUENCING RISK: shipping Google without Apple on an iOS launch can INCREASE App Store rejection exposure (guideline 4.8), so do not ship this to the PUBLIC build before the Apple Sign In BiggerBet lands; for the internal TestFlight it is fine.

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/app/(auth)/signup.tsx

Group: QuickWin | Effort S | Impact High. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #5).
acceptance_criteria: The signup screen shows 'Continue with Google' as the topmost option with email/password below as a secondary section ; Tapping it invokes the same signInWithGoogle flow as login and lands the user in the activation wizard ; Password fields have a show/hide toggle ; No new native dependency is added and no new EAS build is required ; Account-linking risk is documented as an open question (same email via Google vs email/password)
notes: Apple Sign In (jits-rag) is NOT from-scratch: it was implemented then removed, preserved in commit 844b16d, blocked on the com.apple.developer.applesignin entitlement/provisioning. Re-enable + new build must precede exposing Google-on-signup in the PUBLIC store (guideline 4.8).

title: Turn the 'No Gyms Found' / unserved-city dead-end into a real path (client-only half)
description:
PROBLEM: Every Home CTA funnels to the Gyms tab, whose only empty state is a bare dashed 'No Gyms Found' label with zero call-to-action, and the city filter only lists cities that already have a gym, so a geographically-unserved user cannot even select their own city. This is the single worst FTUE dead-end: an instant uninstall for a competitor in a non-seed city.

EVIDENCE: gyms/index.tsx:213-216 (bare 'No Gyms Found' ListEmptyComponent, no CTA); gyms/index.tsx:91-119 (city set built only from loaded gym cities); CreateGymSheet already imported at gyms/index.tsx:21,159

PROPOSED CHANGE: Client-only first pass (the backend seeding half is a separate BiggerBet). Replace the bare label with a guided card offering: (1) primary 'Compete as a free agent' action reusing the existing free-agent path (verify the mobile free-agent activation works end-to-end, trigger needs free_agent=true), (2) a secondary 'Request your gym' mailto/support link (ONLY if the mailbox is actually monitored for TestFlight, else omit, an unanswered request churns harder), (3) a 'Show all cities' filter reset so a user is never trapped by an active city filter, and (4) surface the already-imported CreateGymSheet more prominently in the empty state. Do NOT add free-text city here (that is the wizard change, and has data-fragmentation risk).

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/gyms/index.tsx, apps/mobile/components/gyms/create-gym-sheet.tsx

Group: QuickWin | Effort S | Impact Medium. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #4).
acceptance_criteria: The Gyms empty state shows at least: a 'Compete as a free agent' action and a 'Show all cities' reset ; Selecting a city filter that yields no gyms still offers a one-tap reset back to all cities ; The existing CreateGymSheet is reachable from the empty state ; If 'Request your gym' mailto is included, it opens a prefilled support email; if the mailbox is not monitored it is omitted ; Empty-state respects dark-first, sharp corners, and at most one Signal-Red CTA

title: FTUE / first-run activation program (pre-launch)
description:
FTUE / first-run activation program (pre-launch). Full analysis: research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md.

AHA MOMENT: a new user's first recorded RANKED match result that moves their ELO off the bare starting 1000 (the first time a meaningful, earned rating becomes real). NOT 'finished profile', NOT 'saw ELO 1000'.

ACTIVATION MILESTONE (instrumentable): athlete_activated = backend trigger flips pending->active on an athletes UPDATE supplying display_name + current_weight + (primary_gym_id OR free_agent) + gender + date_of_birth (detect at use-setup-submit.ts:112-121).

CURRENT TTV (mobile): ~6 taps / realistically ~10-12 with in-wizard controls, 10 fields, plus an out-of-app email round trip if confirmation is ON. The aha endpoint is currently UNREACHABLE by a solo user (challenge stubbed, sessions gym-manager-gated).

PROGRAM = 3 parallel tracks: (a) make the endpoint reachable (seed a launch gym), (b) make it measurable (instrument the funnel), (c) remove client friction + de-motivators (quick wins). Sequence: Week 0 seed+instrument; Week 1 client-only quick wins (no new build); Week 1-2 config/web; next EAS build for native-gated items. Apple Sign In = jits-rag (4.8 compliance, must precede public Google-on-signup).
design: Respect dark-first Void theme, Signal-Red for CTAs/negative only, numeric data never red, sharp 4px corners, minimal motion, 4 purpose-bound fonts. Do NOT change activation-trigger logic or write guarded athlete columns.
acceptance_criteria: Quick-win client release shipped (no new EAS build); funnel instrumented end-to-end; launch gym seeded with a joinable session; activation rate measurable as a windowed rate.

title: Sentry user feedback: shake-to-report + screenshot on mobile
description:
Finish mobile Sentry setup for the wider TestFlight rollout and add an impactful in-app feedback mechanism that feeds the AI triage loop.

Scope (mobile only):
- Enhance Sentry.init: attachScreenshot, feedbackIntegration with enableShakeToReport + enableTakeScreenshot + enableScreenshot + useSentryUser + on-brand theming.
- Wrap root layout with Sentry.wrap (mounts FeedbackFormProvider; required for the shake form to render).
- Attribute feedback/errors via Sentry.setUser bootstrap (id/email/display_name), clear on sign-out.
- Settings FEEDBACK row opens the Sentry form when Sentry is live; falls back to the existing Supabase form screen otherwise.
- Add @sentry/react-native/expo config plugin to app.json (org/project placeholders; SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN via env/EAS secret).
- Document env values the user must supply: EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN, SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, org/project slugs.

Decisions (confirmed with user): Sentry User Feedback flow (not Shake.io/custom); mobile only. Tradeoff accepted: RN feedback form is screenshot-attach only, no freehand annotation.

Gate: npm run typecheck + npm run test + cd apps/mobile && npx expo export --platform ios --no-bytecode (app.json/native config changed).
close_reason: Closed

title: Audit/backfill existing web-created athlete weights (kg-magnitude in lbs column)
description: Pre-existing web rows wrote kg-magnitude numbers into the lbs current_weight column (and challenges.challenger_weight/opponent_weight). After the web kg->lbs code fix, existing rows remain wrong. title: Web stores weight in kg into an lbs column (unit bug)
description: Backend canonical unit for athletes.current_weight is POUNDS (jr_be get_weight_division() hard-codes IBJJF division boundaries in lbs; column comments say 'in lbs'). Web signup/eua/edit-profile label weight 'kg', validate 20-300, and write the raw value into the lbs column with NO conversion. Result: web-created athletes have kg-magnitude numbers in an lbs column -> wrong weight division + wrong ELO stakes. Mobile is already correct (stores raw lbs). title: TestFlight launch crash: native TurboModule throws NSException at launch, corrupting Hermes (newArch)
description:
SYMPTOM: ELO RATED iOS TestFlight (com.elorated.mobile) crashes ~0.5s after launch. 4 crash logs (builds 2 & 3) in DoKWRbP0qRetPvPAPA-zLs.xccrashpoint share one signature.

EVIDENCE (crash logs):
- All 4 crash inside Hermes with DIFFERENT garbage fault addrs each run (0x30, 0x08000024, 0x646e6582) and NO Last Exception Backtrace -> heap corruption, not a clean uncaught JS/env throw.
- Decisive frame in 3 of 4: facebook::react::TurboModuleConvertUtils::convertNSExceptionToJSError (RCTTurboModule.mm). Build-2 SIGABRT log: objc_exception_rethrow -> __cxa_rethrow -> std::terminate.
- Throwing call runs on a libdispatch worker thread (ObjCTurboModule::performVoidMethodInvocation) WHILE the JS thread runs the event loop -> off-thread Hermes access -> VM corruption.
- newArchEnabled:true (app.json:12, ios/Podfile.properties.json), Hermes. New-Arch off-thread TurboModule-exception marshalling is the amplifier.

ROOT CAUSE (two layers): (1) a native Obj-C TurboModule method THROWS an NSException during launch [trigger]; (2) RN New-Arch converts it into Hermes off-thread [turns recoverable throw into hard crash]. Must identify WHICH module throws.

TOP SUSPECTS (run unconditionally at launch, native, background queue, depend on signed-build entitlements that differ dev vs TestFlight):
1. expo-secure-store getItemAsync via Supabase auth getSession -- lib/supabase/secure-storage.ts:27 <- lib/auth/auth-context.tsx:57. Keychain entitlement / keychain-access-group mismatch from unfinished eas init / provisioning. NOT try/catch-wrapped at the JS boundary.
2. expo-notifications setNotificationHandler + addNotificationResponseReceivedListener -- lib/notifications/handlers.ts:26,35 <- push-registration-bootstrap.tsx:20 (ungated). aps-environment / remote-notification entitlement (app.json UIBackgroundModes:remote-notification).
Both consistent with the open pre-launch blocker: eas init placeholders + unfinished Apple provisioning (Team ID, push key, entitlements).

RULED OUT: RN/Hermes version skew -- single react-native@0.81.5 tree (npm ls deduped), reanimated 4.1.7 + worklets 0.5.1 correct. Sentry not in the crash stack (initSentry early-returns without DSN; lib/error-tracking/sentry.ts). Supabase module-load env throw (jits-00q) would be a clean JS Error, not this off-thread native corruption.

NEXT STEP (decisive -- get the actual NSException reason):
(a) Release build on-device: npx expo run:ios --configuration Release, read '*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception' in Xcode/Console; OR
(b) Console.app / idevicesyslog filtered to process ELORATED during TestFlight launch; OR
(c) provision EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN + @sentry/react-native expo config plugin so next build reports it.
Then: fix the named module's entitlement/config AND wrap launch-path native calls (SecureStore getItem, notification handler setup) in try/catch so a native throw degrades instead of crashing.

NOTE: This session did NOT change app code (a version-realign attempt was reverted; tree clean, 179 tests green). Crash fix still pending the exception-reason capture above. Related: jits-00q (env-var fix, likely necessary but not sufficient).

title: TestFlight build crashes on launch: Supabase env vars missing from EAS build profiles
description: Cloud EAS builds (preview/production -> TestFlight) crash immediately on app open. Root cause: apps/mobile/lib/supabase/client.ts creates the Supabase client at module load via env.supabaseUrl/env.supabaseAnonKey; apps/mobile/lib/env.ts throws 'Missing env var' when EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY are absent. apps/mobile/eas.json defines only EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV per profile, so cloud builds have no Supabase creds (.env is gitignored, local-only) -> uncaught startup throw -> launch crash. Works in dev because local .env is present. Fix: inject EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY (and EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_*_CLIENT_ID so Google auth works) into all eas.json build profiles; also correct app.json updates.url from PLACEHOLDER_PROJECT_ID to the real EAS projectId.

notes:
BUILD #3 SUCCEEDED 2026-05-29 (eas build --profile production --platform ios). EAS log line 6 confirms all 4 EXPO_PUBLIC_ vars (SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY, GOOGLE_IOS/WEB_CLIENT_ID) loaded from production environment and baked into the binary -> launch-crash fix is in the artifact. Build page: expo.dev/accounts/drozes18/projects/elo-rated/builds/7004a400-aca6-4872-9f4a-fb346b0d7cdc ; ipa: expo.dev/artifacts/eas/eQhs3DD6VNboAdsdXQXQRb.ipa . Submitting to App Store Connect/TestFlight now. NOTE: expo-updates is NOT installed (build warned), so app.json updates.url + eas channel are inert until 'npx expo install expo-updates' -- confirms updates.url was never the crash cause. Close after the TestFlight build launches on device without crashing.
ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE (deeper than env-injection, 2026-06-01): builds 3 AND 4 BOTH shipped WITHOUT EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL in the bundle (verified: 0 occurrences in build 4 main.jsbundle) and crashed identically (SIGABRT via ExceptionsManager.reportException rethrow). Prior note's assumption 'loaded from environment = baked into binary' was WRONG. lib/env.ts reads the value via a COMPUTED access processEnv[`EXPO_PUBLIC_${key}`], which babel's EXPO_PUBLIC inliner cannot statically replace -> never inlinable into a release bundle regardless of EAS injection (Google IDs worked because auth-context.tsx reads them via STATIC process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_X). FIX (commit e0e9783): added apps/mobile/app.config.js copying the values into Constants.expoConfig.extra (read first by env.ts, embedded via EXConstants independent of babel inlining) + build-time guard that fails the EAS build if missing. Also consolidated duplicate-named Supabase EAS env vars into single all-env vars (matching working Google vars). VERIFIED: local Release sim build boots + loads live data; build 5 (id 7585e62d-6e43-4118-80ce-c2eafcb78d9b) embeds URL in EXConstants.bundle/app.config (vs 0 in build 4), auto-submitted to TestFlight. title: Harden the outbound-footage guard: four confirmed evasions
description:
The unreachability guard has two halves. The Instagram half is solid. The
outbound-footage half has four confirmed evasions, all reproduced by the
reviewer running the parser against adversarial input.

## The evasions

The share-sheet check is a hand-rolled paren parser plus a deny-list of
identifier names. Reproduced:

  Share.share({ message: "Nice one :)", url: videoUri })
    EVADES. The ")" inside the string literal closes the parse early;
    args scanned = '{ message: "Nice one :'. The url is never seen.

  const opts = { url: videoUri }; await Share.share(opts)
    EVADES. Args scanned = "opts". This is the natural refactor the
    moment a payload gets conditional.

  Share.share({ ...payload })
    EVADES.

  Share.share({ url: highlightAsset })
    EVADES. The deny-list is an allowlist by omission:
    renderedClip, assetUri, uri all pass.

The import guard likewise: both
  import * as Sharing from 'expo-sharing'    (single quotes)
  require("expo-sharing")
evade /from "expo-sharing"|from "expo-media-library"|.../

## No live reach today

All four existing Share.share call sites were re-confirmed to pass a URL
and a sentence, never a video file, and nothing imports either package.
These are tripwire weaknesses, not a current breach. Same class as the
original guard gap (which missed apps/mobile/modules/ entirely).

## Why it matters

The legal gate covers the generic share sheet and save-to-camera-roll as
well as Instagram, because all three are the same disclosure of the other
athlete's likeness outside the participant set. The guard is what stops
someone shipping "just save it to my photos" as an unflagged convenience.
A tripwire that a routine refactor walks past is not a tripwire.

## Recommended shape

1. Drop the parser. Flag any scanned file containing `Share.share` AND a
   video identifier ANYWHERE in the file. Coarser, some false positives,
   but it cannot be walked past by a refactor or a stray paren, and it
   matches how the Instagram half already works.
2. Import guard -> /["']expo-sharing["']|["']expo-media-library["']/
   which covers single quotes, require() and dynamic import() at once.
3. toHaveLength(4) is a fine anti-vacuity anchor, but a bare count invites
   a silent bump when a legitimate profile-share button lands. Assert the
   SET of four relative paths instead, so a reviewer must look at which
   file changed. Keep the tripwire either way: a new share button
   deserving a deliberate look is a feature, not a cost.

Must land before the share entry point does.

title: Slice B5: TestFlight build for the Reels native module, plus on-device pasteboard-prompt and drop-off measurement
description:
The Reels module and its config plugin are NATIVE changes: a new native module, plus app.json plugin config touching Info.plist and AndroidManifest. Per the workspace mobile-deploy policy this ships via TestFlight (eas build), NOT via EAS Update. An OTA can never carry a native change and will silently ship without it, which here means the share action exists in JS and the platform declarations do not, so availability detection returns a confident false on a device where Instagram is installed. That is exactly the silent failure this policy exists to prevent.

On the build, measure what cannot be measured any other way: how often the iOS 16 pasteboard prompt appears, whether the photo-access prompt appears mid-handoff, and where athletes drop out of the funnel instrumented in Slice B3. Frequency and conversion impact of that prompt are explicitly listed as unverified in research section 9, so this is the issue that verifies them.

Worth a direct look on the same pass: JudoFlow (App Store v1.1.2, ~2026-09-11) advertises 'your training becomes a swipeable story ... ready to share to your Instagram story'. Mechanism undisclosed. It is the nearest live implementation of this feature in a grappling app.
acceptance_criteria: A TestFlight build carrying the native module and the config plugin is in testers' hands. The iOS pasteboard prompt's actual frequency and the funnel drop-off are recorded in this issue as numbers, not impressions. The share affordance remains flag-off in that build.

title: match_videos.duration_seconds is never sent on upload
description:
Verified on a real device upload against local Supabase (2026-09-21): a
16.1 MB clip landed with status=ready and duration_seconds NULL.

## Both halves already exist, nothing connects them

- The mutation ACCEPTS it: packages/shared/src/api/mutations.ts:641 declares
  `durationSeconds?: number`, and writes it on INSERT (:684) and UPDATE (:731),
  each guarded by `!= null`.
- The recorder KNOWS it: apps/mobile/lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:433
  computes `elapsedMs` from `recordStartedAtRef` and already uses it for
  cap-vs-interruption classification at :436.

A grep for `durationSeconds` across apps/mobile/lib/video/ and
apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts returns nothing. Neither client passes it.

## Why it matters

duration_seconds is read and returned by four backend RPCs
(get_athlete_videos, get_match_details, get_match_videos, get_athlete_stills),
so every video list row ships a NULL. It is also the natural field for a
playback UI to show length before load, and for anything sizing analysis work.

Note the column has NO CHECK constraint and is client-supplied, so it is
trusted input. Prefer the recorder's measured elapsed time over anything
user-editable, and consider whether the value should be sanity-bounded on
write given matches.duration_seconds is constrained to 0 < n <= 3600 while
match_videos.duration_seconds is not.

## Scope

- Pass the measured duration from the mobile recorder through
  startMatchVideoUpload into the existing mutation param.
- Same for web (MediaRecorder can report it, or take it from the resulting
  blob via a <video> element the way scripts/test-video/viewer/app.js already
  does at :400-415).
- On a resumed upload the duration must survive the resume, since the row is
  written after the bytes land and possibly in a later process.

Related: the same upload shipped thumbnail_url NULL, tracked separately.

title: Funnel persisted upload writes through one guarded helper
description:
The supersede model in video-upload-manager.ts is now guard-dense rather than
structurally safe: thirteen isCurrent() call sites, each sitting immediately
after the await that opens its window. It is correct today -- verified by
grep and pinned by 38 manager tests covering all five interleavings -- but it
is correct only while nobody adds a fourteenth await without a guard.

## Recommended shape

The implementer proposed a cancellation token threaded into uploadBytes and
writeRow. The reviewer proposed something cheaper with most of the benefit:
funnel every persisted write through a single guardedPatch(handle, matchId,
patch) helper that no-ops when superseded. That is a mechanical refactor a
reviewer can verify by counting call sites, rather than a rewrite of the
function that just carried three P0 races.

Prefer the helper unless the token buys something the helper does not.

## Why this was NOT done now

Explicitly considered and deferred during the review of 1587740. Rewriting
the exact function that just carried three reproduced P0s, before any device
testing has happened, trades a known-good tested state for an unknown one.
The reviewer's verdict was "ship the guard-dense version, do not block".

## Requirements when it lands

Same suite green (mobile 837+, video-path 125+), and its own independent
review pass. Do not let an implementer approve this one.

title: P2: failed match-video upload is terminal, invisible past the wizard, and strands the local file
description: The match-keyed upload store is read only inside MatchRecorderProvider, so once the user taps the summary exit CTA nothing renders it again. Store is in-memory only, there is no manual retry, and deleteAsync appears nowhere in apps/mobile so the recorded MP4 is never cleaned up on success or failure. Failure scenario: both upload attempts fail on gym wifi, the user exits within ~10s, the process is later killed, the video is permanently lost with no notice and a 300MB-1GB orphan in the app cache.
notes:
Confirmed in detail by the video implementer during 46fb344 and deliberately NOT fixed, because it needs a product decision. The match-keyed store is read only inside MatchRecorderProvider, so once the user taps the summary exit CTA nothing renders it again; the store is in-memory only; the single automatic retry inside handleUpload is the only retry anywhere; and deleteAsync appears nowhere in apps/mobile, so the recorded MP4 is never cleaned up on success OR failure. On a ladder night that is one orphaned multi-hundred-MB file per match plus recorded matches whose video silently does not exist. Wants persistence plus a visible retry affordance.
GROUNDWORK EXISTS as of 23590b3, committed but NOT authored in that session and NOT finished. Landed: tus-js-client ^4.3.1 (pure JS, OTA-eligible, does not force a TestFlight build), packages/shared/src/utils/backoff.ts (exponential backoff with EQUAL jitter, deliberately not full jitter because full can return ~0ms), apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-persistence.ts (AsyncStorage-backed unfinished-upload record, one record per match keyed on matchId which is safe because match_videos has uq_match_video_uploader, one AsyncStorage key per record so progress writes and the resume sweep cannot clobber each other, and a bytes-vs-row phase split so a job that finished uploading never re-uploads hundreds of MB to retry one INSERT), apps/mobile/lib/video/tus-rn-shims.ts, and a types shim for the tus browser deep import so Metro and Jest resolve the same file. NOT DONE: nothing consumes any of it (backoff.ts names lib/video/video-upload-manager.ts, which does not exist), and none of the three new source files has tests. The product decision on persistence plus a visible retry affordance is still open.

title: getGymManagerStats discards errors on all four reads, rendering false zeroes on a page athletes read
description:
Found by the queries.ts audit for jits-icei.5, confirmed in review. Not fixed there.

getGymManagerStats (packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:1319) destructures data/count only on all four of its reads (sessions, active member count, session_participants count, matches count). Every failure becomes a zero.

CONSEQUENCE: it is not a manager-only surface despite the name. apps/web/app/(app)/gyms/[id]/gym-detail-content.tsx calls it for ANY athlete viewing a gym and renders the result in GymStatsGrid, so a failed read presents a gym as having run zero sessions and zero matches. Mobile shows the same numbers through lib/gym-manager/use-gym-hub.ts. There is no signal that the numbers are missing rather than real.

FIX SHAPE: getGymManagerStatsResult sibling, strictly additive, same loader-plus-wrapper pattern used in jits-icei.5. Every one of the four reads is a count with no legitimate ambiguity, so the whole payload is fatal-or-nothing here: there is no partial worth rendering, unlike the gym detail case.

COORDINATE: the web call site is in apps/web.

title: getGymDetail degrades the athlete's own RSVP list, so gym detail can tell an attendee they are not attending
description:
Raised in review of jits-icei.5 and confirmed there. Deliberately NOT fixed with that work.

loadGymDetail (packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts) classes the athlete's own session_rsvps and session_participants reads as DEGRADED: they are logged and defaulted to empty rather than failing the payload. That classification is correct and should stand, because promoting them to fatal would hide a live session behind an error plate, which is the harm jits-icei.5 exists to prevent.

But the default is not neutral. An empty rsvpSessionIds is consumed as a positive claim: apps/mobile/components/gyms/gym-detail-parts.tsx:160 renders the Attend affordance for any session not in the list, so an athlete who HAS rsvp'd is told they have not and is re-offered Attend. The backend then refuses the duplicate. Same dead-end shape as jits-tydo: the UI offers an action the server will not accept.

THE REAL FIX is a third state, not a reclassification. The athlete's own attendance is currently a boolean derived from list membership, with no way to say UNKNOWN. It wants to be explicit, so the surface can suppress the CLAIM (render the session without an Attend or Going affordance, or with a muted one) without suppressing the SESSION.

Touches packages/shared (the payload shape), mobile gym-detail-parts.tsx, and the web gym detail page's GymRsvpAction, so it is a real slice rather than a tweak. apps/web is owned by another session; coordinate.

title: Route mobile's raw PostgREST reads through the shared wrappers, in priority order
description: Full sweep of apps/mobile at b5b7d8c found 23 raw PostgREST calls (22 .from, 1 .rpc; 18 reads, 5 writes), verified complete by two independent sweep methods that agree exactly. Realtime .channel and supabase.storage are excluded as having no wrapper. THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS NOT ABOUT WRAPPERS: 14 of the 18 raw reads destructure { data } and drop error on the floor, which given shouldThrowOnError=false means every one renders a FAILED read as an EMPTY read. Exactly one raw read surfaces the error (use-leaderboard-data.ts:56) and exactly one reasons correctly about what a failed read means (use-arena-challenge.ts:344), and that one carries a 20-line comment explaining why, which is a fair measure of how much thought it takes to get right by hand. ORDERED PLAN, from the audit. (1) apps/mobile/lib/session/use-session-lobby-realtime.ts:70 is the closest match in the codebase to the web archetype: it hand-builds a LobbyParticipant from five columns, while the wrapper path (getSessionLobbyData, RPC get_session_lobby) returns two fields the raw copy cannot compute and therefore hardcodes, gymName: null at :80 and eloDistance: 0 at :85, repeated at :197 and :202 for the broadcast path. So the same participant renders one way arriving via realtime and another way after any refetch. It is invisible today only because participant-row.tsx renders just name, elo and weight. The moment a lobby row shows a gym label or an ELO-distance badge, late joiners render wrong and it will look like a realtime bug rather than a wrapper bypass. Also note a failed athlete read there hits , so the joiner silently never appears in the lobby and no retry exists because the INSERT event is consumed. (2) The waiver triangle, tracked separately as jits-ftqy. (3) hooks/use-unread-count.ts:28 re-implements getUnreadCounts while ALREADY IMPORTING UnreadCountRow from that wrapper's module; apps/web/hooks/use-unread-count.ts:24 bypasses it too, so the wrapper is currently called by nobody and a fix to unread semantics would reach neither app. (4) Extract a getAthleteProfile wrapper (use-athlete-profile.ts:45 and the identical web copy both select '*, gyms!fk_athletes_primary_gym(name)'; the * is RLS-legal but ships auth_user_id, date_of_birth, role, platform_role and is_scoutable, every column ATHLETE_GUARD_SELECT was written to exclude), and widen GymListItem/GymDetail to carry latitude/longitude/address so the sidecar gym reads at gyms/index.tsx:61 and gyms/[id].tsx:63 can go. (5) The error-swallowing pass, which should be merged into the shared-query error-signal work (jits-icei.5) rather than duplicated. TWO USER-VISIBLE TODAY, independent of any wrapper question: use-setup-submit.ts:156 discards the error on a status re-read and then tells a user whose profile saved perfectly that activation failed; and the lobby realtime read above. ONE ANTI-PATTERN TO AVOID: do NOT swap use-setup-data.ts:86 for getAllGyms. The raw copy filters status=active and the WRAPPER does not, so the wrapper is the stale one here and swapping would put inactive gyms in the signup picker. getAllGyms needs a status parameter first. Also noted: gyms/[id].tsx:69 puts a .catch() on getGymManagerStats, which resolves on every path, so it is dead code whose comment claims a failure mode that cannot occur.
design: Filed as ONE issue rather than six, because the ordering matters more than the individual fixes and splitting them loses the argument. Priority 2, not 1: nothing here is on fire the way the web playback bug was, but mobile carries the same latent structure that produced that P1 and the sweep found its pre-detonation state in at least five places.
acceptance_criteria: The five items are addressed in the stated order, or consciously deferred with a reason recorded on this issue. use-session-lobby-realtime builds its participant through the same shape the wrapper returns, so a realtime arrival and a refetch render identically. No mobile raw read silently treats a failed read as empty; each either surfaces the failure or documents why swallowing it is correct. getAllGyms gains a status filter before anything is pointed at it. The dead .catch at gyms/[id].tsx:69 is removed.
notes:
CORRECTION to the description: one code fragment was lost to shell quoting. In item (1), the sentence should read "a failed athlete read there hits the early return when the athlete row is falsy (use-session-lobby-realtime.ts, the guard immediately after the read), so the joiner silently never appears in the lobby and no retry exists because the INSERT event is consumed."

CONTEXT FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP. This sweep exists because a parallel session found the same class on WEB and it was a real bug there: apps/web/components/domain/video-analysis-viewer.tsx hand-rolls a match_videos query and signs storage_path directly, never reading normalized_path. So when the shared wrapper getMatchVideoSignedUrl was taught to prefer the normalized H.264 artifact (so iOS Safari can play a source recorded as WebM), that fix never reached web playback at all. Mobile got the same cross-platform case RIGHT FOR FREE, purely because its one playback surface calls the wrapper, and without ever knowing the field existed. Same feature, same helper, same week, opposite outcomes, decided by nothing except whether the caller went through the wrapper.

That asymmetry is the argument for this issue and it is worth keeping attached to it. The audit also recommended rewriting the rationale in CLAUDE.md, which currently justifies the typed-wrapper rule on consistency and type-safety. Both of those framings score a byte-identical raw copy as harmless, which is exactly how the web viewer passed review and how use-unread-count.ts reads today. The stronger and empirically supported rationale is that THE WRAPPER IS WHERE FIXES LAND, so a raw copy silently opts out of every future correction, including corrections written years later by someone who has no idea the copy exists. That CLAUDE.md change is NOT made: it is a project policy file and the call belongs to the user, not to an audit.

title: Waiver identity is resolved three different ways, and two of them race inside one join flow
description: LIVE CORRECTNESS BUG, found by the mobile raw-read sweep. The same concept, 'which waiver is the athlete signing', is resolved three incompatible ways. (1) packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:814-820, inside getSessionForJoin, queries waivers WHERE scope='app' AND is_active with an unordered .limit(1).maybeSingle(), keeps only the boolean requiresWaiver, and computes hasSignedWaiver against ITS row. (2) apps/mobile/lib/session/use-session-for-join.ts:71 then RE-RUNS that identical unordered query by hand to obtain an id to write the acknowledgement against. (3) apps/mobile/lib/profile-setup/use-setup-data.ts:91 pins the same concept by HARDCODED SLUG 'app-liability-v1'. The waivers table has UNIQUE(slug) only, with no constraint on (scope, is_active), and jr_be/supabase/migrations/20260405000200_waivers.sql:23 explicitly says a new version is a new row. So with two active scope='app' waivers, the two unordered limit(1) queries are free to return DIFFERENT rows: the athlete is checked against waiver A and signs waiver B, hasSignedWaiver stays false forever, and they are re-prompted on every single join. Meanwhile signup has signed v1 by slug while session-join checks an arbitrary active row. Publishing a v2 waiver detonates all three at once. apps/web has the identical pair at join-content.tsx:38, so this is not mobile-only. Today it is live-on-data rather than live-on-every-request (it needs a second active app waiver to exist), which is exactly why it will be discovered at the worst possible moment, when someone publishes an updated waiver.
acceptance_criteria: One shared wrapper, suggested name getActiveAppWaiver, returns the waiver ID (not just a boolean) and is the single place the active app waiver is chosen, with a deterministic order rather than an unordered limit(1). getSessionForJoin, the mobile join hook, the mobile profile-setup hook and the web join content all resolve the waiver through it, so no two code paths can disagree about which waiver is current. The hardcoded 'app-liability-v1' slug is gone. A test proves that with two active scope='app' waivers present, the check and the acknowledgement refer to the same row. Consider whether the backend should also enforce at most one active waiver per scope, since that would make the class impossible rather than merely unlikely.
notes:
Found 2026-09-19 by an audit of raw PostgREST reads in apps/mobile, prompted by a parallel session finding the same class on web (a component hand-rolling a query that shadows a wrapper, then drifting from it). Flagged as the one item in that sweep that is a correctness bug today rather than a latent one.


=== 2026-09-24: this now gates a legal deliverable, not just a join flow ===

jr_be-17f (consent model for sharing match footage, now the gate on the highlight-clip share step)
is likely to require a new or revised waiver, because no existing waiver mentions recording,
likeness or publication and the waivers table's scope CHECK admits only 'app', 'gym' and
'insurance', so a media release has no scope to occupy. Publishing a v2 waiver with this bug live
means athletes are checked against waiver A and sign waiver B, hasSignedWaiver stays false forever,
and they are re-prompted on every join. So this must be fixed BEFORE any new waiver version ships,
and jr_be-17f's acceptance criteria now say so. Consider raising priority when that decision moves.

title: getArenaData returns null cast as ArenaData on a failed RPC, a latent crash at the call site
getSessionForJoin discards errors on four reads: a failed waivers read silently skips the waiver step
description:
Found by the queries.ts audit for jits-icei.5.

getSessionForJoin (packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts, the getSessionForJoin block) destructures data only on all four reads.

1. session read fails -> returns null -> the join wizard reports the session as not found or not joinable. Same 'failed read reads as absent' shape as jits-icei.5.
2. waivers read fails -> activeWaiver null -> requiresWaiver = false -> the wizard SKIPS the waiver step entirely, and hasSignedWaiver is never even checked.
3. waiver_acknowledgements read fails -> hasSignedWaiver false -> the athlete is asked to sign again (harmless).
4. athletes read fails -> athleteWeight null -> the weight step starts blank.

Case 2 is NOT a compliance hole: the BE join_session RPC raises P0001 with HINT waiver_required and the FE maps it to the WAIVER_REQUIRED domain code, so the server still refuses the join. The real consequence is a confusing dead end: the wizard skips the step, then the join fails with an error the athlete was given no way to satisfy.

FIX SHAPE: getSessionForJoinResult sibling, with the session and waivers reads fatal and the other two degraded, mirroring the fatal/degraded split documented on loadGymDetail.

title: getActiveSession discards errors on all seven reads, so Home can tell an athlete they are not in a session
description:
Found by the queries.ts audit for jits-icei.5.

getActiveSession (packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts, the getActiveSession block) destructures data only on every one of its seven reads: the participant rows, the active-session lookup, the gym name, the participant count, the rsvp rows, the upcoming-session lookup, and the check-in row. It returns null on any failure, and mobile Home renders ActiveSessionCard with 'no active session'.

This is the same class of lie as jits-icei.5 and it sits on the SAME SCREEN: Home's Promise.all runs getActiveSession alongside the discovery reads. An athlete who is checked into a live session is told they are not, on a dropped request.

NOT fixed with jits-icei.5 deliberately: unlike the discovery surface, ActiveSessionCard has no error affordance at all, so wiring a signal needs UI work (a failed/retry state on the card) rather than just a query change. That makes it its own slice.

FIX SHAPE: getActiveSessionResult as a sibling, same additive pattern, plus an error state on ActiveSessionCard. Note two of the reads are legitimately 'absent' rather than failed (no participant rows, no rsvps), so the Result payload wants to stay ActiveSessionInfo | null inside ok:true.

title: Arena mobile: accepting while your own challenge is out abandons it without cancelling
description:
Found in review of the Arena mobile branch (A13).

In apps/mobile/lib/arena/use-arena-challenge.ts, enterMatch clears BOTH incoming and outgoing local state. So if A has a challenge out to B and then accepts C's challenge, A's challenge to B is dropped from A's screen but stays 'pending' in the database. B can still accept it, which creates a second match with A in it while A is already in a match with C.

The screen partly hides this (actionsLocked suppresses the Challenge action while either incoming or outgoing is set) but it cannot prevent the race: B's accept is a separate client.

Fix: cancel the outgoing challenge server-side before navigating into an accepted one, or refuse the accept while an outgoing challenge is live and say why. The first is better; it keeps the handshake single-keyed on 'the match you are actually in'.
acceptance_criteria: Accepting a challenge while one of your own is outstanding cannot leave a pending row the other party can still turn into a second match.

title: Arena mobile: the roster only refreshes on pull
description:
Found in review of the Arena mobile branch (A11), and it is the enabling condition for the cap misattribution fixed in fbdc24e.

apps/mobile/lib/arena/use-arena-roster.ts fetches once on mount and then only when `refresh()` is called (pull-to-refresh, or the new onOpponentUnavailable path). There is no realtime subscription on `athletes` and no refetch on focus, so `acceptsRanked` and the roster membership itself are a snapshot that ages the whole time the screen is open. Presence keeps the Online/Open split honest for people who are IN the roster, but someone who goes live AFTER the snapshot never appears at all until a manual pull.

This is more visible now that the product keeps people live while they wander into profiles and matches: the Arena screen can stay mounted for a long time.

Options: refetch when the Arena tab regains selection (useIsTabSelected already computes it), a postgres_changes subscription on athletes filtered to looking_for_ranked, or a slow poll.
acceptance_criteria: An athlete who goes live while another athlete is already sitting on the Arena appears to them without a manual pull.

title: Arena mobile: the 3-challenge cap has no remedy on this surface
description:
Found in review of the Arena mobile branch (A8).

The cap plate tells the athlete to cancel one of their three outgoing challenges, but Cancel only exists for the challenge THIS screen session created: `outgoing` in apps/mobile/lib/arena/use-arena-challenge.ts is in-memory state, not a read of pending rows. Three unanswered challenges sent yesterday cap the athlete for the full 7 days of challenges.expires_at while the plate offers an action they cannot take.

Options:
1. Read the athlete's own pending outgoing challenges on Arena load and let the cap plate list and cancel them. Needs a shared query (getPendingChallengeOpponentIds is close but returns both directions and no ids of the challenges themselves).
2. Give Arena-origin challenges a short TTL, so an unanswered live challenge expires in minutes rather than a week. This is a backend question: challenges.expires_at defaults to now() + 7 days for every origin, and a live handshake has different semantics from an asynchronous challenge.
3. Both.

Option 2 is the one that matches the product: a challenge sent to someone standing in a lobby is meaningless an hour later.
acceptance_criteria: An athlete who is at the cap can see and clear what is holding them there, or Arena-origin challenges expire fast enough that the cap cannot strand them.

title: Arena mobile: confirm that leaving the Arena surface should drop you out of the lobby
description:
Decision made while building jits-y1lg, worth a product confirmation before the device pass.

apps/mobile/lib/arena/use-arena-live.ts takes the athlete fully offline (untrack lobby:online AND clear looking_for_ranked) on blur and on app background. Blur rather than unmount, because a tab navigator keeps its screens mounted, so unmount would almost never fire and the flag would linger exactly the way it does on web.

The consequence to confirm: tapping an athlete row to read their profile blurs the Arena, so you come back offline and have to tap Go live again. That is correct under the strict reading of the rule (leaving Arena clears the flag) and it can never advertise an athlete who is not there, but it is a papercut on the most common in-Arena navigation.

Options if it bites during the device pass:
1. Keep as is.
2. Restore live automatically on refocus when the athlete did not toggle off themselves (sticky-live within a session), which reintroduces a small window where the flag is false but the intent is true.
3. Exempt pushes that stay inside the Arena stack (athlete profile) from the blur clear, and keep it for tab switches, matches and background.

Also noted while building: the incoming challenge prompt shows the challenger's weight in lbs rather than an IBJJF division name, because there is no shared weight-division helper on the JS side (get_weight_division() is backend only). If the division label is wanted, it needs a shared util first.
acceptance_criteria: A product decision is recorded and either the current behaviour is confirmed or one of the alternatives is implemented and tested.
notes: Resolved by the user: STAY LIVE UNTIL YOU LEAVE THE ARENA TAB. Implemented in fbdc24e via apps/mobile/lib/arena/use-arena-tab-focus.ts, which reads the tab navigator's own index (that survives a push over the tabs) rather than screen focus. A pushed athlete profile or match keeps you live; another tab, backgrounding or teardown clears you. Both directions are tested.
close_reason: Closed

title: Token drift guard F8: modern colour syntax false-fails
description: normalizeColor() in tokens-mirror-drift.test.ts understands only #rgb/#rrggbb/#rrggbbaa and legacy comma-form rgb()/rgba(). Space-separated modern syntax rgb(107 114 128 / 45%), color-mix() and oklch() fall through to a lowercased string compare and false-fail against the equivalent mobile value. Relevant the moment a designer regenerates the brand file from a modern tool. Fix: parse the space/slash form and percentage alpha; decide explicitly whether color-mix()/oklch() should be an unsupported-syntax FAILURE rather than a silent mismatch.

title: Token drift guard F6: !important breaks value comparison
description: normalizeColor() in tokens-mirror-drift.test.ts does not strip a trailing !important, so '#8D929D !important' normalises to '#8d929d !important' and false-fails against '#8d929d'. No current mirror uses !important. Fix: strip a trailing !important before normalising, and decide whether its presence should itself be reported.

title: Token drift guard F5: light theme does not inherit :root token declarations
description: In apps/mobile/__tests__/lib/tokens-mirror-drift.test.ts, resolvedPalette() looks a mapped token up ONLY in its own theme scope. The CSS cascade says [data-theme="light"] inherits every :root declaration it does not override, so a mirror that legitimately omits a redundant light declaration is reported as "(not declared)" instead of resolving through inheritance. Today every mirror declares all 17 tokens in both blocks so nothing is mis-reported, but a tidy-up of a web mirror would produce a false divergence. Fix: fall back to the dark/root scope for the token lookup itself, not just for var() resolution.
notes: COORDINATION 2026-09-19: stays a follow-up, deliberately NOT pulled forward. The risk was that the jits-ozvd author (another session, owns apps/web) would hit a false '(not declared)' divergence on top of the expected red if they tidied a web mirror by deleting a light declaration that is redundant with :root. That session was warned and replied that its change is value substitution rather than tidying, so the edge never fires for it. The one deletion in the delta package, --color-signal-red-dark going unreferenced once light --accent-cta-hover moves to #F0556B, will be COMMENTED OUT rather than deleted, which sidesteps the inheritance edge entirely and keeps the primitive visible to whoever regenerates from the SharePoint brand source. That session verified --color-signal-red-dark is referenced in BOTH web mirrors (design-system/tokens.css:41 declared and :278 used, public/design/tokens.css:35 declared and :272 used), so the comment-out approach covers both. It also confirmed both web mirrors already use [data-theme="light"] rather than @media (prefers-color-scheme), so the guard's palette-form constraint is already satisfied on web and no form change is needed. Fix this when convenient, not before jits-ozvd.

title: Five session-screen exits still point at /gyms, which is no longer a tab: retarget them at Home
description:
DEFERRED FROM THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF THE NAVIGATION SURGERY DIFF. Dangling navigation references left over from the tab-bar change.

WHY THIS EXISTS. The nav surgery removed /gyms as a TAB. It is now a pushed, bar-less screen, and Home owns gym and session discovery. Five exits on the session screens still send athletes to /gyms, which means they leave a session and land on a bar-less pushed screen instead of on the surface that now owns discovery.

The five sites:
- apps/mobile/components/session/lobby/leave-button.tsx:50, router.replace("/gyms")
- backFallback="/gyms" at apps/mobile/app/(app)/session/[id]/join.tsx:31
- backFallback="/gyms" at apps/mobile/app/(app)/session/[id]/join.tsx:46
- backFallback="/gyms" at apps/mobile/app/(app)/session/[id]/join.tsx:63
- backFallback="/gyms" at apps/mobile/app/(app)/session/[id]/lobby.tsx:140
- backFallback="/gyms" at apps/mobile/app/(app)/session/[id]/lobby.tsx:164

These should point at Home, which is now the discovery surface and a real tab.

RELATIONSHIP TO jits-qimh. This is the SAME CLASS of dangling reference that jits-qimh was filed for. jits-qimh scoped itself to the 17 gym-manager props and does not cover these five session-screen exits, so they need their own pass. Whoever works both should check for overlap before starting.

WHAT DONE MEANS. All five exits resolve to Home. A leave or back from a session lands the athlete on a tabbed screen that can actually continue the journey, never on the bar-less pushed /gyms screen with no way back into the app's primary navigation.
acceptance_criteria: None of the five listed sites references "/gyms" as its exit target: apps/mobile/components/session/lobby/leave-button.tsx:50, apps/mobile/app/(app)/session/[id]/join.tsx at its three backFallback props, and apps/mobile/app/(app)/session/[id]/lobby.tsx at its two backFallback props all point at Home. Leaving a session lobby, and backing out of the join screen with no navigation history, both land on Home with the tab bar visible. A repository scan finds no remaining "/gyms" exit on the session screens. Overlap with jits-qimh is checked and noted so the two passes do not fight. Typecheck and the full mobile and shared test suites stay green.
notes: Deferred from the independent review of the navigation surgery diff. Same class of dangling reference as jits-qimh, which scoped itself to the 17 gym-manager props and does not cover these five sites. Check for overlap before starting.

title: Gym-manager portal: param typing, silent gym substitution, double empty state, unguarded managed-gyms fetch
description:
Raised by review of c277f11 (F9, F10, F11, F13). Four small correctness and polish items in the relocated portal, grouped because they all sit in the same two files.

F10, TYPE: useGymManagerGymId declares useLocalSearchParams<{ gymId?: string }>, but expo-router can hand back string[] when a param repeats in the URL (?gymId=a&gymId=b). The comparison then never matches and it silently falls back to gyms[0]. Behaviour is safe (review confirmed the fallback holds for array values), but the declared type is a lie. Narrow it explicitly.

F11, UX: when the param names a gym the athlete does not manage, the portal silently shows a DIFFERENT gym with no signal. A stale bookmark after losing manager rights on gym B shows gym A's roster under no explanation. Consider a toast or an explicit not-a-manager state.

F9, UX: gym detail and the discovery surface can both render an empty-sessions state in the same flow.

F13, ROBUSTNESS: useManagedGyms (lib/gym-manager/use-managed-gyms.ts) has no rejection guard on its getManagedGyms await. A rejection leaves isReady false forever, so the portal sits on its spinner rather than showing a state. Mirror the catch pattern used elsewhere.

title: Five session-screen exits still fall back to /gyms, now a pushed bar-less screen
description:
Raised by review of c277f11 (F8). session/[id]/join.tsx (3 headers) and session/[id]/lobby.tsx (2) still use backFallback=/gyms. That resolved to a tab root before the navigation surgery; /gyms is now pushed over the tab bar with no bar of its own.

They are not broken: /gyms now carries its own back chevron falling back to Home. But landing an athlete on the gym FINDER after they back out of a session lobby is probably the wrong destination now that Home owns discovery. Consider /(app)/(tabs)/(home) or the session's gym detail instead.

Audit all five together and pick one destination.

title: Remove the unreachable wait step from the match flow: accepts a visible Step 2/8 to Step 1/7 renumber
description:
DEFERRED FROM THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF jits-3929 (the MatchFlowWizard sessionId decoupling). Confirmed dead code, deliberately left in place because removing it changes what athletes see.

WHY THIS EXISTS. The `wait` step in apps/mobile/lib/match-flow/step-router.ts is unreachable. getCurrentStep can only ever return `weight`, `live` or `summary`; nothing in the codebase sets `wait`. It is nevertheless still the FIRST entry in MATCH_STEPS, and apps/mobile/components/match-flow/match-step-renderer.tsx:73-75 still renders WaitStep when it is asked for. So it is dead-but-live code: it can never run, but it is fully wired as though it can, and it inflates the step list.

WHY IT WAS NOT JUST DELETED. Removal is NOT trivially safe. MATCH_STEPS.length feeds the visible "Step N / T" progress header. Deleting `wait` therefore changes the first screen an athlete sees from "Step 2 / 8" to "Step 1 / 7" and drops one segment from the progress bar. That is a user-visible renumbering of the whole flow, which is the entire reason it was held back from a diff that was supposed to be a behaviour-preserving decoupling.

WHAT DONE MEANS. The `wait` step is removed from the step type, from MATCH_STEPS, and from the renderer switch, and WaitStep is deleted or kept only if something else genuinely uses it. The progress header renumbering is an accepted, intentional consequence: the flow reads "Step 1 / 7" at the start. Anything asserting the old counts (tests, snapshots, screenshots, docs) is updated in the same change rather than worked around.
acceptance_criteria: `wait` no longer appears in the step union, in MATCH_STEPS, or in the match-step-renderer switch in apps/mobile/components/match-flow/match-step-renderer.tsx. WaitStep is deleted, or a comment records why it survives. The first wizard screen reads "Step 1 / 7" and the progress bar shows seven segments, and that renumber is called out explicitly in the change description so it is not mistaken for a regression. No code path can request a `wait` step. Every test, snapshot or fixture that encoded the old eight-step numbering is updated, not skipped. Mobile typecheck and the full mobile and shared test suites stay green.
notes: Deferred from the independent review of jits-3929. Held back because MATCH_STEPS.length drives the visible progress header, so this is a user-visible change and did not belong in a behaviour-preserving decoupling diff.

title: Match wizard cancel dialog still promises a lobby return: origin-aware copy needed once Arena lands
description:
DEFERRED FROM THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF jits-3929 (the MatchFlowWizard sessionId decoupling). Real defect, deliberately left out of that diff so the decoupling stayed reviewable.

WHY THIS EXISTS. jits-3929 made the match wizard origin-agnostic: it no longer requires a sessionId and its exit navigation is now injected. The component's own doc comment was updated to claim it serves both session matches and Arena matches. But one piece of session-specific COPY was left behind inside it. apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/ready-step.tsx:125, the body of the cancel-confirmation Alert, still reads "Your opponent will be returned to the lobby."

That sentence is correct for a session match, where the opponent really does land back in the session lobby. It is wrong for an Arena match, where there is no lobby to be returned to. So the component now asserts in its doc comment that it is origin-agnostic while still telling the athlete something that is only true for one origin. This is user-visible text in a confirmation dialog, which is exactly where a wrong promise costs the most trust.

WHAT DONE MEANS. The cancel-confirmation copy becomes origin-aware, driven by the same injected origin information the exit navigation already uses rather than by a new required prop. Session matches keep the current wording or an equivalent. Arena matches get wording that describes what actually happens to the opponent when an Arena match is cancelled.

SEQUENCING. This cannot be finished until Arena lands, because the Arena cancel behaviour is what the Arena copy has to describe. File now so the stale sentence is not forgotten once Arena ships.
acceptance_criteria: The cancel-confirmation Alert body in apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/ready-step.tsx no longer hardcodes lobby-return language. Copy is selected from the match origin already available to the wizard, with no new required prop added to MatchFlowWizard. A session-origin match shows lobby-accurate copy and an Arena-origin match shows copy that matches Arena's actual cancel behaviour. The component doc comment and the copy agree about which origins are supported. Mobile typecheck and the full mobile and shared test suites stay green, with test coverage asserting the per-origin copy.
notes: Deferred from the independent review of jits-3929. Blocked in practice on Arena, since the Arena branch of the copy has to describe Arena's real cancel behaviour.

title: Surface the cross-gym ladder to every athlete, not just gym managers
description:
Split out of jits-2svp during the navigation surgery, as that issue instructed.

The gym ladder (lib/gym-manager/use-gym-ladder.ts) has NO manager predicate: get_gym_ladder is aggregate-only data about gyms ranked by average member ELO, with a city filter and momentum arrows. It is a general-interest feature that happens to be stranded inside the manager-only portal at /gym-manager/ladder, reachable only by a gym manager.

WHAT DONE MEANS: the ladder is reachable by any athlete, most naturally from the gym detail screen (/gyms/[id]) or alongside Rankings. The manager-portal copy can stay or become a link to the shared surface. The own-gym highlight currently comes from the manager's managed-gym list; for a general audience it should key off the athlete's primary gym instead.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (JS only).

title: [epic] Mobile style refresh (gated on an approved design direction)
description:
WAVE 3. LAST. Nothing here starts until the user approves a design direction (see the decision child, which blocks every other child).

WHY IT IS LAST AND WHY IT IS CHEAP ONCE STARTED: the app is in unusually good shape for a restyle. NativeWind className covers 149 of 173 files (86%), 1138 className occurrences. Only 4 files use StyleSheet.create and all four are brand splash components. No styled-components, no tamagui. Dark-first is fully implemented and persisted to AsyncStorage, with ZERO `dark:` variants in the codebase because everything flips through CSS vars. A token edit retints the whole app.

WHY IT IS NOT FREE: tokens live in TWO manually mirrored files (`apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js` for authoring and `apps/mobile/lib/tokens.ts` for runtime light/dark objects), and `apps/web/app/design-system/tokens.css` is a THIRD hand mirror. Nothing enforces sync. Two naming families coexist: legacy shadcn (~34 usages left) and the ELO system (surface/ink/cta/hairline, ~1300 usages; this is the live system). And there is no spacing scale, no fontSize scale, and no shadows (flat is an explicit brand rule), with ~440 hardcoded `text-[Npx]` classes against only 25 uses of the default text-xs/sm/base scale. So a typography refresh is a ~440 call-site migration UNLESS a fontSize scale is added first, which is why the scale work blocks the migration in this graph.

DELIVERY, AND THE TRAP: almost everything here is OTA-safe. Fonts (Bebas Neue, DM Sans, Inter, JetBrains Mono) load at RUNTIME via @expo-google-fonts with NO expo-font config plugin, so font swaps ship over the air. Icons are lucide-react-native over already-linked react-native-svg, also OTA. The tab bar and all app headers are custom JS. NATIVE REBUILD is needed only for the native splash, the app icon, the Android adaptive icon, the push accent color, userInterfaceStyle, and edgeToEdgeEnabled.
THE TRAP: `runtimeVersion.policy` is "appVersion" (app.json:10). Bumping `expo.version` in a style-only release ORPHANS the OTA update, because it will only reach binaries at the same version (currently 0.2.0). Do not bump the version for a JS-only style release.
acceptance_criteria: An approved design direction is implemented across the mobile app with no visual regressions, tokens have one enforced source of truth, the legacy shadcn token family is retired, and the native-asset changes are bundled into a single approved rebuild rather than dribbled out. No OTA release in this epic bumped expo.version.

title: Native-asset bundle: splash, app icon, adaptive icon, push accent color, userInterfaceStyle
description:
THE ONLY NATIVE-REBUILD ISSUE IN THIS EPIC. Everything here changes the compiled app, so it is deliberately batched into ONE change rather than dribbled across releases, because each one costs a build and (if it goes further) an Apple round trip.

WHAT IS IN THE BUNDLE:
- The native splash: `app.json:96-102`, background #0D0F14 plus splash-icon.png.
- The app icon: `app.json:7`, and the Android adaptive icon at `app.json:44-47`. Note the existing icon issue jits-ais (E-R lettermark) and the icon-concept pipeline described in the `icon-batch-rerun-pipeline` memory; do not start a parallel icon process.
- The push accent color: `app.json:120-124` is currently a STALE #ef4444 that does not match the brand CTA #E63946. `lib/notifications/register-push.ts:40` DUPLICATES the same stale value; fix both or they will drift again.
- `userInterfaceStyle` and `edgeToEdgeEnabled` if the approved direction changes them.

DELIVERY: NEEDS A NATIVE REBUILD. This cannot ship over the air, and an OTA carrying these changes would silently ship WITHOUT them. Per the delivery gate, no `eas build` and no TestFlight submission happens without the user's explicit go. Verify locally first with `npx expo run:ios --device`.
ALSO: do NOT bump `expo.version` as part of this unless the user is doing a real release, because `runtimeVersion.policy` is "appVersion" and a bump orphans every subsequent OTA for the old binaries.
acceptance_criteria: All native assets match the approved direction, the push accent is the brand CTA #E63946 in BOTH app.json and register-push.ts, and the change has been verified on physical hardware from a local `expo run:ios --device` build. No cloud build or TestFlight submission was run without an explicit user go. The version was not bumped unless the user asked for a release.

title: Two athletes recording the same match produce two identical, unlabelled rows
description:
GAP 9. WHY: match_videos is unique per (match_id, uploaded_by), so when both athletes record, BOTH rows exist, and the profile list renders two identical entries with no `camera_angle` label and nothing to tell them apart. The user cannot tell which one is theirs or why there are two.

WHAT DONE MEANS: the video list distinguishes multiple videos of the same match, by uploader and by camera angle where it is known. Decide the presentation: label both, group them under one match, or show one with a way to reach the other. Any of those is better than two identical rows; say which you chose and why.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: A match with two uploaded videos renders unambiguously: the user can tell the two apart and can reach either. A match with one video is unchanged. Covered by a component test with a two-video fixture.

title: Small style defects: unthemed toast, hardcoded icon color, legacy stack tokens, duplicated stale accent
description:
WHY: four small, individually trivial defects that each break the "one token edit retints everything" property, which is the whole value of the token system. Cheap to fix, and they all get worse during a restyle.

THE FOUR:
1. `components/ui/toast.tsx` exports the LIBRARY Toaster with NO configuration, so toasts ignore the theme entirely. This is the most visible one: toasts appear over every screen. Existing issue jits-4zp.4 ("Brand the mobile toast appearance to the Void/Signal-Red system") already owns this; link or close it rather than duplicating.
2. `components/gym-manager/stats-parts.tsx:68` has the app's ONLY hardcoded icon color. Related: jits-a8y.32 notes that a `className` on a lucide-react-native icon is a no-op, so check that the fix actually takes effect rather than looking right in source.
3. `app/(app)/(tabs)/gyms/_layout.tsx:20-22` uses legacy tokens while every other stack uses ELO ones. Coordinate with the legacy-token retirement issue so this is not fixed twice.
4. `lib/notifications/register-push.ts:40` duplicates the stale #ef4444 push accent that also sits in app.json. The JS half is OTA-fixable; the app.json half is in the native bundle issue. Fix both halves together or the value drifts again.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update) for items 1, 2, 3 and the JS half of 4. The app.json half of item 4 belongs to the native-asset bundle issue.
acceptance_criteria: Toasts follow the theme in both light and dark. No hardcoded icon color remains, and the fix is verified visually (not just in source, given the lucide className no-op). The gyms stack uses ELO tokens. The push accent is #E63946 in register-push.ts. Overlapping issues jits-4zp.4 and jits-a8y.32 are closed or explicitly linked.

title: Retire the remaining legacy shadcn token usages (~34 sites)
description:
WHY: two naming families coexist. The ELO system (surface/ink/cta/hairline) is the live one with ~1300 usages; the legacy shadcn family has ~34 usages left. Those 34 are the sites that will look wrong after a retint, because they are wired to the wrong variables, and they are the reason "a token edit retints the whole app" is currently almost-but-not-quite true.

Known offenders already identified: `apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/gyms/_layout.tsx:20-22` uses legacy tokens while every other stack uses ELO ones. Several are catalogued in the QA sweep epic jits-a8y (for example jits-a8y.17 OnlineIndicator, jits-a8y.22 sheet/dialog/input primitive defaults, jits-a8y.16 OfflineBanner). Reconcile with those rather than duplicating them: close or link whichever the sweep already owns.

WHAT DONE MEANS: no legacy shadcn token name remains in mobile app code, or the remaining ones are a documented, deliberate exception with a reason. Dead legacy `ui/` primitives (jits-a8y.28) are either fixed or removed rather than left as a footgun.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: A grep for the legacy token names in apps/mobile returns nothing, or only documented exceptions. A token retint visibly reaches every screen with no stragglers. Overlapping jits-a8y children are closed or explicitly linked. Typecheck and tests green.

title: Real upload progress via FileSystem.createUploadTask
description:
GAP 3. WHY: `uploadProgress` is declared and hardcoded to null (`lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:134`). A match clip is a large file on a phone network, and a progress-free upload is indistinguishable from a hung one, for the user and for us when debugging in the field.

THE CONSTRAINT: `FileSystem.uploadAsync` with BINARY_CONTENT exposes NO progress callback. That is why the field is null, and it is why the existing persistent-banner issue correctly specced state-based signals rather than a percentage. `FileSystem.createUploadTask` DOES expose progress and is the fix.

WHAT DONE MEANS: the upload runs through createUploadTask, real progress reaches the persistent upload banner, and the percentage is shown alongside (not instead of) the state signals. The storage path convention is unchanged, because it matches prod storage RLS exactly and must not drift.

ORDERING: this lands after the persistent banner exists, so progress has somewhere to render.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). expo-file-system is already installed.
acceptance_criteria: Uploading a real clip on device shows a moving percentage that reaches 100 before success. title: Test coverage for the Arena presence and handshake layer
description:
WHY: Arena is realtime, multi-device, and racy. It has three channels, an idempotent RPC, a broadcast that must fire before navigation, and a double-tap guard that deliberately bypasses React state. None of that is verifiable by eye, and a regression in it looks like "the app is flaky" rather than like a bug.

WHAT DONE MEANS, at minimum:
- Presence: join, sync, leave, and that the channel is NOT re-created on re-render.
- Challenge create: the busyRef guard yields exactly one challenge under rapid double-invoke.
- Incoming: a filtered INSERT payload opens the prompt; a cancel closes it.
- Accept ordering: acceptChallenge, then startMatchFromChallenge, then broadcast, THEN navigate. Assert the order, not just that each happened, because the ordering is the whole point.
- Decline and cancel paths clear state on both sides.
- Error paths: each mutation failing leaves the UI in a recoverable state, never in a permanent pending.
- Lobby rendering: the Online / Open split given a presence state and a roster, plus each empty and error state.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (tests).

title: Arena swipe deck
description:
WHY: the user asked for a swipe surface on mobile. Web's is decorative and writes nothing, so the behavior is defined by the swipe decision issue, not ported. BUILD NOTHING UNTIL THAT DECISION IS ANSWERED.

WHAT DONE MEANS, assuming the recommended Option A (swipe to challenge):
- Route `apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/arena/swipe.tsx`, reached from a header action on the lobby and returning to it.
- The deck is the "Online now" roster one card at a time. Card face: avatar, display name, ELO, weight division, gym, win/loss record, online dot.
- Right swipe opens a confirm sheet ("Challenge <name>?", Send / Cancel). Send runs the SAME hook as the lobby, not a second implementation.
- Left swipe passes and suppresses that athlete from the deck for 24h, stored in AsyncStorage, not the database.
- States: loading (card skeleton), empty deck, end of deck ("You have seen everyone who is live", with refresh), challenge sent confirmation, error.

If the decision lands on Option B (mutual intent), this issue is DEFERRED behind a new jr_be backend epic and must not be attempted client-first.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update) PROVIDED the gestures use react-native-gesture-handler and react-native-reanimated, both already linked. Any other animation or gesture package flips this to a NATIVE REBUILD and must come back to the user before a build is run.
acceptance_criteria: The swipe deck implements exactly the behavior the decision issue settled. Under Option A: a right swipe plus Send produces a real challenge that the opponent sees live, a left swipe removes the card and the athlete does not reappear for 24h across app restarts, and every listed state is reachable. No new native dependency was added, or the user approved one explicitly.

title: Upload never sends durationSeconds or a thumbnail, so the video list rows are bare
description:

title: Migrate the ~440 hardcoded text-[Npx] call sites onto the fontSize scale
description:
WHY: ~440 hardcoded `text-[Npx]` classes against 25 uses of the default scale means typography is not currently a system, it is 440 independent decisions. Until they move onto a scale, every future type change is a 440-site migration.

WHAT DONE MEANS: hardcoded pixel type classes are replaced with scale tokens. This is mechanical but not blind: sizes that do not map cleanly onto the scale are a signal that either the scale or that screen is wrong, and those get flagged rather than rounded silently.

ORDERING: strictly after the scale exists. Doing it before means migrating twice.

SIZE WARNING FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: this is the single largest diff in the program. Split it into reviewable slices by area (auth, home, arena, gym, profile, match flow, shared components) rather than opening one 440-site PR that cannot be meaningfully reviewed. Per the workspace policy, parallel implementers on disjoint slices each get their own worktree.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: No hardcoded text-[Npx] class remains outside documented exceptions. Every screen is visually diffed before and after, with intentional changes called out and unintentional ones fixed. Sizes that did not map to the scale are listed on this issue with the resolution taken. Typecheck and tests green.

title: Oversize upload produces the wrong error message (correctness, not a live risk)
description:
WHY THIS IS SMALL AND FILED ANYWAY: the 2 GiB client cap matches the prod bucket limit exactly and is UNREACHABLE at 720p for 600s, so this is not a live production risk and must not be treated as one. But the error path exists, and if it ever fires it should say the true thing (the file is too large for the bucket) rather than a generic upload failure, because a wrong message here would send someone chasing network problems.

WHAT DONE MEANS: an oversize file produces a specific, accurate message naming the size limit, and the check is consistent with the actual prod bucket limit rather than a drifting client-side constant.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: An artificially oversized upload produces a specific size-limit message. The client cap and the prod bucket limit are documented as the same number in one place. Covered by a unit test.

description:

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: Both scales exist in both token files with matching values, are usable from className, and are documented. The app is visually unchanged by this issue alone (adding a scale changes nothing until call sites move). Typecheck and tests green.

title: Playback has one generic error panel for every failure and never reads match_videos.status
description:
GAP 10. WHY: `apps/mobile/app/(app)/video/[id].tsx` shows a single generic error for every failure and never reads `match_videos.status`. So "you are not a participant", "still processing", "failed", and "does not exist" all look identical. BACKEND NOTE: jr_be surfaces a top-level `error_message` from `get_video_progress` where a reason is available (NULL means no reason). Use it where it is there; do not invent copy that claims a reason we do not have.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: Each of the five failure classes renders a distinct, accurate panel with the right next action. A backend-provided error_message is shown when present and not fabricated when absent. Covered by component tests for every state.
