title: Real upload progress via FileSystem.createUploadTask
description:
GAP 3. WHY: `uploadProgress` is declared and hardcoded to null (`lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:134`). A match clip is a large file on a phone network, and a progress-free upload is indistinguishable from a hung one, for the user and for us when debugging in the field.

THE CONSTRAINT: `FileSystem.uploadAsync` with BINARY_CONTENT exposes NO progress callback. That is why the field is null, and it is why the existing persistent-banner issue correctly specced state-based signals rather than a percentage. `FileSystem.createUploadTask` DOES expose progress and is the fix.

WHAT DONE MEANS: the upload runs through createUploadTask, real progress reaches the persistent upload banner, and the percentage is shown alongside (not instead of) the state signals. The storage path convention is unchanged, because it matches prod storage RLS exactly and must not drift.

ORDERING: this lands after the persistent banner exists, so progress has somewhere to render.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). expo-file-system is already installed.

title: [epic] Mobile style refresh (gated on an approved design direction)
description:
WAVE 3. LAST. Nothing here starts until the user approves a design direction (see the decision child, which blocks every other child).

WHY IT IS LAST AND WHY IT IS CHEAP ONCE STARTED: the app is in unusually good shape for a restyle. NativeWind className covers 149 of 173 files (86%), 1138 className occurrences. Only 4 files use StyleSheet.create and all four are brand splash components. No styled-components, no tamagui. Dark-first is fully implemented and persisted to AsyncStorage, with ZERO `dark:` variants in the codebase because everything flips through CSS vars. A token edit retints the whole app.

WHY IT IS NOT FREE: tokens live in TWO manually mirrored files (`apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js` for authoring and `apps/mobile/lib/tokens.ts` for runtime light/dark objects), and `apps/web/app/design-system/tokens.css` is a THIRD hand mirror. Nothing enforces sync. Two naming families coexist: legacy shadcn (~34 usages left) and the ELO system (surface/ink/cta/hairline, ~1300 usages; this is the live system). And there is no spacing scale, no fontSize scale, and no shadows (flat is an explicit brand rule), with ~440 hardcoded `text-[Npx]` classes against only 25 uses of the default text-xs/sm/base scale. So a typography refresh is a ~440 call-site migration UNLESS a fontSize scale is added first, which is why the scale work blocks the migration in this graph.

DELIVERY, AND THE TRAP: almost everything here is OTA-safe. Fonts (Bebas Neue, DM Sans, Inter, JetBrains Mono) load at RUNTIME via @expo-google-fonts with NO expo-font config plugin, so font swaps ship over the air. Icons are lucide-react-native over already-linked react-native-svg, also OTA. The tab bar and all app headers are custom JS. NATIVE REBUILD is needed only for the native splash, the app icon, the Android adaptive icon, the push accent color, userInterfaceStyle, and edgeToEdgeEnabled.
THE TRAP: `runtimeVersion.policy` is "appVersion" (app.json:10). Bumping `expo.version` in a style-only release ORPHANS the OTA update, because it will only reach binaries at the same version (currently 0.2.0). Do not bump the version for a JS-only style release.

title: Two athletes recording the same match produce two identical, unlabelled rows
description:
GAP 9. WHY: match_videos is unique per (match_id, uploaded_by), so when both athletes record, BOTH rows exist, and the profile list renders two identical entries with no `camera_angle` label and nothing to tell them apart. The user cannot tell which one is theirs or why there are two.

WHAT DONE MEANS: the video list distinguishes multiple videos of the same match, by uploader and by camera angle where it is known. Decide the presentation: label both, group them under one match, or show one with a way to reach the other. Any of those is better than two identical rows; say which you chose and why.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).

title: Small style defects: unthemed toast, hardcoded icon color, legacy stack tokens, duplicated stale accent
description:
WHY: four small, individually trivial defects that each break the "one token edit retints everything" property, which is the whole value of the token system. Cheap to fix, and they all get worse during a restyle.

THE FOUR:
1. `components/ui/toast.tsx` exports the LIBRARY Toaster with NO configuration, so toasts ignore the theme entirely. This is the most visible one: toasts appear over every screen. Existing issue jits-4zp.4 ("Brand the mobile toast appearance to the Void/Signal-Red system") already owns this; link or close it rather than duplicating.
2. `components/gym-manager/stats-parts.tsx:68` has the app's ONLY hardcoded icon color. Related: jits-a8y.32 notes that a `className` on a lucide-react-native icon is a no-op, so check that the fix actually takes effect rather than looking right in source.
3. `app/(app)/(tabs)/gyms/_layout.tsx:20-22` uses legacy tokens while every other stack uses ELO ones. Coordinate with the legacy-token retirement issue so this is not fixed twice.
4. `lib/notifications/register-push.ts:40` duplicates the stale #ef4444 push accent that also sits in app.json. The JS half is OTA-fixable; the app.json half is in the native bundle issue. Fix both halves together or the value drifts again.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update) for items 1, 2, 3 and the JS half of 4. The app.json half of item 4 belongs to the native-asset bundle issue.

title: Native-asset bundle: splash, app icon, adaptive icon, push accent color, userInterfaceStyle
description:
THE ONLY NATIVE-REBUILD ISSUE IN THIS EPIC. Everything here changes the compiled app, so it is deliberately batched into ONE change rather than dribbled across releases, because each one costs a build and (if it goes further) an Apple round trip.

WHAT IS IN THE BUNDLE:
- The native splash: `app.json:96-102`, background #0D0F14 plus splash-icon.png.
- The app icon: `app.json:7`, and the Android adaptive icon at `app.json:44-47`. Note the existing icon issue jits-ais (E-R lettermark) and the icon-concept pipeline described in the `icon-batch-rerun-pipeline` memory; do not start a parallel icon process.
- The push accent color: `app.json:120-124` is currently a STALE #ef4444 that does not match the brand CTA #E63946. `lib/notifications/register-push.ts:40` DUPLICATES the same stale value; fix both or they will drift again.

DELIVERY: NEEDS A NATIVE REBUILD. This cannot ship over the air, and an OTA carrying these changes would silently ship WITHOUT them. Per the delivery gate, no `eas build` and no TestFlight submission happens without the user's explicit go. Verify locally first with `npx expo run:ios --device`.

WHAT DONE MEANS: an oversize file produces a specific, accurate message naming the size limit, and the check is consistent with the actual prod bucket limit rather than a drifting client-side constant.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).

title: Onboard non-technical partner to edit web via Claude Code web + PR-only access (per-PR Vercel previews as his environment)
description:
GOAL: let the non-technical business partner make copy, layout, and new-page changes to a deployed web environment and see them himself, without being able to reach production data or ship production code.

WHY A CMS IS NOT THE ANSWER HERE (recorded so this is not relitigated): apps/web is an authenticated product app with no marketing site, no landing page, no CMS, and no i18n or strings module. Every route sits under (app) or (auth). Roughly 95 percent of the words on screen are inline in TSX, about 360 quoted human-readable strings across 206 non-design TSX files. The only content-shaped data structures are HELP_SECTIONS at apps/web/app/(app)/settings/help/page.tsx:9-39 and NAV_TABS at apps/web/components/layout/nav-config.ts:14-19. So copy edits, layout changes, and new pages are all necessarily code changes.

Additionally, apps/web/next.config.ts:5 sets cacheComponents: true, which makes CMS visual editing a multi-day per-route refactor rather than a drop-in. Sanity is the only vendor that documents a cacheComponents pattern (page splits into an orchestrating component, a dynamic component resolving params/cookies, and a cached component carrying 'use cache'); Sanity's own performance documentation states that per-section query isolation does not work on Next.js App Router. Storyblok has three unresolved reports of broken visual editing on the exact Vercel plus Next App Router plus RSC configuration used here (storyblok/monoblok issues 37 and 76, plus a Vercel community thread from 2026-01-16). Neither vendor documents visual editing against auth-gated routes, which is every route in this app.

CHOSEN APPROACH: the partner uses Claude Code on the web, scoped so it can only open pull requests. Each PR gets its own Vercel preview URL automatically, and that per-PR URL is his environment. He iterates by commenting; he never waits on a developer to SEE a change, only to SHIP one. Per-PR previews are preferable to a shared long-lived staging branch because his in-progress experiments do not stack on top of each other.

BLOCKED BY: jits-jsh (second Supabase project, so his previews do not write to live TestFlight data) and jits-syu (branch protection, so he cannot merge to main or development). Do not grant access before both are closed.

WORK:
1. Add him as a GitHub collaborator with the narrowest role that still allows opening PRs. Confirm branch protection prevents him from merging his own PR to main or development.
2. Confirm he has a Claude account with Claude Code web access, and connect it to the repo.
3. Verify Vercel Deployment Protection settings. If protection is on, he needs either a Vercel seat or shareable links to open his own preview URLs. If it is off and the repo is public, every preview is publicly reachable. Pick deliberately.
4. Enable Vercel Comments on preview deployments so he can click an element and say "this heading," rather than describing it in prose. Pointing removes most of the ambiguity that makes AI-generated diffs go wrong.
5. Write a one-page onboarding doc for him covering: what a PR is, what the preview URL is, how to iterate, and what he must not do. Assume no prior git knowledge.
6. Run one end-to-end rehearsal with a trivial copy change before handing it over.

OPEN QUESTIONS: whether the repo stays public (his PRs and preview URLs would be public artifacts); whether the four CI jobs are fast enough that his iteration loop is not painful.

title: Web feature flags: read the feature_flags table instead of the hardcoded 9-line object (web has no runtime toggle today)
description:
Two unconnected feature-flag systems exist; the web one cannot be toggled without a deploy.

WEB: apps/web/lib/feature-flags.ts is 9 lines total and hardcodes a single flag object, const FLAGS = { timekeeperEnabled: true }, with one consumer at apps/web/app/(app)/session/[id]/match/[matchId]/match-flow-content.tsx:42. Changing it requires a code change and a deploy.

BACKEND: the feature_flags table (jr_be/supabase/migrations/20260405000500_feature_flags.sql) is runtime-togglable and currently holds two rows, timekeeper_role (default true) and video_position_taxonomy (default false). It is readable by any authenticated user and written through the audited admin_set_feature_flag(p_key, p_enabled) RPC (20260608000000_admin_platform_roles.sql:315). packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:1648 already exposes listFeatureFlags.

MOBILE: has an admin UI at apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/admin/flags.tsx that reads and writes the table.

THE PROBLEM: the web app never reads the table, and its local flag duplicates timekeeper_role by name while ignoring the database value. So the two can silently disagree, and nothing on web is togglable at runtime.

WORK:
1. Have the web app read flags via the existing listFeatureFlags query, server-side, with the hardcoded object as a fallback only.
2. Reconcile the naming so timekeeperEnabled and timekeeper_role are unambiguously the same flag.
3. Decide whether web needs its own admin UI or whether the mobile admin screen is sufficient for now.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: runtime flags are the cheapest way to let a non-developer turn a section of the site on or off without touching code, and they are the natural kill switch for anything a collaborator ships.

title: Render waivers.body instead of the hardcoded TOS_TEXT/WAIVER_TEXT constants (table is already queried, only for its id)
description:
Highest-value, lowest-effort step toward letting a non-developer change site content without a deploy. The infrastructure already exists and is roughly 90 percent wired; only the read is missing.

CURRENT STATE: legal copy lives in four places and they do not agree.
1. packages/shared/src/utils/tos-content.ts:10 defines TOS_TEXT, five numbered clauses, rendered on web via apps/web/components/auth/eua-form.tsx:87. The constant self-describes as a placeholder that "will be replaced with legally reviewed copy before launch."
2. apps/web/app/(app)/session/[id]/join/steps/waiver-step.tsx:8-16 defines a SEPARATE WAIVER_TEXT constant, rendered in the session join wizard.
3. The waivers table (jr_be/supabase/migrations/20260405000200_waivers.sql:10-21) has slug, title, body, version, scope, and is_active columns.
4. Repo-root TERMS.md and PRIVACY_POLICY.md are app-store artifacts and are never rendered by either app.

THE GAP: the waivers table is already queried on both surfaces, but only for its id. apps/web/app/(app)/session/[id]/join/join-content.tsx:37-44 and apps/web/components/auth/eua-form.tsx:143-149 both select the active waiver row purely to record an acknowledgement foreign key, then render the hardcoded constant instead of the row's body.

WORK:
1. Extend the existing queries to select body (and title) alongside id.
2. Render the fetched body in eua-form.tsx and waiver-step.tsx, keeping the hardcoded constants only as a fallback if the fetch returns nothing.
3. Seed the waivers table with the current TOS_TEXT and WAIVER_TEXT content so behaviour is unchanged at cutover.
4. Mirror the same change on mobile so the two platforms cannot drift.
5. Confirm the version column is incremented when body changes, and that acknowledgement rows still point at the correct waiver version.

PAYOFF: terms and waiver text become editable by a non-developer (or a lawyer) through Supabase Studio, with no code change and no deploy. This is the single largest content surface that can be moved out of code cheaply, and it is genuinely urgent given the placeholder text is what is currently shipping.

title: BE: widen technique_tags manual-INSERT policy to non-participant viewers on PUBLISHED videos
description:
technique_tags already supports source='manual' INSERTs by athletes, but the current policy presumably restricts to match participants. Community tagging means an unrelated active athlete tags a technique they spot in a PUBLISHED video.

SPEC (decided): widen, scoped to published videos only.
- INSERT policy: caller is an active athlete AND (is a participant OR the target video is published; reuse the can_view_match_video()/published predicate helper from jits-kaf.3.1). source must be 'manual' for this path; tagger identity column (whatever exists, e.g. created_by/athlete_id) must be the caller (WITH CHECK).

- DELETE: own manual tags only. AI-sourced tags untouched.
- Verify the analysis-merge pipeline is unaffected (it writes AI tags via service role / DEFINER, not this policy).

pgTAP for the matrix. Repo: jr_be; small migration. After: npm run db:types in jits_web.

title: Mobile confirm step can strand a user on 'waiting for opponent to confirm' if the opponent's result_confirmed broadcast is missed
description:
FOUND during live simulator walkthrough. In the session flow record_match_result completes the match (+applies ELO) BEFORE the confirm step mounts. use-match-completion.ts advances only on (a) a fresh postgres_changes UPDATE to completed/disputed (already happened at record time -> missed), or (b) a matchStatus PROP that is stale 'pending'/'in_progress' from the wizard's initial fetch (match-flow-wizard fetches once, doesn't refetch until confirm onCompleted). So the user relies solely on the opponent's realtime result_confirmed broadcast (confirm-step.tsx onResultConfirmed). If that broadcast is missed (opponent confirmed before this client subscribed, reconnect, or - here - the NPC exited), the user is stuck on 'WAITING FOR OPPONENT TO CONFIRM...' forever even though the match is fully completed in the DB.

Works in the common case (two live humans both present exchange broadcasts). NOTE: naive fix (advance whenever match is completed on mount) is WRONG - it would auto-skip the confirm/dispute window for everyone since the match is always completed by record time. Recommended: on confirm-step mount, reconcile opponent confirmation from match_confirmations (RLS permitting) and/or once THIS athlete has confirmed, advance independently of the opponent (the match is already finalized; opponent acks on their own device; summary already handles a later disputed status). Needs design decision on confirm semantics before implementing.

title: Video clip can be silently dropped if End fires before recorder reaches recording
description: apps/mobile/lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:143 stop() early-returns unless state==='recording'; if End/onMatchEnded runs while start() is mid-flight, stop() no-ops, stoppingRef stays false, and when recordAsync resolves the code goes idle and never uploads. Reachable on very short matches. Fix: track a pending-stop intent so a stop requested before 'recording' triggers stopRecording()+upload once recording starts.
acceptance_criteria: Ending a match immediately after start still stops and uploads the clip (or cleanly cancels); no orphaned/dropped recording on short matches.
close_reason: Verified and hardened on physical hardware (2026-06-10 live device session). The feared hardware behaviors were real and BOTH observed live: recordAsync rejects 'Camera is not ready yet' even after onCameraReady, and stopRecording can be silently ignored. Fixed: camera-ready deferral + 3s backstop + 500ms retry loop on start, stop re-issued until the record promise settles, OS-finalized clips uploaded. End-to-end recording verified on iPhone (match ed8041f6, video f4d9a7d9: record -> upload -> slice). jits_web 79006e7.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: FIXED in the Phase 1 pass (left open for review); it shares the exact code path (apps/mobile/lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts). Two-part fix: (1) recorder state is mirrored into a stateRef read at call time, so a stale stop closure (broadcast handlers capture the callback once) can no longer no-op against old React state; (2) a stop() arriving while the recorder is still 'idle' sets pendingStopRef, and start() honors it immediately after initiating recordAsync: it flips to stopping, calls cam.stopRecording(), and the resolved recording is uploaded (or transitions cleanly to idle when no URI). Acceptance covered by tests: 'honors a stop requested before recording starts' (clip uploaded, videoId set) and 'cleanly goes idle when a pending stop yields no clip URI' in apps/mobile/__tests__/lib/video/use-video-recorder.test.ts.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: Pending-stop hardening (review follow-up): a stopRecording() issued synchronously right after recordAsync() can be silently ignored on real hardware if native capture has not begun, leaving the hook stuck in 'stopping'. The pending stop is now deferred and re-issued on a 250ms interval (up to 8 attempts, ~2s window) until the recordAsync promise settles (issuePendingStop in apps/mobile/lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts). Covered by unit tests including a stubborn-camera case that ignores the first stop. CAVEAT: verified only against the JS contract with a fake camera; the exact native timing window still needs verification on physical iOS/Android hardware before this sub-issue is closed.

title: Profile-setup City field is required but labeled optional (silent disabled CTA)
description:
In the profile-setup 'Where You Train' (Training) step, City is REQUIRED for activation but its hint reads like an optional nicety, and nothing tells the user why Save is disabled.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed):
- apps/mobile/lib/profile-setup/validation.ts isTrainingComplete (line 62-70) returns false unless city is non-empty (line 69) -> CtaButton disabled (training-step.tsx:38, 108).
- apps/mobile/components/profile-setup/training-step.tsx:96 the City EloField helper is 'Helps you find local sessions and gyms.' with no 'Required' cue. Contrast the Home Gym field (line 86) whose helper says 'Required to activate your profile...'.

PROPOSED FIX (lowest-risk, do NOT change validation — City IS intentionally required per the wizard design, see beads memory 'mobile-signup-flow-state'): update the City field helper/label to clearly indicate it's required, matching the Home Gym field's pattern. E.g. helper 'Required. Helps you find local sessions and gyms.' or add a 'Required' affordance consistent with how Home Gym communicates it. Optionally surface a hint when the CTA is disabled (out of scope; relabel is enough).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- The City field visibly communicates it is required (parity with Home Gym field copy/treatment).
- No validation change: city remains required; Save stays disabled until city is chosen.
- Wording follows global style (no em-dashes).

RISK: low (copy-only).
SCOPE: mobile only (training-step.tsx). Web signup parity: confirm apps/web/app/(auth)/signup city field copy and mirror if it has the same ambiguity (the mobile validation mirrors web).

title: Gym card 'N in lobby' is actually gym member count, not lobby occupancy
description:
On the gym list card, the live subtitle reads '{city} · N in lobby' but N is the gym's active-member count, NOT current session-lobby occupancy. Observed: a gym showed '29 in lobby' while its live session had 2 participants.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): apps/mobile/components/gyms/gym-card.tsx:33-36 renders `${gym.memberCount} in lobby`. gym.memberCount comes from getGymsWithSessions (packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:464-468, 477-482, 509): it counts athletes where status='active' AND primary_gym_id = gym (i.e. members who claim this gym as home gym). It has nothing to do with who is checked into the live session.

PROPOSED FIX (lowest-risk): relabel. Change the subtitle to '{city} · N members' (or drop the count when live and rely on the LivePill). memberCount is an accurate member count, just mislabeled. If true lobby occupancy is desired instead, getGymsWithSessions would need to also count session_participants for active sessions (status IN ('checked_in','available','in_match')) per gym and expose e.g. lobbyCount on GymListItem — larger change; recommend the relabel now and file occupancy as a separate enhancement if product wants it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- The live subtitle no longer says 'in lobby' for a number that is the member count.
- Either it reads 'N members' (accurate) or the count is removed in favor of the LivePill.
- Brand: numeric stays font-mono tabular-nums, muted-foreground; no decorative color.

RISK: low (label-only if we relabel; med only if we choose to compute real occupancy).
SCOPE: mobile (gym-card.tsx) for relabel. If web shows the same string, mirror it for parity (web gyms-content/gym-card). Confirm web copy during impl.
close_reason: Implemented + independently reviewed + quality gate green (typecheck, jits_web tests 389, web build, jr_be 038 test all pass).

title: Gym list 'LIVE' vs detail 'No Sessions' inconsistency (dead-end)
description:
Gym LIST and gym DETAIL use DIFFERENT filters for what counts as a live/joinable session, so a gym can show 'LIVE' on the list but 'No Sessions Scheduled' in detail — a dead end.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed), both in packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:
- getGymsWithSessions (line 452): flags hasActiveSession purely on sessions.status='active' (lines 472, 490-491, 512). It does NOT check scheduled_end. Drives gym-card.tsx LivePill (gym.hasActiveSession, gym-card.tsx:28).
- getGymDetail (line 526): fetches sessions with status IN ('scheduled','active') AND .gt('scheduled_end', now) (lines 546-548). So an 'active' session whose scheduled_end is already in the past is EXCLUDED from detail, yielding sessionListItems=[] -> mobile renders 'No Sessions Scheduled' (gym-detail-parts.tsx:120). Web (gym-detail-content.tsx) consumes the same query so it has the same dead-end.

PROPOSED FIX: adopt ONE rule in both queries: a session is live/joinable iff status='active' AND scheduled_end > now(). In getGymsWithSessions, when building activeMap (lines 489-491) also require s.scheduled_end > now (add scheduled_end to the select at line 471). This makes hasActiveSession agree with detail. (Alternative considered: relax detail to include past-end active sessions — rejected; a session past its end shouldn't be presented as joinable. Keeping the stricter rule and applying it to the list is the consistent, correct choice.)

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- A gym shows 'LIVE' on the list IFF its detail shows at least one joinable (status=active, scheduled_end>now) session. No gym can be LIVE on the list and empty in detail.
- An 'active' session with scheduled_end in the past is treated as not-live by BOTH queries.
- Existing unit tests for these queries updated/added to cover the past-scheduled_end case.

RISK: low (pure query-filter change in shared, no schema change).
SCOPE: shared (packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts) — both web and mobile inherit the fix automatically (web parity is automatic).
close_reason: Implemented + independently reviewed + quality gate green (typecheck, jits_web tests 389, web build, jr_be 038 test all pass).

title: Backend: get_athletes_elo_delta batch RPC for real leaderboard deltas (jr_be)
description: PROBLEM: The leaderboard cannot show a real recent ELO delta per row. elo_history (table) + get_elo_history(p_athlete_id) RPC exist, but get_elo_history is own-profile-only / per-athlete (RLS-scoped), so the frontend cannot read other athletes' deltas for a 50-row board. No batch/public/windowed ELO RPC and no leaderboard view exist (verified in packages/shared/src/types/database.ts; research/005:579 lists get_leaderboard as planned-not-built). CHANGE (in jr_be — the copy in this workspace is stale): add a batch SECURITY DEFINER RPC get_athletes_elo_delta(p_athlete_ids uuid[], p_window_days int default 30) RETURNS TABLE(athlete_id uuid, elo_delta int) = COALESCE(SUM(delta),0) FROM elo_history WHERE athlete_id = ANY(p_athlete_ids) AND created_at >= now() - (p_window_days * interval '1 day') GROUP BY athlete_id. No new table/column. Then npm run db:types + add getAthletesEloDelta() wrapper in packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts. Until then the leaderboard shows delta={0} (neutral em-dash), never fabricated. From research/013 + leaderboard recon.
acceptance_criteria: RPC returns one signed 30-day elo_delta per athlete in a single round-trip ; SECURITY DEFINER bypasses elo_history RLS while gating active/inactive ; db:types regenerated ; getAthletesEloDelta typed wrapper added in @jits/shared ; no fabricated delta anywhere

title: Fire the already-defined match haptics on result-record and errors
description:
PROBLEM: matchHaptics.resultRecorded and matchHaptics.error are defined in the haptic vocabulary but never called anywhere (only matchStart/matchEnd/timeWarning are wired). Recording a result and confirming are the most decisive commitments in the flow yet give no tactile confirmation, and no error haptic ever fires. expo-haptics is already in the binary.

EVIDENCE: apps/mobile/lib/match-flow/use-haptics.ts:22-24

CHANGE: Fire matchHaptics.resultRecorded() on the success path after recordMatchResult returns ok (in the result/confirm submit handlers) and matchHaptics.error() on the failure path / error toast. Keep it MINIMAL per the design system: decisive commitments only, do not add a haptic to every tap.

PROBLEM: Many touchables and images lack accessibilityLabel/Hint/State: the notification bell badge announces a static 'Notifications' with no count; athlete/profile photos have no accessible name; gym rows lack a navigation hint; result-entry chips, live/lobby icon controls, and theme segments lack labels; and the notifications ToggleRow double-binds onToggle on both a role='switch' Pressable AND a nested real <Switch>, announcing a switch inside a switch to VoiceOver.

title: UI/UX polish (safe, client-only, app-wide)
description:
Safe, client-only UI/UX polish backlog (app-wide, mobile + web). Full analysis: research/013-ux-polish-backlog.md.

title: Add iOS provisional push authorization (build-gated, defer to next EAS build)
description:
PROBLEM: Even with a primer, some users decline. iOS provisional authorization ([.alert,.badge,.provisional]) delivers quiet notifications to Notification Center with ZERO prompt, letting the user upgrade themselves, ideal for the TestFlight phase to preserve the full prompt for later. The critique corrected the panel: provisional is NOT a quick win, the entitlement/behavior is baked at build time.

EVIDENCE: register-push.ts:44-48 (current binary authorization, no provisional); critique: provisional requires passing UNAuthorizationOptions.provisional through expo-notifications and is build-time on iOS; research: provisional is the recommended pre-launch path (https://onesignal.com/blog/how-to-create-more-compelling-opt-in-messages-for-ios-push/)

PROPOSED CHANGE: In the NEXT EAS build (after the primer ships), verify expo-notifications supports the provisional flag, request provisional UNAuthorizationOptions for quiet delivery, and make the status check accept provisional OR authorized. This layers on top of the primer (the primer becomes the upgrade-to-prominent path). Flagged build-required, not this week.

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/lib/notifications/register-push.ts, apps/mobile/app.json (notifications config)

Group: BiggerBet | Effort M | Impact Medium. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #16).
acceptance_criteria: expo-notifications provisional support is verified before relying on it ; Quiet notifications deliver to Notification Center with no prompt on a fresh device ; The permission status check treats provisional as a valid delivery state ; Shipped in a deliberate new EAS build, not bundled with the client-only primer

title: Fix the web FTUE: add the missing email/password login form, reconcile free-agent signup, default dark theme
description:
PROBLEM: If launch includes web, the panel almost entirely ignored it and there are P0-class defects. /login has NO email/password sign-in field at all, returning members cannot sign in from the primary entry route. Web /signup BLOCKS free agents (requires a gym) while /eua ALLOWS them, two activation entry points that disagree. And the web root layout defaults to LIGHT theme against the dark-first 'Void' brand, a wrong-theme first paint.

EVIDENCE: login-form.tsx:46-72 (only Register/Google/Apple/Forgot, no password sign-in); sign-up-form.tsx:89,259 + signup-form-validation.ts:82-84 (gym required, free_agent:false) vs eua-form.tsx:284 (Free agent option); app/layout.tsx:50 (defaultTheme='light')

PROPOSED CHANGE: Web-only. (1) Add an email/password sign-in form to /login (the (auth) group already has the supporting routes). (2) Reconcile the free-agent inconsistency: allow free agents on /signup to match /eua, or pick one canonical entry, do not ship two contradicting gates. (3) Set the root layout default theme to dark to match the brand. These touch routes/layouts/auth, so per CLAUDE.md run build:web + Playwright e2e before shipping. Confirm with product whether web is in the launch scope first.

AFFECTED: apps/web/components/auth/login-form.tsx, apps/web/components/sign-up-form.tsx, apps/web/lib/profile-setup/signup-form-validation.ts, apps/web/components/auth/eua-form.tsx, apps/web/app/layout.tsx

Group: Medium | Effort M | Impact Medium. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #15).
acceptance_criteria: A returning user can sign in with email/password from /login on web ; Free-agent activation is consistent between /signup and /eua (no path blocks what the other allows) ; Web first paint uses the dark 'Void' theme by default ; build:web passes and Playwright e2e is green
notes: DEFERRED (native-first, 2026-06-02): web FTUE rolled out after native reaches product. Revisit (missing /login email-password form, free-agent reconcile, dark default) when web is in scope.

title: Add a merged 'How rating works' explainer in plain BJJ language (anchored to ELO inline copy)
description:
PROBLEM: The core value (a meaningful rating) is expressed in chess/programmer jargon: 'ELO 1000', 'ranked vs casual', 'Pressure Score', 'weight_division_gap +50 phantom ELO', with no BJJ-native anchor. The competitor persona understands belt/stripe/weight class/open mat instantly but not these terms. If the rating does not map to what they feel in the gym, the number is noise and they will not trust or chase it, and trust in the rating IS the product.

EVIDENCE: CLAUDE.md business rules (weight-aware +50/division, draws cost both via Pressure Score, casual does not change rating); competitor persona jargon list; research: goal-matched, value-mapped explanation reduces the 'this number is noise' bounce (https://www.airbridge.io/en/blog/social-proof-for-apps)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Client-only content. MERGE with the inline ELO anchor (the 0%/ELO-anchor quick win): keep the one-line anchor inline on the EloTile, and put the fuller explanation behind a single dismissible info affordance off the tile, ONE static screen, not a multi-screen tutorial. Copy in gym language: 'Everyone starts at 1000. Win ranked matches to climb. Beat someone heavier or higher-rated and you gain more. Casual rolls don't change your rating; ranked matches do. Draws cost both athletes a little.' CONTENT-CORRECTNESS RISK: pull the exact rules from the BE FRONTEND_INTEGRATION_GUIDE / research/005, do not paraphrase from memory, wrong rules destroy trust. Brand: amber for draws, green only for gains, no red on numbers. Do NOT auto-assign a belt from ELO.

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/components/ui/elo-system/elo-tile.tsx, apps/mobile/components/ (new how-rating-works modal)

Group: Medium | Effort S | Impact Low. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #14).
acceptance_criteria: An info affordance on the Home ELO tile opens a single dismissible 'How rating works' screen ; The copy accurately states: 1000 start, ranked-vs-casual, heavier/higher-rated wins earn more, draws cost both (verified against BE docs, not memory) ; No belt rank is implied to map to ELO ; Draws shown amber, gains green, no numeric value in red ; It is one screen, not a multi-step tour

title: Add a one-time static pre-login value screen + a Skip on the splash
description:
PROBLEM: The ~2.3s brand splash ('WE ARE / ELO RATED / ARE YOU?') is mood, not meaning, and hands straight to a hard login wall. A logged-out user reaches a form not knowing this is BJJ matchmaking + ELO. This is the cheap 80% of explore-before-signup; the full read-only guest browse was DROPPED (see risks) because it needs anon RLS and breaks the authenticated-athlete presence model.

EVIDENCE: index.tsx:17 (hard redirect of unauthenticated users to /login); splash-statement.tsx (~2.3s mood splash); research: showing value/comprehension before the auth wall, but framing screens have skip-through behavior so this buys comprehension not conviction (https://uxcam.com/blog/10-apps-with-great-user-onboarding/)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Client-only, no RLS, no presence impact, no new build. Insert one (or two) static cards between splash and login: tagline ('See where you rank in BJJ. Get matched. Track your ELO.') + a couple of REAL screenshots (that do not look like a ghost town) + a Signal-Red 'Get started' to signup and a secondary 'Sign in' to login. Show it ONCE (persist a seen flag) and add a Skip affordance on the splash so the pre-auth delay does not compound. No animation beyond brand limits. Do NOT fabricate a placeholder ELO/rank (the Growth#4 'see where you'd rank' variant was rejected, a fake number that later changes destroys trust in the rating).

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/app/index.tsx, apps/mobile/components/splash/splash-statement.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(auth)/ (new value screen)

Group: QuickWin | Effort S | Impact Low. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #9).
acceptance_criteria: A first-time logged-out user sees one value screen explaining ELO RATED before the auth screen ; The value screen is shown at most once (persisted seen flag) and is skippable ; The splash can be skipped so total pre-auth delay does not increase for returning users ; No fabricated rating/rank is shown; no anon data fetch occurs

title: Unify the three progress counters into one continuous, entry-path-aware label
description:
PROBLEM: The user crosses three disconnected counters: login shows none, signup says 'Step 1 of 2 / Account', then the wizard restarts at 'Step 1 of 3'. The real journey is ~4 steps; each counter implies near-completion then resets, undermining the goal-gradient pull progress meters are meant to create.

EVIDENCE: signup.tsx:96 ('Step 1 of 2 / Account'); wizard-progress.tsx:21 ('Step 1 of 3'); login has no counter; research: progress bars lift multi-step conversion (https://foundrycro.com/blog/form-conversion-rate-benchmarks-2026/)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Adopt one continuous static counter across signup->activation: signup '1 of 4', TOS '2 of 4', Identity '3 of 4', Training '4 of 4, almost there'. Keep it a static mono label / segmented bar (no animated fill) per the motion rule. CRITICAL per critique: the SSO path skips the password-entry portion of signup, so make the counter conditional on entry path (an SSO user effectively starts at the wizard), or it will lie to SSO users. The two surfaces are separate route groups ((auth)/signup vs profile-setup), so the offset must be passed/recomputed across the navigation boundary.

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/app/(auth)/signup.tsx, apps/mobile/components/profile-setup/wizard-progress.tsx, apps/mobile/components/profile-setup/setup-wizard.tsx

Group: QuickWin | Effort S | Impact Low. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #8).
acceptance_criteria: A continuous 'Step N of 4' label appears across signup and the wizard with no reset to 'Step 1' mid-journey ; The counter is correct for the email path (starts at 1) and the SSO path (does not claim a skipped step) ; The indicator is static (no animation) per the minimal-motion rule

title: Enable Sign in with Apple: Supabase provider + Apple Developer capability + build
description: Mobile Apple sign-in CODE is being added this round, but it cannot be exercised until: (1) Apple provider enabled in Supabase dashboard (jr_be config.toml currently [auth.external.apple] enabled=false) with Service ID/client_id (bundle com.elorated.mobile) + secret; (2) 'Sign in with Apple' capability enabled on the App ID in Apple Developer console; (3) a fresh EAS/TestFlight build (native module, won't run in current build/Expo Go). App Store guideline 4.8 makes Apple sign-in mandatory since Google is offered.
acceptance_criteria: Apple provider live in Supabase; capability enabled; new build can complete an Apple sign-in end to end.
notes:
Apple sign-in was built then REMOVED before shipping TestFlight build 8 (removed in commit d687272; full working impl preserved in 844b16d). The expo-apple-authentication package injects the com.apple.developer.applesignin entitlement at EAS prebuild, so a production build FAILS unless the App ID actually has the Sign in with Apple capability. To re-enable: (1) npm install expo-apple-authentication; (2) restore signInWithApple in lib/auth/auth-context.tsx + the Apple button/availability effect in app/(auth)/login.tsx & signup.tsx from 844b16d (+ the APPLE_SIGN_IN_ENABLED flag if you still want the gate); (3) re-add 'expo-apple-authentication' to app.json plugins and ios.usesAppleSignIn=true; (4) enable the 'Sign in with Apple' capability on App ID com.elorated.mobile + regenerate the provisioning profile (EAS can auto-register interactively); (5) enable+configure the Supabase Apple provider; (6) verify nonce settings.
FTUE program (jits-r75): Apple Sign In is rec #13 of research/012. Adversarially verified it is NOT built on mobile (no expo-apple-authentication, no Apple button/signInWithIdToken). It is an App Store guideline 4.8 compliance BLOCKER and MUST land before Google-on-signup is exposed in the PUBLIC build (see jits-r75).
Correction: the Google-on-signup issue is jits-r75.5 (Apple must precede its PUBLIC exposure for guideline 4.8).

title: Splash variant flag: switch between Climb & Statement (default + future user toggle)
description:
Cheap flag so both splash variants are preserved and switchable; The Climb (live on TestFlight) is parked, never deleted. NO backend flag — splash is pre-auth/cold-start, so the toggle is LOCAL (mirrors the elo-cache pattern).

title: Improve Gyms tab load performance + loading UX
description:
The Gyms tab feels slow/unresponsive on first open (observed live on iOS sim). Root causes found in code review:

1. getGymsWithSessions() (packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:452) runs THREE sequential, independent network round-trips (gyms -> athletes -> sessions). They have no data dependency and should be Promise.all'd. Biggest win: ~3x -> ~1x latency.
2. The Gyms screen hook useGymsList() (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/gyms/index.tsx:48) fires a 4th query for gym coords (id, latitude, longitude) that duplicates the gyms table read already done in getGymsWithSessions step 1. Fold latitude/longitude into that first select to drop a round-trip.
3. No caching / no stale-while-revalidate. Every first mount pays full latency and shows a bare centered ActivityIndicator. Consider a lightweight shared cache so re-navigation is instant, and show cached data immediately while refreshing in background.

Loading UX improvements to make broadly (not just Gyms):
- Replace bare centered spinners with skeleton placeholders (perceived performance).
- Stale-while-revalidate pattern for list screens so navigating back to a tab is instant.
- Audit other tabs (Rankings/leaderboard, Home, Profile) for the same sequential-query and no-cache patterns.
notes: Surfaced during live iOS-sim debug session 2026-05-29. Measure before/after with timing instrumentation. Web app may share getGymsWithSessions so verify both consumers.
close_reason: Done on feat/loading-states (merged to development @ f1d535d): shared Skeleton primitive + SWR cache hook + skeletons & caching on all 4 tabs + parallelized getActiveSession/profile queries. Remaining micro-opt (fold gym coords into the main fetch) deferred: the coords query already runs in parallel so it is not a latency bottleneck.

title: Confirm Result step doesn't auto-advance when opponent confirms via API/DB

title: Share the match-uploads directory name between the plugin and recording-file
description:
Cheap strict improvement, deliberately deferred during the review of 21a452e.

plugins/with-android-backup-rules.js hardcodes the directory name as a string
baked into the generated XML; recording-file.ts has RETAINED_DIR_NAME. The
duplication is currently defended by a test asserting the two constants are
equal.

## The test IS sufficient today

Worth recording so nobody "fixes" this under the impression it is unsafe.
The assertion compares two imports from two modules, not a literal restated,
so a rename of either constant alone fails it. The three XML-shape tests do
hardcode "match-uploads" in their regexes, which means a correct, coordinated
rename fails loudly and forces the author to look -- the right failure
direction.

## Why it cannot just read the constant today

recording-file.ts is TypeScript and imports expo-file-system. Expo's prebuild
require()s the config plugin at config time, before any TS transform, which
is why the plugin is .js with a hand-written .d.ts.

## Fix

Hoist the string into a plain .js constants file that the plugin can require
and recording-file.ts can import. That deletes the duplication rather than
testing it, and the equality test can go with it.

## Also fold in while there

modules/backup-exclusion/index.ts's summary comment says "a single local
metadata write, once per recording". It is two per recording, directory and
file. The per-call docblocks are accurate; only the summary rounds down.
Cosmetic, no behavioural consequence.

title: A supersede during getSession() wastes a full 600 MB transfer
description:
Correctness is fully handled by the isCurrent() guards added in 1587740. This
is pure waste, not a defect.

upload-recording.ts awaits supabase.auth.getSession() BEFORE it calls
onAbortHandle?.(...). So from the moment uploadBytes invokes
uploadFileResumable until that promise resolves, handle.abort === null and
claimRunner's previous.abort?.() is a no-op. On this codebase getSession()
goes through the expo-secure-store adapter and refreshes a near-expiry token
over the network, so the window is routinely multi-millisecond and sometimes
a full round trip.

A supersede landing in that window leaves the loser uploading the ENTIRE clip
-- up to 600 MB of cellular data -- before discardSupersededObject deletes the
result. The guards make this correct; it is still a waste worth closing.

This window is also the real reachability story behind the P0-1 race: it
upgrades that bug from "needs an unlucky abort" to "needs a supersede during
a token read", which is why the first probe written against it passed
vacuously (a mock registering onAbortHandle synchronously never reproduces
the window).

## Fix

Either wire onAbortHandle before the getSession() await, or add one
isCurrent() check immediately after it so the loser gives up before sending
a byte.

title: Two concurrent sweeps double-abandon the same expired upload job
description:
Reproduced by the verification pass (probe G against 1587740):
  expect(mockRemoveUploadedObject.mock.calls.length).toBe(1)
  Expected: 1 / Received: 2

video-upload-manager.ts:679-682. The `await abandonJob(...)` inside the sweep
loop is itself a yield point. Sweep A enters it; sweep B -- which already has
its job list -- passes runners.has() (false, expired jobs have no runner) and
isJobExpired() (still true, A has not removed the record yet), and calls
abandonJob too.

## Impact: Sentry noise, NOT data loss

removeUploadJob and releaseRecording are both idempotent and the object is
already gone. But the second removeUploadedObject gets a 200 with {data: []},
which upload-recording.ts:94 reports as "removed 0 objects (silent RLS
denial?)" to console.warn AND Sentry. So it fires a spurious alert that
specifically claims an RLS denial which did not happen -- actively misleading
to whoever investigates. It also double-fires the "Match-video upload
abandoned" event.

## Fix

Same shape as the bug fixed one line above in 1587740, one level out: claim
the job synchronously before the await. Either a Set<matchId> of in-flight
abandons, or extend the runners.has claim to cover the expiry branch too.
~3 lines.

## Why this was filed rather than folded into 1587740

Impact is a misleading alert, not lost data, and folding it in would have
needed another implement-review round on already-verified code. The reviewer
leaned toward folding it in while the code was hot; that was overruled on
proportionality. The probe is described above precisely enough to rebuild.

title: Upload banner drops truncation on the error branch, so a truncated clip whose upload failed is never told it was cut short
description: N4 from the b5b7d8c review. Pre-existing from 37e52ec. UploadProgressBanner renders truncation only on its 'uploaded' branch; the error branch renders {message} alone. deriveUploadBannerState does carry truncation through on the error kind (lib/video/upload-banner-state.ts), so the data is there and the component simply ignores it. Consequence: a clip the OS cap cut short (or an interruption) whose upload then FAILED tells the user about the upload failure and never that the recording was also short. Both facts matter, and jits-2zpe is explicit that a truncated clip must not pass silently. Fix is a couple of lines in the error branch, appending the same truncationCopy() the uploaded branch uses. Worth a test in upload-status-visibility.test.tsx seeding {status:'error', truncation:'limit'} and asserting both sentences render.

title: Arena nits from re-review: navigation-state re-render, zombie channel tail, and the tab walk's first-match assumption
description: Three non-blocking observations from the Arena adversarial re-review, recorded so they are not rediscovered. (1) use-arena-tab-focus.ts calls useRootNavigationState(), which is a subscription, so the Arena screen re-renders on ANY navigation state change anywhere in the app. Correctness is unaffected: the roster effect keys on tick, presence on athleteId, and live on isArenaTabSelected. Performance nit only. (2) The tab walk returns the FIRST tab node found depth-first, including from a non-focused branch, and an out-of-range index returns null from inside the tab branch so the parent loop continues into siblings. Both are latent rather than live, because exactly one tab navigator exists today. Add a comment, and revisit if a second tab navigator is ever introduced. (3) In use-lobby-presence.ts ensure(), the athlete-change rebuild path retains a narrow zombie tail: if BOTH releaseChannel() and the stray sweep fail to confirm, supabase.channel(LOBBY_TOPIC) hands back the still-registered instance, on() would not throw (its state is leaving, not joined) but subscribe() would no-op, reproducing the dead channel. Requires a sign-out and sign-in PLUS two consecutive 10s unsubscribe timeouts. If on() did throw it would surface as an unhandled rejection from void ensure(), not a render crash. Worth a comment rather than a fix.
acceptance_criteria: A comment in use-arena-tab-focus.ts records the first-tab-node assumption and what to change if a second tab navigator is added. A comment in use-lobby-presence.ts records the double-failure zombie tail and why it is judged acceptable. The re-render observation is either measured and dismissed, or narrowed with a selector. None of these should change behaviour.
notes: All three were explicitly graded NOT ship-blocking by the reviewer that approved jits-hlm1 for merge (merged as 64b6f60). Filed for the record, not as a regression.

title: Cite the jr_be duration_seconds CHECK constraint that makes the recording cap ceiling unreachable
description: From the 3b8e97f review (S3). recording-limits.ts clamps computeMaxRecordingSeconds at RECORDING_CAP_MAX_SECONDS (7200), and exports MAX_FULLY_COVERED_MATCH_SECONDS (6586) as the point past which a full-length recording would truncate. What actually makes that unreachable is the backend CHECK on matches.duration_seconds <= 3600 (jr_be supabase/migrations/20260204034401_create_matches_tables.sql:38), and neither the module nor the test says so. The test asserts the ceiling is clear of a HAND-WRITTEN array of realistic durations instead, which would silently weaken if the backend constraint were ever raised. Add the citation to the module comment, and consider asserting against 3600 as the documented backend maximum rather than against the array.

title: MatchStepRenderer re-renders all eight steps on every recorder transition
description: From the 3b8e97f review (S2). MatchStepRenderer calls useMatchRecorder() and useMatchUpload() unconditionally at the top, so every recorder state change and every upload store write re-renders the renderer and therefore whichever step is mounted. It is correct (local state survives a re-render, only a remount would lose it) and the tree is small, but it is avoidable: only the live step needs the recorder and only the summary step needs the upload entry. Options: move each read into the step that uses it (costs the steps their presentational purity), or memoize the steps that take no recorder input. Not urgent; noted so it is a deliberate choice rather than an oversight.

title: accessibilityLiveRegion is Android-only: iOS announces nothing on the upload status chip
description: From the 3b8e97f review (F8). UploadProgressBanner sets accessibilityLiveRegion='polite' on every variant, which React Native implements on Android only. On iOS the chip changes from uploading to uploaded or to a failure with no announcement at all, so a VoiceOver user gets nothing from a surface whose entire purpose is telling the user what happened to their upload. Cross-platform route is AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility, fired from an effect when the derived banner kind changes (see lib/video/upload-banner-state.ts, which already gives a single value to key on). Keep the live region for Android; add the announce for iOS. Worth checking whether anything else in the app already sets a live region and has the same gap.

title: Truncation classification uses Date.now(), so it is not monotonic and its tolerance is one-sided
description: From the 3b8e97f review (F7). use-video-recorder classifies an unexpected recordAsync settle as 'limit' vs 'interrupted' by comparing a Date.now() delta against maxDuration, with a 2s CAP_DETECTION_TOLERANCE_MS applied on ONE side only (elapsed >= cap*1000 - tolerance). Two consequences: (1) Date.now() is wall-clock, not monotonic, so an NTP correction or a manual clock change during a match skews the delta; (2) the one-sided tolerance means the error can only ever produce a FALSE 'limit', never a false 'interrupted'. Harmless to the user, because both labels render the same warning chip and the clip is uploaded either way, but it makes the label untrustworthy for field diagnostics, which is the only reason it exists. Fix: measure with a monotonic source (performance.now(), available in Hermes) and make the tolerance two-sided, or drop the distinction and report one honest 'the recording ended before the match did'.

title: Arena mobile: force-quit while live leaves looking_for_ranked set
description:
Found in review of the Arena mobile branch (A12).

apps/mobile/lib/arena/use-arena-live.ts clears the flag on tab change, on background and on teardown. A force-quit runs none of those: iOS delivers no reliable signal, so the flag survives.

Harm is bounded. Presence lapses on its own, so the athlete drops out of Online now and lands in Open to challenges, which is a section for people who are not here; a ranked challenge to them is valid and waits in their notification bell. And it self-heals: the next Arena visit re-asserts the flag if they go live, and clears it when they leave.

The durable fix is server-side, not client-side: a sweep that clears looking_for_ranked for athletes with no recent presence, or the short Arena-challenge TTL from the cap issue. Worth deciding alongside that one.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded: either accepted as bounded, or a backend sweep clears stale looking_for_ranked.
notes: REVIEW ADDENDUM 2026-09-19 (Arena re-review, finding 5.1): this issue now also covers a SECOND path to the same end state, and the reviewer recommends closing both with the one durable fix already named here rather than opening a separate issue. In lib/arena/use-arena-live.ts, step()'s offline branch sets actualRef.current = false BEFORE awaiting writeLookingFlag(id, false), and does not roll it back when that write fails. The reconcile loop then exits because desired === actual, while the DB flag is still true. Both non-UI callers invoke it as void requestOfflineRef.current() and discard the false return, so there is no retry beyond the two inside writeLookingFlag. VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by the desired-state rewrite: the original goOffline had the identical shape (setLive(false); await leaveLobby(); return writeLookingFlag(id, false)). End state is identical to force-quit: flag set, presence absent, athlete shows in 'Open to challenges' with no Challenge affordance, self-heals on the next Arena visit. The sweep this issue already proposes (clear looking_for_ranked for athletes with no recent presence) closes both causes at once, which is why it belongs here.

title: Arena mobile: challenger recovery is bounded to one screen session
description:
Found in review of the Arena mobile branch (A9).

apps/mobile/lib/arena/use-arena-challenge.ts recovers a challenger whose match_started broadcast went missing by watching the challenge row's status change. That listener only exists while the Arena screen is mounted and while `outgoing` is set in memory. A challenger who backgrounds, force-quits, or loses the row from memory never recovers into the match, even though the match exists and they are a participant.

The general fix is an on-load check: when the Arena mounts, look for a challenge of mine in status accepted or started whose match is not finished, and offer to rejoin it. That is also what would make the notification bell's challenge_accepted item actionable, which it currently is not.
acceptance_criteria: A challenger who leaves the app between accept and navigation is offered a way back into the match that was created for them.

title: Token drift guard nit: NOT_DECLARED sentinel is comparable as an ordinary value
description: tokens-mirror-drift.test.ts records a missing token as the string '(not declared)'. It flows through the same comparison and ledger path as a real colour, so a mirror that literally declared the text '(not declared)' would compare equal, and a ledger entry cannot distinguish 'absent' from 'present but weird'. Low impact, but the sentinel should be a distinct type rather than an in-band string.

title: Token drift guard F7: regression test for non-brace at-rules
description: Originally reported as: a non-brace at-rule such as @import before a theme block swallows it and produces bogus leak diagnostics. The recursive parser rewrite in jits-xmwn appears to have fixed this incidentally, because a segment is now terminated at ';' so '@import url(...);' no longer consumes the following block. Verified by hand against the brand file. This issue is to LOCK that behaviour with a dedicated test, and to check the sibling cases (@charset, @namespace, @layer without a block).

title: Unhandled getManagedGyms rejection pins the gym-manager portal on a permanent spinner
description:
DEFERRED FROM THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF THE NAVIGATION SURGERY DIFF. Unhandled rejection that pins the gym-manager portal on a spinner.

WHY THIS EXISTS. apps/mobile/lib/gym-manager/use-managed-gyms.ts:35-40 awaits getManagedGyms with NO catch. If that await rejects, isReady is never set true, and every screen in the gym-manager portal sits on a spinner indefinitely with no error, no retry and no way out except backing out of the portal entirely.

The window is narrow but real. getManagedGyms returns [] on a Supabase error, so a query failure does not reject. Only a THROWN error reaches this code, which in practice means a network-layer failure (offline, DNS, TLS, an unexpected client throw). That is exactly the condition a phone hits regularly.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW. Before the nav surgery the portal was a TAB: an athlete who hit the hang could tap another tab and effectively retry later. After the nav surgery the portal is entered by an explicit "Manage Gym" tap from a gym detail screen. The athlete has performed a deliberate action and gets a permanent spinner in response, which reads as the feature being broken rather than as a transient network blip.

WHAT DONE MEANS. The await is wrapped so a thrown error is caught, isReady still resolves, and the portal renders an error state with a retry instead of a spinner that never ends. The distinction between "no managed gyms" (empty result, a legitimate state) and "could not load managed gyms" (an error) is preserved, since collapsing them would tell a manager they manage no gyms when the truth is the request failed.
acceptance_criteria: The getManagedGyms await in apps/mobile/lib/gym-manager/use-managed-gyms.ts is wrapped in error handling, and a thrown error still resolves isReady. With the network forced to throw, entering the portal via "Manage Gym" shows an error state with a retry within one load cycle, never an indefinite spinner. The empty-result state ("you manage no gyms") and the error state render differently and are not collapsed into one. Retry actually re-issues the request and recovers once the network returns. A test simulates a thrown getManagedGyms and asserts isReady becomes true with the error surfaced. Typecheck and the full mobile and shared test suites stay green.
notes: Deferred from the independent review of the navigation surgery diff. Narrow window (getManagedGyms returns [] on a Supabase error, so only a thrown network error reaches it) but no escape once hit, and more visible now that the portal is entered by an explicit Manage Gym tap rather than a tab.

title: Four nav-surgery nits: double empty state, string[] route param, silent gym substitution, un-normalised /(app)/gyms route
description:
DEFERRED FROM THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF THE NAVIGATION SURGERY DIFF. Four small defects grouped into one issue because each is a few lines and they all sit in the same nav-surgery surface. None is urgent; all are real.

NIT 1, DOUBLE EMPTY STATE. A member whose gym has nothing scheduled sees two empty states stacked. apps/mobile/components/dashboard/session-discovery-section.tsx:108-119 renders UpcomingSessionsSection, which draws its own "No Sessions Scheduled" box, AND then renders a second "Nothing scheduled" line underneath it. Pick one. The fix is to suppress the outer line when the inner section is already showing its own empty state, or to stop the inner section drawing one in this context.

NIT 2, WRONG PARAM TYPE. apps/mobile/lib/gym-manager/use-gym-manager-gym-id.ts:32 declares useLocalSearchParams<{ gymId?: string }>. expo-router can yield string[] for a route param, so the declared type is a lie the compiler cannot catch. It is currently SAFE only by accident: the value is consumed in a === comparison, which just returns false for an array instead of crashing. Any future consumer that calls a string method on it breaks. Declare the param as string | string[] | undefined and normalise at the boundary.

NIT 3, SILENT GYM SUBSTITUTION. When a gymId is supplied that the athlete does not manage, the code falls back to gyms[0] with NO user-visible signal. The athlete asked for one gym and is shown a different one, silently, with the portal looking entirely normal. Either surface the substitution, or refuse and show a not-authorised state, but do not swap gyms behind the athlete's back.

NIT 4, UN-NORMALISED ROUTE SPELLING. apps/mobile/components/dashboard/active-session-card.tsx:40 still uses router.push("/(app)/gyms") while three sibling files were normalised to "/gyms" in the same diff. One inconsistent spelling in a group of four defeats the point of normalising and makes future route scans miss this site.

WHAT DONE MEANS. All four are addressed. They may be fixed in one change since they are small and adjacent.
acceptance_criteria: NIT 1: a member whose gym has nothing scheduled sees exactly ONE empty state, verified against apps/mobile/components/dashboard/session-discovery-section.tsx, with a test covering the empty case. NIT 2: apps/mobile/lib/gym-manager/use-gym-manager-gym-id.ts declares the route param as string | string[] | undefined (or the expo-router equivalent) and normalises it to a single string before use, so correctness no longer depends on the consumer happening to be a === comparison. NIT 3: an unmanaged gymId no longer results in a silent swap to gyms[0]; the athlete sees either an explicit signal that a different gym is being shown, or a not-authorised state. NIT 4: apps/mobile/components/dashboard/active-session-card.tsx:40 uses "/gyms", and a repository scan finds no remaining "/(app)/gyms" spelling in the dashboard components. Typecheck and the full mobile and shared test suites stay green.
notes: Deferred from the independent review of the navigation surgery diff. Grouped into one issue because each is a few lines in the same surface; they can be fixed in a single change.

title: Record the known false negative in the exit-navigation regression guard (do not fix unless observed)
description:
DEFERRED FROM THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF jits-3929. TEST HYGIENE, filed to RECORD A KNOWN LIMIT, not to request a fix.

RECOMMENDATION UP FRONT: do NOT fix this unless it actually happens in real code. The escape is evasion-shaped, not accident-shaped, and tightening the guard to catch it would cost more in false positives and scanner complexity than the residual risk is worth.

WHY THIS EXISTS. The exit-navigation regression guard added alongside the MatchFlowWizard decoupling scans for reintroduced hardcoded session-lobby navigation two ways: a scan for route literals, and a scan for the `sessionId` identifier. The review confirmed exactly one residual false negative. A URL escapes both scans when it is BOTH assembled from a prefix constant that stops before the trailing slash AND built from an identifier not named sessionId, for example:

  const LOBBY_PREFIX = "/session";
  return `${LOBBY_PREFIX}/${originId}/lobby`;

The route-literal scan misses it because no scanned literal appears in the source (the prefix is cut before the slash and the rest is interpolated). The sessionId identifier scan misses it because the variable is called originId.

Both conditions have to hold at once. A developer who accidentally reintroduces lobby navigation writes the obvious form and gets caught; only someone deliberately routing around the guard writes this one.

WHAT DONE MEANS. The limit is written down where the next person reading the guard will see it, which this issue satisfies on its own. If the escape is ever observed in a real diff, reopen the question then and decide whether a stronger check (for example, a scan over assembled route strings rather than source literals) is justified.
acceptance_criteria: The known false negative is recorded as a comment on the exit-navigation regression guard itself, naming both conditions that must hold at once (a prefix constant cut before the trailing slash, plus a non-sessionId identifier) and stating that the guard deliberately does not catch it. No scanner change is required and none should be made on the strength of this issue alone. This issue may be closed as documented-and-accepted once that comment exists. If a real diff is ever found containing this pattern, a new issue is filed to revisit the guard.
notes: Deferred from the independent review of jits-3929. Filed only so the limit is recorded. The review judged the escape evasion-shaped rather than accident-shaped and deliberately did not chase it; the recommendation is NOT to fix unless it shows up in a real diff.

title: Runtime warning: Supabase auth token > 2048 bytes in SecureStore (chunked adapter)
description:
Persistent yellow warning: 'Value being stored in SecureStore is larger than 2048 bytes ...'. The Supabase auth session payload (access+refresh token + user metadata) exceeds expo-secure-store's 2048-byte soft warning limit.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): apps/mobile/lib/supabase/secure-storage.ts SecureStoreAdapter.setItem (line 29-35) writes the whole serialized session to a single SecureStore key via SecureStore.setItemAsync; expo-secure-store warns above ~2048 bytes. The adapter's own doc-comment (lines 14-21) anticipates this and names the LargeSecureStore pattern as the fix.

PROPOSED FIX: implement a CHUNKED SecureStore adapter — split the value into <2048-byte chunks across keys (e.g. ${key}.0, ${key}.1, ... plus a ${key}.meta count), reassemble on getItem, and delete all chunks on removeItem. Keep the web localStorage branch unchanged. CRITICAL: do NOT regress the cold-start auth-lock fix (CHANGELOG/git 322039e + beads memory 'mobile-supabase-auth-lock-coldstart'): the adapter must remain a drop-in async storage; processLock and the synchronous onAuthStateChange callback in auth-context.tsx must be untouched; getItem must reliably return the full reassembled value (a partial/empty read at cold start could wedge the Loading gate). Add migration handling: if an old single-key value exists, read it, re-chunk on next write (or read-through then delete). Alternative (encrypt-to-AsyncStorage LargeSecureStore) is heavier and adds AsyncStorage dependency — prefer pure chunked SecureStore.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- No 'larger than 2048 bytes' warning after sign-in/refresh on mobile.
- Session persists across cold start (sign in, force-quit, reopen -> still authenticated, no Loading hang).
- Token rotation (autoRefreshToken) updates all chunks; sign-out clears all chunks (no orphans).
- No regression to the cold-start auth lock fix; processLock + sync onAuthStateChange unchanged.
- Existing/added unit test for the adapter round-trips a >2KB value across chunks.

RISK: med (auth persistence + cold-start path is the previously-fragile area). Requires a new EAS build to verify on device (native-adjacent).
SCOPE: mobile only (apps/mobile/lib/supabase/secure-storage.ts). No web parity (web uses localStorage).
close_reason: Implemented + independently reviewed + quality gate green (typecheck, jits_web tests 389, web build, jr_be 038 test all pass).

title: Runtime warning: Realtime send() falling back to REST (use httpSend or join before send)
description:
Persistent yellow warning toast: 'Realtime send() is automatically falling back to REST API. ... Please use httpSend() explicitly for REST delivery.'

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed in @supabase/realtime-js 2.105.4, RealtimeChannel.js:487-492): channel.send({type:'broadcast',...}) warns + REST-falls-back whenever the channel can't push over the websocket (!canPush()) — i.e. the broadcast fires before the channel has finished JOIN, or on a channel not configured for WS broadcast. Our broadcast senders that hit this:
- packages/shared/src/hooks/use-session-match-sync.ts:60 (channelRef.current?.send({type:'broadcast',event,payload})) — used by the ready step (broadcastReady) and timer/result events; readiness broadcasts commonly fire right at mount before join completes.
- packages/shared/src/hooks/use-match-sync.ts:55,63,71
- packages/shared/src/hooks/use-lobby-sync.ts:80,88,96
- apps/mobile/components/session/wizard/confirm-step.tsx:86 (await channel.send(...))

PROPOSED FIX (supabase-js-correct): for these fire-and-forget broadcasts, call channel.httpSend(event, payload) explicitly (the API the warning recommends; present in 2.105.4, RealtimeChannel.d.ts:355) instead of send({type:'broadcast'}). This is the intended REST path and silences the warning. Alternatively/additionally, gate sends on the channel being SUBSCRIBED (track subscribe status and queue/drop until 'SUBSCRIBED') so WS push is used when available. Prefer httpSend for the one-shot lobby/ready/result events; keep send for events guaranteed to fire post-join. Apply consistently across the shared hooks so web and mobile both stop warning.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- No 'send() falling back to REST' warning during lobby join, ready-check, and result broadcast on mobile.
- Broadcast events still deliver (opponent still sees ready/challenge/match/result events).
- Change lives in shared hooks; web behavior unchanged functionally and also warning-free.

RISK: low/med (realtime delivery semantics; verify opponent still receives events).
SCOPE: shared (use-session-match-sync.ts, use-match-sync.ts, use-lobby-sync.ts) + apps/mobile/components/session/wizard/confirm-step.tsx. WEB PARITY automatic (shared hooks consumed by both).
close_reason: Implemented + independently reviewed + quality gate green (typecheck, jits_web tests 389, web build, jr_be 038 test all pass).

title: EUA/edit-profile re-prompt inconsistency for active athletes (seed-data artifact)
description:
Reported: an athlete with status='active' but missing gender/dob/city and no waiver_acknowledgements row was routed into the 3-step EDIT PROFILE wizard on explicit login, but on cold relaunch went straight to home.

INVESTIGATION (confirmed in code): On MOBILE there is NO such inconsistency. Both explicit login (apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx onSubmit/onGooglePress call router.replace('/')) and cold relaunch funnel through the SAME guard, apps/mobile/app/index.tsx, which routes to /profile-setup ONLY when !athlete || status===PENDING (index.tsx:18-21); an 'active' athlete always goes to /(app)/(home) in BOTH paths. No mobile login path routes an active-but-incomplete athlete into the EDIT PROFILE wizard. The EDIT PROFILE wizard (isEditing, use-setup-data.ts:117) is reachable only by explicitly navigating to /profile-setup (e.g. from settings). The reported login-into-wizard behavior is a WEB behavior (the /eua route exists only on web: apps/web/app/(auth)/eua/).

REACHABILITY: A real MOBILE user reaches status='active' only by completing the wizard (TOS/EUA -> identity gender+dob -> training weight+gym+city), so a real active user already has gender/dob/city + a waiver_acknowledgement. An active row missing those fields is a SEED-DATA artifact (jr_be seed sets status directly, bypassing handle_athlete_activation + the wizard).

RECOMMENDATION (lowest-risk): For the mobile scope of this sprint, CLOSE-AS-WONT-FIX / not-a-bug (no mobile code defect). If the web /eua + login routing shows the actual divergence, file a WEB-scoped issue to make web's login routing consistent with its cold-start guard. Separately, recommend fixing the jr_be seed so seeded 'active' athletes carry gender/date_of_birth/city + a waiver_acknowledgements row (so verification doesn't hit phantom states). Do not change mobile index.tsx — adding a fields-complete check there would force real-but-edge users (and every seed account) into the wizard and risks an activation loop given the athlete-column guard trigger.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Documented decision: mobile = no code change (not a bug). 
- (If pursued) jr_be seed produces complete active athletes, OR a separate web issue tracks web login/guard consistency.

RISK: low (decision/doc; optional seed fix in jr_be).
SCOPE: investigation/decision. Optional: jr_be seed; optional separate web issue. Mobile: no change.
close_reason: Not a mobile bug: seed-data artifact. Mobile login and cold-start both use the status-only guard in apps/mobile/app/index.tsx, so an 'active' athlete always routes home on both paths; the EUA re-prompt is web-only and a real mobile user reaches 'active' only by completing the wizard. Optional follow-ups (separate issues if desired): (a) jr_be seed completeness (gender/dob/city + waiver_acknowledgements), (b) web login/guard parity.
